title: ECOMM-410 Users cannot reactivate subscriptions after Stripe cancellation (credit card and invoice)
body:
## Pull request overview

This PR adjusts the two-screen purchase flow to better handle reactivating subscriptions that were canceled (via `cancelAtPeriodEnd`), aiming to treat those workspaces as “new subscription creation” rather than “paid-to-paid” updates.

Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/ECOMM-410 & https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/ECOMM-413

Test Env: https://sub-reactivation.mural.engineering/

**Changes:**
- Update `isPaidToPaid` derivation to treat `cancelAtPeriodEnd: true` subscriptions as effectively “no subscription”.
- Refactor checkout-session requirement logic and reorganize the purchase confirmation action branching.
- Adjust UI gating for payment details / purchase button visibility, with new/updated unit tests.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 8 out of 8 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.

title: [SCQM-1641] Send `usage` and `cost` in AI feature responses
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR adds `usage` and `cost` to `AIFunctionResult` and all makes all the function calls that resolve through an AI operation report their usage and cost back to the AI Chat along with their function call response message.

It can be followed commit by commit. The first one adds the new `AIFunctionExecutionResult` type and implements sending the new props when received. The rest of the commits add the new props to the features that need them, one feature per commit.

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1641) to understand the context of this effort.

Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes:
Run all of the following AI features and confirm that on their call to the `/ai/chat` endpoint, the payload includes `usage` and `cost` accordingly:
- [ ] Cluster by topic
- [ ] Generate ideas
- [ ] Generate mindmaps
- [ ] Summarize
- [ ] Suggest title
- [ ] Classify by sentiment
- [ ] Translate

**NOTE**: other features, like Spell check or Mermaid diagrams, don't incur external usage/cost because they are either handled by the chat itself or don't require external AI calls to resolve.

title: [NEXT-440] Phase 1 of moving sdk/apis/widgets/changes/systems
body:
Test env: https://sdk-apis-cont-3.mural.engineering


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Broad refactor across absorption/connector systems and helper exports; while largely import-path and module-boundary changes, it touches core widget-parenting/stacking logic and could cause subtle runtime regressions if any exports or paths are missed.
> 
> **Overview**

title: [FEP-6441] - fix tooltip hover in floating widget toolbar
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

[Test Environment](https://tooltip-hover-widget-toolbar.mural.engineering)

[JIRA Issue - FEP-6441](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/FEP-6441)

### Problem Statement

**Widget toolbar tooltips interfere with canvas interactions**

When users hover over tooltips in widget toolbars, canvas panning and zooming become unresponsive. 


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62afdbff-d537-4c5a-a0c4-e02766ffc749


This issue occurs because:
- Tooltips are rendered in a separate DOM layer from the canvas
- The tooltip layer captures mouse wheel events before they reach the canvas
- The canvas `WheelManager` cannot process these events, disabling pan/zoom functionality, when hovering over tooltips, See [@micaelbergeron comment](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/FEP-6441?focusedCommentId=368061) for more details

### Solution Approach

After evaluating multiple approaches, we implemented a targeted solution:

**Option 1:** Move tooltip rendering inside the canvas container
- Would ensure proper event delegation to `WheelManager`
- Risk: Significant changes to tooltip positioning logic and potential rendering bugs

**Option 2 (Implemented):** Disable tooltip hover behavior for widget toolbars
- Maintains existing tooltip positioning and rendering
- Minimal risk and focused scope

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/608d65c8-6b2c-424c-a83d-ccad8f26a6ce

### Implementation Details

This PR introduces the `disableTooltipHover` prop that prevents tooltips from capturing hover events, allowing mouse interactions to pass through to the canvas.

**Key Changes:**
1. **Core Toolbar Component** - Added `disableTooltipHover` prop to the main `Toolbar` component ([src/lib/tools-api/renderers/toolbar/index.tsx](src/lib/tools-api/renderers/toolbar/index.tsx))

2. **Targeted Application** - Enabled only for widget-specific toolbars:

title: [MFRD-93] Fallback to `img` tag for rending external photo links in Activity Log
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When you add a photo widget via an external link to the canvas, in the backend this is the order of events:
1. The widget gets created **with the external link as the thumbnail**
2. **The creation activity is added to the activity log** ****
3. A callback called `updatePhotoWidgetWithInternalAsset` runs to update the widget, replacing the external link with an internal asset path. 

This means that when you open the activity log, the widget data stored still has the **external** link to the image. When the `RenderWidget` component uses the engine to load and take a snapshot of it (a change made last October), the `toDataURL()` call to read from the canvas throws a security error because it's cross origin. The other places that use `RenderWidget` (outline / voting results) are not impacted since they use the current widget data (with the internal asset) and not a snapshot of the widget prior to that callback. 

TLDR: This change specifically looks for photo widgets with an external link and reverts to using an `img` tag to load them in the activity log. The solution to get it to render the way the rest of the widgets do with `RenderWidget` would likely include making changes to the create widget flow in the backend - since this is not a high priority feature I was hesitant to go tinkering with a critical path. 

Loom: https://www.loom.com/share/3ff5a470148949849f57dac7a498ae71

title: Added extended tracking for autoresize ussage
body:
## Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Added improved telemetry around table cell auto-resize usage:

- New table_autoresize_toggled event emitted from the widget toolbar toggle with precision if event was toggled on or off.
- New table_autoresize_resized event emitted when autoResize=true and fitting content actually changes table layout, with aggregated resize impact fields (counts + total deltas).

## Case Solved
We needed better observability to evaluate the risks/benefits of permanently disabling/removing auto-resize. Previously, we could only infer usage from the generic toolbar_button_pressed event (no “from/to” state), and we had no tracking for actual resize operations caused by autoResize=true.

## How the Change Fixes It

**Toggle telemetry:**

- When the user clicks the toolbar toggle, we capture the current table autoResize state and emit a dedicated event including both from and to, so we can distinguish on→off vs off→on.

**Resize telemetry:**

- In fitTableCellsToContent, after computing the resulting newColumns/newRows, we compare against the original dimensions.

- We only emit table_autoresize_resized when:
 -- autoResize is enabled,
 -- child widgets are considered (ignoreChildren=false),
 -- and at least one row/column dimension actually changes.
- Payload summarizes impact (how many rows/cols changed + total deltas) and whether any fitted cell had child widgets.

title: [FEP-6440] - fix packages unit tests performance
body:
# Improve packages unit tests performance

## Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

[https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/FEP-6440](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/FEP-6440)
[https://packages-unit-tests-performance.mural.engineering/](https://packages-unit-tests-performance.mural.engineering/)

**Prior to these changes:** Package unit tests in CI ran with `--runInBand` (single Jest worker per package), and individual test files used a mix of local timeouts. There was no shared CI-specific Jest configuration or visibility into slow tests and memory usage.

**With these changes:** Package tests run in parallel (no `--runInBand`), use a shared CI Jest config with configurable timeout and worker limits, report memory and test duration (slowest first), and rely on a single global timeout instead of per-test overrides. This improves CI runtime and reduces risk of OOM while making slow tests visible.

### Changes

- CI workflow
  - Removed `--runInBand` from the "Package tests" job in `.github/workflows/quality.yml` so packages can run with multiple Jest workers when `npm run test:packages -- --concurrency=4` runs.

- Shared Jest CI config (`packages/config/jest/`)
  - `jest.ci.config.js` (new): Central CI config used when `CI=true`. Sets:
    - `testTimeout`: 30s default (override via `JEST_TEST_TIMEOUT`)
    - `maxWorkers`: 50% of CPU (override via `JEST_MAX_WORKERS`, e.g. `75%` or `12`)
    - `workerIdleMemoryLimit: '75%'` to recycle memory-heavy workers
    - `workerThreads: true` for lower memory and faster worker startup
    - Custom reporter: `memory-and-time-reporter.js`, it will report the 5 slowest tests in a package.
  - `jest.react.config.js` and `jest.ts-library.config.js`: Spread `jestCiConfig` when `CI === 'true'`.

- Global timeout instead of per-test timeouts
  - Replaced local timeouts in 7 test files with the global `testTimeout` from the CI config so behavior is consistent and CI doesn’t hang on stuck tests:

title: [ESC-1874]-related Fix tracking dashboard events
body:
Jira: [ESC-1874](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/ESC-1874)-related Testing environment: https://esc-1874-dashboard-tracking.mural.engineering/ ### Summary Fix tracking dashboard events by adding an `identify()` call in `AuthenticatedUserConsumer`. Commit 0e0d7650787b5295e119b48d6ac016509766c9d9 introduced a regression where `identify()` is no longer called when loading the dashboard. Because the event tracker sends events for authenticated users only after `identify()` has been called[^1], it silently dropped dashboard events unless `identify()` was called in another area of the code. For example, if a user opened a mural from the dashboard, the mural view calls `identify()`, and dashboard events would be tracked once the user returns to the dashboard. More specifically, loading the dashboard used to call `fetchUser()` to retrieve load the user data; that calls `identify()`. After the dashboard changed to use `AuthenticatedUserConsumer` to load the user data, `identify()` is not called and dashboard events are not tracked. ### Testing To reproduce, show verbose logs in the browser console, sign in to Mural and wait for the dashboard to load. Reload the page. Before this change, events are not tracked after reloading the page. After this change, events are tracked after reloading the page. ### Example As an example, the `VIEWED_ITEM_IN_DASHBOARD` event count dropped by about 25% after the regression was deployed on Oct. 30, 2025:
Databricks query ```sql select action_date, count(*) from prod.cdp.fe_event where action_type_performed = 'VIEWED_ITEM_IN_DASHBOARD' and action_date > '2025-09-01' and action_date < '2026-02-01' group by 1 order by 1 ```
[^1]: https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/b51e7b0c39bb18f1fa08b316acefa13b4

title: Add deployment watcher for beta and stable
body:
## Summary

Adds a deployment watcher that polls the deployed app until the version comment in the HTML matches the pushed commit SHA.

### Changes
- **scripts/wait-for-deployment.js**: Node.js script that polls a URL, extracts `<!-- version: <hash> -->` from the HTML, and exits when it matches the expected commit
- **beta-deployment.yml**: Waits for beta.mural.co to serve the pushed commit; cancels in-progress runs when a new push lands
- **stable-deployment.yml**: Waits for app.mural.co to serve the pushed commit; cancels in-progress runs when a new push lands
- **Removed**: alpha-deployment.yml, master-deployment.yml

### Behavior
- Polls every 30s, up to 15 minutes (configurable via env)
- Concurrency: when a new push triggers a deployment, the previous run is canceled
- Clear success/failure messages with the environment URL

title: Refine/unify add image logic
body:
## Ticket 🎫 

https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CWI-2567

## What was changed and why? 🤔 

Demo Loom: https://www.loom.com/share/6aa0a2b3657d4fe6be603b15528096c6

It seems that Google has changed the html layout of their image search results, and when a user drags the images from the search results onto the canvas, they fail to upload onto the canvas.

This is because the urls for these images are now base64 encoded, and this was breaking uploads.

In order to handle this properly, we needed to make sure have the base64 asset go through the entire upload file flow, rather than adhoc, since we need to make sure users don't upload base64 data that is not supported by Mural.

## Testing 🤖 

- Test Env: https://unify-add-image-logic.mural.engineering/
- Added unit tests
- Tested manually (see Loom)


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Refactors core mural upload paths (files/URLs) and introduces new base64 parsing/conversion that impacts user-facing uploads; broad changes are covered by new unit tests but could still affect edge-case upload behavior and notifications.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refactors mural asset uploading to a new `createUploadAssetsApi` pipeline, replacing the large inline `uploadAssets` implementation with composable steps for `byFiles` and `byUrls` (notifications, blocked/too-many checks, metadata extraction/positioning, sequential uploading, and error handling).
> 
> Adds base64 data-URL support for URL uploads (e.g., Google image drag results) by introducing `@muralco/base-64` helpers `isBase64` and `base64ToFile`, and routing base64 links through the standard file-upload flow rather than ad-hoc URL handling.
> 
> Moves/updates call sites (`file-preview`, `persistThirdPartyImage`, `update-natural-dimensions`) to use the new upload-assets utilities and exports `ByUrlMetaData` from canvas dispatcher types.

title: Update `move-to-package` to handle converting internal package imports to relative paths.
body:
## Pull request overview

This PR enhances the `move-to-package` refactoring tool to handle internal package imports when moving files into a package. 

Example: when a file is moved into `@muralco/utils` and imports symbols from that same package (e.g., `import { X } from '@muralco/utils'`), those imports are now converted to relative imports pointing to the actual defining files (e.g., `import { X } from './path/to/x'`).

## Summary
- Adds support for converting package barrel imports to relative imports when moving files into a package
- When a file is moved into `@muralco/utils`, imports like `import { X } from '@muralco/utils'` are now converted to `import { X } from './path/to/x'` pointing at the actual defining file
- Introduces new `move-to-package-internal-imports.ts` module with symbol resolution logic that follows re-exports to find original definitions
- Handles edge cases: dist/.d.ts to src/.ts path normalization, multi-file symbol splitting, type-only imports

title: [CAN-8206] Fix arrow absorption when connecting to grouped widgets
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes a bug when trying to connect an arrow inside an area to a grouped widget inside the same area.

_This PR:_
![Feb-04-2026 16-21-56](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84d1efb4-6a3a-4104-a183-33a881fea163)

_Master:_
![Feb-04-2026 16-21-48](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a4db3b7-3844-4a58-b532-fb6f3c61c6c0)

### The issue
The problem was in the connector absorption system. This system runs an algorithm to find, according to some specific rules, the best suitable widget to parent the arrow after an action has taken place.

One of these rules state that an arrow should be absorbed by a parent P if it's connected on one side to a widget inside P.

Because of this rule, when moving the arrow near the grouped widget we were switching back and forth between connecting to a widget inside P (the group) and a widget _not_ inside P (the grouped widget whose true parent is the group, not P).

The fix consists in adding a consideration for grouped widgets: if a widget W is inside a group G, and the group G is inside parent P, we'll consider W to be inside P _only for this best suitable parent lookup_.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8206)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://arrow-absorption-with-groups.mural.engineering)

title: Improved text handling when merging cells. Now texts that are not  in the default cell are merged in the remaining cell too when the remaining cell has no text.
body:
## Summary of Changes
Preserved table‑cell text when merging by copying the first non‑empty cell’s textContent in reading order into the keep (top‑left) cell when the keep cell is empty. Added unit tests for copy behavior, keep‑cell preservation, and reading‑order selection, plus updated table‑cell text mocks in the merge‑cells tests.

## Case Solved
Merging cells ignored text in non top‑left cells when the top‑left cell was empty, so the merged cell ended up blank even though one of the merged cells had content.

## How the Change Fixes It
Before deleting merged cells, the merge flow now:

- Checks if the kept cell has text.
- If not, sorts the selected cells by row/column index (reading order) and picks the first non‑empty cell.
- Copies that cell’s full textContent (text + format) into the keep cell, then proceeds with the merge in the same transaction (so undo/redo includes it).

## Tests
- Tests validate the new behavior and ensure keep‑cell content isn’t overwritten when it already has text.
-

title: Fixed issue where merging row/column with interconnected widgets breaks the connection
body:
## Summary of Changes
Reworked table cell merge persistence and undo/redo to keep collaborator views consistent without changing realtime update behavior. Updates now persist in two phases (updates before deletes), and undo/redo replays the same ordering via a dedicated MergeCellsStep.

## Case Solved
Merging table cells with child widgets (including connectors) could leave collaborators with missing widgets or detached connections until a refresh or local movement. This could also affect the originator in certain undo/redo paths, not just synced users.

## How the Change Fixes It

### Fix undo ordering by splitting persistence into two commits inside the same transaction:

- **Persist updates before deletes** so remote clients receive reparent/span updates before the merged-away cell is removed (persistence applies deletes before updates within a commit).
- **Split commits:** update commit (span + reparent + system-derived changes), then delete commit.
- **Dedicated undo/redo step (MergeCellsStep)** replays the same order on redo and restores deleted cells with keepPartOfId on undo, preventing invalid table states after refresh.
- **Realtime remains authoritative:** no systems are run on remote UPDATE_WIDGET paths; the server patch is the source of truth.

### Tests
- Added a regression assertion for persistence call ordering (updates before deletes)
- Updated the undo persistence test harness to correctly accumulate diffs across multiple commits within a single transaction
- Added regression coverage for realtime table-cell `colSpan`/`rowSpan` updates using the systems path

## Reviewer Resources

title: CAN-8379 More reliable trackpad wheel event detection
body:
Prior to this changes, trackpad detection considered any dual axis event coming in the last second as an indicator. But this meant that Magic Mouse users had an erratic behavior, where they often get a few moments of wheel to zoom until any horizontal axis movement happens which moves to pan. 

Now, with these changes, we detect any dual axis event as a trackpad event, but added special heuristics to detect single axis events that are likely from a trackpad. In Mac, trackpad events are always integers in both Chrome and Safari, while mouse wheel events have decimal points. In Mac Firefox, mouse wheel events are also integers but always multiple of 16, so we have a special case to detect that.

This has been tested with Mac Chrome, Mac Safari and Mac Firefox with a Magic Mouse, a Macbook Trackpad and a Logitech wheel mouse. 

Further work is needed to add heuristics for high precision trackpads in windows Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

body:
**[CAN-8369 Unlocked sticky notes cannot be moved or edited](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8369)**

This PR fixes comparison for legacy `text` field. Now `undefined`, `null`, and `""` are considered as the same empty value.
Previously because of different `text` the dited sticky was considered as modified. At the same time backend do not send any updates expected by other side.

title: Code package analysis
body:
Migrating the **code package analysis** tool from local usage into the **murally** monorepo so it can be run via `npx muralco-refactoring-tools`.

## What the utility does

The **code-packages** command analyzes how code is distributed between `src/` and `packages/` in the monorepo. It:

- **Counts lines of code** in TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, and SASS/SCSS under `src/` and under each package in `packages/`.
- **Excludes** build artifacts (`dist`, `build`, `.turbo`), dependencies (`node_modules`), tests (`.test.*`, `.spec.*`, `test/`, `__tests__`), and generated files (`.d.ts`, `.min.js`).
- **Prints a modularization report** to stdout with totals for `src/` vs `packages/`, per-package line/file counts, and a summary of the top packages by size.

Usage: `npx muralco-refactoring-tools code-packages [--root=/path/to/monorepo]`. When run from within the murally repo without `--root`, it uses the repo root automatically.

title: Improve Cucumber Distributed Running Implementation
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Reorganizes and improves the Cucumber distributed test (AKA React Test Rig) runner infrastructure with a focus in improve clarity on discovering issues, and future improvements, and at the same time reducing duplicated config.

**Changes:**
- Reorganized cucumber-cluster directory structure with dedicated folders for common utilities, patch files, scripts, and reporters
- Consolidated GitHub Actions workflows by creating a reusable `cucumber-rig-runner.yml` that handles both producer and consumer roles. Removed deprecated `cluster-runners.yml` workflow and theme configuration
- Add notification and information of the dispatched consumer to allow traceability of errors for the remote workflow. For future reference, this could be improved once the next feature in API Workflow dispatch operation are released by GH:
	- https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/9752
	- https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/lets-talk-about-github-actions/ 
- Improve documentation around code and a proper `README.md`

#### Reviewer Resources
- No productive changes, so if it builds and executes the test, it works

- The process would work as usual, except from some minimum changes
	- Now it's clear the role of the "Producer" and the "Consumer" in the run itself.
	- If a run is successful ([like this one](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/actions/runs/21451789569/job/61782476376?pr=46934)) then:
		- [x] The _Dispatched Consumer_ jobs inform the consumer's runs related to this execution
	- If a run fails ([like this one](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/actions/runs/21451262311/job/61780820443?pr=46881)), then:
		- [x] The _Producer run_ also informs of how to access the consumer's run if needed for troubleshooting.

- Draft PR where this approach was tested in several scenarios: https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46881

- [Jira ticket](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HwVh8pmOot4)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Moderate risk due to widespread type/import rewiring across `canvas` register components and the Tools API; runtime behavior should be mostly unchanged, but incorrect exports/import paths could cause build-time or subtle UI regressions (e.g., toolbar badges/menus).
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves several *register* component/type definitions out of app-local files into `@muralco/canvas/register` (new exports for `navigation`, `sidebar`, `snipping-selection`, and `BottomBarPropTypes`), and updates consumers to import from the package instead of `src/mural/register/...`.
> 
> Promotes more of the Tools API surface into `@muralco/tools-api`: adds `core` type exports (e.g., `Tool`, `ToolNode`, `ToolSpec`, `MenuSpacing`) and a new exported `Badge` renderer, then updates internal adapters/builders/addons/tests to consume these package exports and replaces the previous shared `isNumber` badge helper with a local numeric check.
> 
> Adds `classnames` as a dependency of `@muralco/tools-api` and adjusts related imports/exports to support the moved badge renderer/styles.

title: [CAN-8344] Navigation-improvements clean up for hand-off
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer Before anything else, we were planning on doing this work on the next sprints, but due to the re-org changes, I have to handoff the navigation-improvements, so I went ahead and did the two biggest changes we had planned: 1) I migrated the navigation sidebar buttons to the tools API, so now the Select and Pan buttons are actually tools which make it easier to maintain and hopefully becomes to first step to migrating the whole sidebar. This can be found in the first commit ee4e8f1260453824c6bbd414ad3f49d8e762668b 2) A big refactor of the callouts we have been implementing this past 2 weeks in preparation for the navigation-improvements: For example: Prior to these changes, the callout system for canvas onboarding and navigation improvements had significant code duplication and complexity. Each flow type (onboarding vs rollout) required separate navigation logic, manual tracking in every callout, and inconsistent handler implementations. This made adding new flows or callouts error-prone and difficult to maintain. Now, with these changes, we have a unified flow architecture with a single registry, standardized handler factories, and automatic tracking. All callout flows share the same navigation functions, handlers are created with simple factory functions, and tracking happens automatically via SDK callbacks. This makes the system significantly simpler to understand, maintain, and extend. #### Reviewer Resources - Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**]() to understand the context of this effort. - 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**

title: [MFRD-38] Add facilitation dispatcher fn to hide / show bottom bar follow notification
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Currently: There's a bug where the bottom bar reactions menu gets hidden behind the follow notification. 

In the past there were unsuccessful attempts to move the reactions menu so both could be visible that caused other issues, this solution is to make sure they're not displayed at the same time. 

When following someone, if you activate the reactions menu from the bottom bar, the follow notification should temporarily hide and only display the reactions menu. When the reactions menu closes, the follow notification should return. 

https://www.loom.com/share/c30f84c9d5c34e218398e5e4c5a2d2bc

- 
1. Add multiple users to a mural 
2. Follow another user
3. Verify the follow notification shows up above the bottom bar
4. Mouse enter the reactions menu item in the bottom bar
5. Verify that the follow notification hides
6. Verify that the full reactions menu is visible (and that you can react)
7. Mouse exit the reactions menu item
8. Verify the follow notification returns 

Same behavior should be shared when a user is summoned / receives a request to be followed.

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR refactors and modularizes mural business rules by extracting common business logic from src/mural/business/ into the shared @muralco/canvas package (packages/canvas/src/business/). This enables better code reuse across the codebase and improves the architectural separation of concerns.

Changes:

- Extracts reusable business logic functions and types from src/mural to packages/canvas/src/business
- Updates all import statements across the codebase to reference the new centralized locations
- Adds fast-url-parser dependency to the canvas package for URL parsing utilities
- Creates proper TypeScript type definitions for the new fast-url-parser dependency
- Updates test files to import from the new module locations


#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/NEXT-413) to understand the context of this effort.

### Required Checklist for Author
- [x] Unit tests were added/updated
- [ ] No new cucumber tests were added 
- [ ] Exception: no unit tests were added or updated for this change




<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Broad refactor touching many call sites (delete/clipboard/connectors/tables/system-of-record/integrations) by changing imports and public exports; behavior should be unchanged but regressions could come from incorrect re-exports or subtle package boundary differences.
> 
> **Overview**

>

title: [CAN-8349] Fix widget dragging with grid areas
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes a bug related to dragging widgets out of a grid area.

With the introduction of the `reset` concept during dragging, the behavior of widgets within grid areas stopped working as expected.

The [following comment](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8349?focusedCommentId=363496) in the attached Jira card explains the current flow of the dragging logic and the reason behind the bug.

The TL;DR version of it is that every time we try to move a widget out of a grid area, the resetting puts it back in.

---

This fix is based on how the dragging currently works: we first move the widget to the new position, and then find the best cluster to absorb it (or to expel it from).
Because this is currently a two step process, the first step triggers the grid areas system which puts forces the sticky into a gridded position if needed.

The fix, therefore, consists in unifying both steps into one, so the grid areas system only runs after the second part has been calculated. This releases the widget from the grid area claw when the new position is out of its bounds.

In order to test this, you simply need to try to move a widget out of a grid area. If you can, success!

Please note that grid areas still work funky as hell, this is not fixing those weird behaviors, they will still occur until we can properly address how grid areas in general work.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8349)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://grid-area-dragging.mural.engineering)


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Unifies drag movement and absorption feedback into a single, atomic action pipeline to prevent grid areas from snapping widgets back while dragging out.
> 
> - Reworks `dragSelectedWidgets` to build a single `ActionList`: appends `beforeDragMove` + `sdk.dragging.move` + `dragWidgetsOverCluster.drag(...).appendTo(...)`, then applies once

body:

title: Migrates 3rd of "medium" priority dependencies from `src/mural` to `@muralco/canvas`
body:
This PR is the third of a series moving ready to modularize canvas dependencies into the canvas package. This PR handles the third batch of `medium` priority dependencies.

Dependency priority was determined by evaluating the number of times a specific file was being imported within the `src` directory. The breakdown of priority is as follows:

- **CRITICAL** (≥20 imports)
- **HIGH** (10-19 imports)
- **MEDIUM** (5-9 imports)
- **LOW** (1-4 imports)
- **NONE** (0 imports)

## Prerequisite Migrations

Several commits in this PR were prerequisite file migrations required to support `MuralState` and `RegisterState` types:

- **Right bar types** (`59feb86`) - `src/mural/register/components/right-bar/types.ts` → `@muralco/canvas/register/components/right-bar/types`
- **Contains widget helper** (`140c42e`) - `src/mural/helpers/contains-widget.ts` → `@muralco/canvas/helpers/contains-widget`
- **Outline items helper** (`7b4d414`) - `src/mural/helpers/outline-items.ts` → `@muralco/canvas/helpers/outline-items`
- **Outline types** (`f281ef1`) - `src/mural/register/components/outline/types.ts` → `@muralco/canvas/register/components/outline/types`

These migrations were necessary to establish the type dependencies required for `MuralState` and `RegisterState` to be properly defined within the canvas package.

## What Was Migrated

### Addons
- **AI create workshop types** (`addons/ai/ai-create-workshop/types.ts`) - AI workshop creation types and interfaces
- **Dev table** (`addons/dev/table/`) - Development table component and styles
- **Lexical serialization types** (`addons/core/editors/lexical/widget-editor/serialization/types.ts`) - Lexical editor serialization type definitions

### Business Logic
- **Content extension system of record** (`business/content-extension/shared/handlers/common/system-of-record.ts`) - System of record handler utilities for content extensions

### Components
- **Arrow utilities** (`components/widgets/arrow/util.ts`)

title: Breaks apart and migrates `src/mural/register` ui-component types
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, UI component types for the register system were centralized in `src/mural/register/types/ui-components.ts`, which contained types for bottom bar menus, sidebar buttons, and secondary top bar components. This monolithic file made it difficult to reuse types across packages and created tight coupling between the main codebase and the canvas package.

Now, with these changes, we've broken apart and migrated these types into more appropriate locations:
- **Bottom bar types** (`BottomBarButton`, `BottomBarMenuSpec`, `BottomBarMenuState`, etc.) moved to `packages/canvas/src/register/types/bottom-bar.ts` - making them available via `@muralco/canvas/register`
- **Tab types** (`TabProps`) moved to `packages/canvas/src/register/types/tabs.ts` - also available via `@muralco/canvas/register`
- **Sidebar types** (`SidebarButton`, `SecondaryTopBarSpec`) moved to `src/mural/register/types/sidebar.ts` - keeping them in the main codebase as they have dependencies on mural-specific state

This refactoring improves code organization, enables type reuse across packages, and reduces coupling between the main codebase and canvas package. All 58 affected files have been updated to use the new import paths.

title: Improved automated test coverage for undo operations on tables
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR adds automated undo/persistence coverage for the After Fix table scenarios and strengthens the shared test harness so undo commits are validated against persisted store diffs.

- Undo test helper now captures commit diffs and stubs engine/text/table-cell APIs to simulate realistic undo persistence flows.
- Added a shared layout consistency assertion to catch orphaned cells after undo.
- Added new unit tests for merge undo variants, cell color/child widget undo, internal border resize undo, and outer table resize undo.

### Case Covered

- Delete row/column + undo with child widgets and connected arrows; asserts persisted layout updates and layout consistency.
- Insert row/column + undo persists table layout updates.
- Merge (horizontal, vertical, 2x2) + undo, including interconnected widgets.
- Internal row/column resize + undo.
- Outer border resize (horizontal, vertical, both) + undo.
- Cell background change + undo and child widget add + undo.

### How the tests work

- Undo is now validated against the same store diff that commit() uses, so any missing persistence on rows/columns/cells is caught by tests.
- Layout integrity is asserted after undo to detect orphaned cells and missing grid coverage.

### Reviewer Resources
-  🏷️ [JIRA](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8341)

title: Migrates additional "high" and "critical" priority dependencies from `src/mural` to `@muralco/canvas`
body:
This PR continues the series of modularizing canvas dependencies into the canvas package, handling remaining `high` and `critical` priority dependencies that were missed in previous migration PRs.

Dependency priority was determined by evaluating the number of times a specific file was being imported within the `src` directory. The breakdown of priority is as follows:

- **CRITICAL** (≥20 imports)
- **HIGH** (10-19 imports)
- **MEDIUM** (5-9 imports)
- **LOW** (1-4 imports)
- **NONE** (0 imports)

## What Was Migrated

### Addons
- **Mindmaps types** (`addons/mindmaps/types.ts`) - Mindmap handler types, node connection types, and expand/collapse utilities

### Business Logic
- **Discovery call** (`business/discovery-call/`) - Discovery call types and business logic utilities
- **Kanban types** (`business/kanban/types.ts`) - Kanban board types and utilities (122 imports)

### Dispatcher
- **Rightbar types** (`dispatcher/rightbar/types.ts`) - Rightbar API types and interfaces (25 imports)

### Helpers
- **Shapes utilities** (`helpers/shapes/`) - Shape path utilities and shape-related helper functions

## Export Reorganization

This PR reorganizes several exports for better consistency:

**Business Module**:
- Changed from selective exports to wildcard export for `inclusive-selection`
- Added `discovery-call` export path

**Dispatcher Module**:
- Reorganized export order for better consistency
- Added `rightbar` export path

**Helpers Module**:
- Added `shapes` export path

**Addons Module**:
- Updated mindmaps types to use relative imports for internal dependencies

## Changes Summary

- **203 files changed**: 307 additions, 281 deletions
- **Updated imports**: All consuming files now import from `@muralco/canvas` instead of relative paths
- **Reorganized exports**: Improved consistency in barrel exports across business, dispatcher, and helpers modules

title: [CAN-8303] Implement `reset` on resize
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR implements the concept of `reset` when resizing widgets.

After this change, every resize step is considered as an atomic movement between the initial point and the current one.

The motivation behind this change is to have a more accurate reflection of what resizing an absorbing widget over one or more absorbable widgets represents in terms of layering.
This is a change that goes along the new stacking order system, therefore in order for it to make sense, the flag controlling the stacking order system needs to be enabled (without it this change is innocuous).

Without this change, resizing an area over two widgets would send to the front the widgets as they were getting absorbed, so the last one would end up on the front every time, even if it wasn't beforehand.
By resetting the changes on each movement, the stacking order between the two widgets is respected:

_Before resetting:_
![Jan-20-2026 15-31-47](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57ac1380-cd4a-4169-a3e6-d405f793520e)

_After resetting:_
![Jan-20-2026 15-37-36](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59a0dd24-4fa7-4814-85f5-bc06032eac1b)


#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8303)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://reset-on-resize.mural.engineering)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> Implements atomic resize steps and aligns APIs/types across canvas and app layers.

title: chore: update pluralize types and eslint config to disallow usage of non-existant globals
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Follow up to #46828 

This PR proposes a solution to a quirk with our usage of the `pluralize` npm package. The types for that package in the version we're currently using on `master` [expose a global `pluralize` definition for UMD purposes](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/pull/27064). Combined with our current `eslint` configuration, this allowed for committing references to `pluralize` without explicitly importing it in the referencing file, passing our current set of pre-commit and build checks, but causing a runtime type error in the bundled code. Changes:

- Updates the `@types/pluralize` package to trigger TS level warnings / typecheck failures when the package is not explicitly imported
- Update: adds a new custom/internal eslint rule to catch references to a global `pluralize` as errors so they will be flagged in an IDE and caught in precommit checks
- Drops some mocks in the rig V1 and V2 test config that didn't seem to be doing anything as there are no more references to a global `pluralize` instance anyway
- ~Removes an existing eslint rule override downgrading `no-restricted-global` violations as warnings~
- ~Adds an explicit and narrow eslint rule override ensuring references to a global `pluralize` will be flagged as errors so they will be flagged in an IDE and caught in precommit checks~


#### Reviewer Resources
This is a type level / linter fix. You can verify locally by finding a file that uses `pluralize` and commenting out the `import * as pluralize from pluralize` line, attempting to commit it (should see warnings and failed pre-commit checks)

title: [CAN-8302] Refactor `afterResizeEnd` hook to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors the `afterResizeEnd` hook to return a list of changes instead of letting handlers apply them directly.

The motivation behind this change is related to keep control of who originates widget changes and when.
On a resizing operation, the changes to the widgets model should be restricted only to the resizing operation core logic.

This is the last of the hooks related to resizing that needed amending.

In this particular case, we need to address two handlers related to Smart Planners that were applying changes within their logic.

In this PR there's also a change in the `CODEOWNERS` to move ownership of the widget composition addon from the Smart Canvas team onto the Workflows and Integrations team.

No change in the app or its behavior is expected whatsoever.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8302)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://after-resize-end.mural.engineering)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Modernizes the resize hook pipeline to collect and apply changes centrally.
> 
> - Refactors `ResizeWidgetsHookHandler.afterResizeEnd` to return `ActionList`; dispatcher now aggregates with `reduceHandlersFor` and applies before `commit`
> - Updates Kanban/compositor plugins to return actions instead of mutating state directly (e.g., column visual updates, clearing temporary widgets); replaces direct `apply/commit` with action builders

title: Upgrade sass and sass-loader
body:
[https://linear.app/mural/issue/FEP-70/investigate-sass-upgrade-to-a-version-higher-than-171](https://linear.app/mural/issue/FEP-70/investigate-sass-upgrade-to-a-version-higher-than-171)

[https://update-sass-version.mural.engineering/](https://update-sass-version.mural.engineering/)

FEP-70

# Upgrade SASS

This branch updates Sass and sass-loader to the latest supported versions, then adjusts syntax and tooling to match modern Dart Sass behavior. The upgrade is important to keep builds compatible with current tooling, reduce deprecation noise, and unblock future cleanup of legacy `@import` usage.

### Dependencies versions

- `sass` from `1.45.2` to `1.97.2`.
- `sass-loader` from `10.2.0` to `16.0.6`

### Changes

The following deprecation warnings were fixed:

1. Replace global functions with module-based equivalents.

Example:

```sass
background-color: transparentize($white, 0.2)

// replaced with

@use "sass:color"
background-color: color.adjust($white, $alpha: -0.2)
```

Color helpers (e.g., `transparentize`, `darken`, `lighten`, `mix`) now use `sass:color`, list/map/string utilities use `sass:list`, `sass:map`, and `sass:string`, and percentage/round helpers move to `sass:math`.

1. Replace `if()` that was deprecated in Dart Sass in favor of the `@if` directive.

1. Import path syntax no longer supported (sass/sass-loader upgrade).

The following import path forms are no longer supported and were updated:

- `~`-prefixed module paths (Webpack-only resolution).
  `@use "~@muraldevkit/ds-foundation/src/styles/_mixins"` -> `@use "@muraldevkit/ds-foundation/src/styles/_mixins"`

title: Migrates second batch of "medium" priority dependencies from `src/mural` to `@muralco/canvas`
body:
This PR is the second of a series moving ready to modularize canvas dependencies into the canvas package. This PR handles the second batch of `medium` priority dependencies.

Dependency priority was determined by evaluating the number of times a specific file was being imported within the `src` directory. The breakdown of priority is as follows:

- **CRITICAL** (≥20 imports)
- **HIGH** (10-19 imports)
- **MEDIUM** (5-9 imports)
- **LOW** (1-4 imports)
- **NONE** (0 imports)

Test env: https://migrate-medium-priority-deps-2.mural.engineering

### Business Logic
- **2-way sync types** (`business/2-way-sync/types.ts`) - Fields status, sync result, and sync function types for two-way synchronization
- **Add template to canvas types** (`business/add-template-to-canvas/types.ts`) - Widget ID mapping, tracking data, and success arguments for template operations
- **Inclusive selection** (`business/inclusive-selection.ts`) - Inclusive selection capability checking and state utilities
- **Integrations bulk sync** (`business/integrations/bulk-sync/`) - Bulk synchronization types and service status management
- **Kanban constants** (`business/kanban/consts.ts`) - Kanban board column limits (min/max)

- **Wheel handler** (`components/wheel-handler.tsx`) - Mouse wheel event handling component with zoom constants

### Dispatcher

title: [CAN-8299] Refactor `beforeResizeStep` to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors the hook `beforeResizeStep` to return a list of changes instead of letting handlers apply them directly.

Unlike other similar hooks, this one is expecting a result back from the handlers, so we can't just make the hook return a list of changes directly, but append this to the expected returned value.

Therefore, the hook now expects, instead of `Point | null`, an object with a potential list of changes to apply, and the previously expected point.

The only hook handler registered has been adapted to this new interface. Luckily it wasn't applying any changes so the refactor is rather trivial.

No change in the app is expected whatsoever.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8299)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://before-resize-step.mural.engineering)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Introduces a new return type for `widgets.resize.beforeResizeStep` to support both delta adjustments and batched model updates.
> 
> - Changes `beforeResizeStep` signature from `Point | null` to `{ changes: ActionList; newDiff: Point | null }` and updates the reducer in `sdk/hooks/widgets/resize/create.ts` to aggregate both
> - Applies returned `changes` in `resize-widgets/index.ts` during `drag` before main resize updates
> - Adapts Enhanced Kanban Board resize plugin to return the new object shape (currently returns `ActionList.empty`) and updates related tests to read `.newDiff`
> - Test scaffolding updated to mock the new hook shape

[CAN-8255] Rename WidgetStore iteration methods to `*Unindexed`
body:
**[CAN-8255 Rename WidgetStore iteration methods](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8255)**

The idea of this PR is to mark non-performant `WidgetStore` methods with the `Unindexed` suffix to discourage their usage.
In most cases, we don’t need to iterate over the whole store — we usually know something about the widgets, for example their type, parent, location area, or composition id. WidgetStore has indexes for these cases, which allows us to retrieve a subset of widgets. Working with subsets is usually much faster than iterating over all widgets.

`WidgetStore` method renamed:
* `filter` -> `filterUnindexed`
* `map` -> `mapUnindexed`
* `find` -> `findUnindexed`
* `reduce` -> `reduceUnindexed`
* `toArray` -> `toArrayUnindexed`

The environment: https://can-8255.mural.engineering/

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Marks whole-store iteration APIs as "unindexed" and updates the codebase accordingly.
> 
> - Renames `filter`/`map`/`find`/`reduce`/`toArray`/`forEach` to `filterUnindexed`/`mapUnindexed`/`findUnindexed`/`reduceUnindexed`/`toArrayUnindexed`/`forEachUnindexed` in `WidgetStore`
> - Migrates selectors, addons, business logic, and tests to the new names
> - Replaces several full-store scans with indexed queries (`getByType`, `getPartsOf`, `get`, `getChildren`) where applicable
> - Adjusts derivative/stacking-order computations to use `mapUnindexed`/`reduceUnindexed`

title: [CAN-8297] Refactor `beforeResizeStart` hook handler to prevent doing `apply` or `commit`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors the `beforeResizeStart` hook to return a list of changes instead of letting handlers apply them directly.

The motivation behind this change is related to keep control of who originates widget changes and when.
On a resizing operation, the changes to the widgets model should be restricted only to the resizing operation core logic.

Given that the hook was already returning a value (a list of widgets to replace for the resizing ones), the hook is now split into two so the intention is clearer: `beforeResizeStart` only notifies the operation that is about to start (and expects back a potential list of changes to apply), and a new hook called `widgetsToResize` allows handler to modify the list of affected widgets.

The change had little repercusion because most of the hook handlers were not doing any changes already, but there were a couple of exceptions.

- The Smart Planner resize plugin has been adapted to this new logic, and modified to return the newly created placeholder widget (the deletion is still in the plugin, it'll be refactored in a different PR)
- The `verifyBoard` method from the Smart Planner has been adapted to use the resizing plugin directly instead of emulating a resize operation using the hooks.

We expect no change in logic whatsoever, everything should keep working exactly as it did before.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8297)

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
[CPT-2475](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CPT-2475)
This PR implements a new truly public template preview experience that allows unauthenticated users to view and interact with templates without being redirected to sign-in. This feature is gated behind the TRULY_PUBLIC_TEMPLATE_PREVIEWS Optimizely feature flag.
<!--
1. New Route & Page Structure
- New route: /template-preview/:id/:hash for public template previews
- Route registration: Added route in src/mural/routes/index.tsx with onEnterTemplatePreview middleware
- Feature flag gating: Route middleware checks TRULY_PUBLIC_TEMPLATE_PREVIEWS flag and redirects to /template/:id/:hash if disabled

2. New Components
- TemplatePreviewPage: main page component that fetches template data and handles loading/error states
- TemplatePreviewContent: manages SDK initialization for both template and example murals
- PublicTemplateCanvas: renders the canvas with zoom controls and example toggle
-->
### Key Implementation Details
1. Dual SDK Support: For global templates with examples, both the template SDK and example SDK are initialized, allowing users to toggle between viewing the blank template and a filled-in example
2. Proper Resource Management:
isMounted flag prevents state updates on unmounted components
Cleanup function disposes both SDKs (engine.destroy(), dispatcher.dispose())
Timeout handling prevents infinite loading states
3. Canvas Integration:
Uses EngineCanvasLayer for rendering
key prop forces remount when toggling between template/example (required because EngineCanvasLayer.shouldComponentUpdate() returns false)
Includes VisualizationControlsEmbed for zoom/pan controls
4. Styling:
Uses UI Toolkit design tokens
Full viewport layout with proper canvas dimensioning
Show Example toggle positioned in bottom-left corner

title: [CAN-8323] Fix mindmap button visibility on sidebar
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes the placing of the `Mind Maps` button in the sidebar.

Because of how it was implemented, the button relied on another button (`images`) existing in the sidebar in order to be placed in the right order.
At this moment, that panel is changing into a unified panel that uses a different name. This means that when the flag controlling that feature is enabled, the `images` panel doesn't exist and the button is not registered.

This PR fixes the situation by considering both options, but also adding some fallbacks so the button is always present, even if the desired position for it can't be obtained.

### How to test this?
- Enter any mural and check that the `Mind Maps` button is present in the sidebar.
- Using the Flags Manager, turn on the `UNIFIED_IMAGES_PANEL` flag, reload, and check that the button is still appearing.

title: [CAN-8050] Unflag call to `reset` in `dragSelectedWidgets`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR removes the flag that was controlling resetting the dragging before each movement.

The motivation behind this is that, when we enable absorption as a system, we want to treat each dragging step as an atomic move between the initial state and the current, but since dragging works as a diff between last and current step, we can't make that change just yet in the productive app.

### Decisions made

In order to make the concept of `reset` work seamlessly across the app, a couple of decisions had to be made on code associated with the dragging operation:
- **The Smart Planner plugin**: this plugin handles custom behavior when the dragging involves interacting with a smart planner.
The in-a-nutshell logic behind it is that upon a `beforeDragMove` event, it will analyze if the dragging is inside an affecting operation (i.e. it involves a Smart Planner), and if not, it will not do anything afterwards.
When dragging worked in a "per movement" basis, this worked because it would constantly analyze whether the widget is about to enter a Smart Planner.
With the new `reset` logic, every `beforeDragMove` event starts from the initial point, so if it was not in a Smart Planner at the beginning, then the plugin would never act.
The solution consist in analyzing the `afterDragMove` event. So if it didn't started inside a Smart Planner, but it ended inside one, then this is, again, an affecting operation.

- **Ignore table snapping guidelines integration tests**: The tests in the modified feature file require a two steps dragging simulation. This is because the check for snapping guidelines runs _before_ the table is set as a snappable cluster.
With the introduction of the `reset` concept on each dragging movement, those two steps are now considered as "one step done twice", and so the setup needed for the tests is never accomplished, which makes the tests fail.

title: Migrates remaining "high" priority dependencies from `src/mural` to `@muralco/canvas`
body:
This PR is the second of a series moving ready to modularize canvas dependencies into the canvas package. This PR handles remaining `high` priority dependencies.

Dependency priority was determined by evaluating the number of times a specific file was being imported within the `src` directory. The breakdown of priority is as follows:

- **CRITICAL** (≥20 imports)
- **HIGH** (10-19 imports)
- **MEDIUM** (5-9 imports)
- **LOW** (1-4 imports)
- **NONE** (0 imports)

Test env: https://migrate-high-priority-deps-2.mural.engineering

## What Was Migrated

### Addons
- **Lexical command types** (`addons/core/editors/lexical/common/commands/types.ts`) - Lexical command registration and unregistration types
- **Mouse utilities** (`addons/core/mouse/right-click-pan/util.ts`) - Mouse button constants for right-click pan functionality
- **Mermaid utilities** (`addons/mermaid/extract-node-id.ts`) - Node ID extraction utilities for Mermaid diagrams
- **Mindmaps constants** (`addons/mindmaps/constants.ts`) - Mindmap formatting constants and default values

### Business Logic
- **Labels types** (`business/labels/types.ts`) - Label API types and interfaces
- **Smart frameworks types** (`business/smart-frameworks/types.ts`) - Smart framework model service types and interfaces
- **System of Record tracking** (`business/system-of-record/utils/tracking.ts`) - SOR tracking utilities

### Helpers
- **AI function call** (`helpers/ai/ai-function-call.ts`) - AI function call error handling and custom response utilities
- **AI permissions** (`helpers/ai/permissions/constants.ts`) - AI permission error constants
- **Almost equal** (`helpers/almost-equal.ts`) - Floating point comparison utility
- **Find utilities** (`helpers/find.ts`) - Widget find and filter utilities
- **Time constants** (`helpers/time-constants.ts`) - Delay and expiration time constants
- **Widget type name** (`helpers/widget-type-name.ts`) - Widget type name utilities and tracking name helpers

title: Migrates "high" priority dependencies from `src/mural` to `@muralco/canvas`
body:
This PR is the second of a series moving ready to modularize canvas dependencies into the canvas package. This PR handles `high` priority dependencies.

Dependency priority was determined by evaluating the number of times a specific file was being imported within the `src` directory. The breakdown of priority is as follows:

- **CRITICAL** (≥20 imports)
- **HIGH** (10-19 imports)
- **MEDIUM** (5-9 imports)
- **LOW** (1-4 imports)
- **NONE** (0 imports)

## What Was Migrated

### Business Logic
- **Tables utilities** (`business/tables/get-cell-format.ts`) - Table cell format utilities and default format constants
- **System of Record constants** (`business/system-of-record/constants.ts`) - SOR model version and batch size constants

### Helpers
- **Widget type name** (`helpers/widget-type-name.ts`) - Widget type name utilities and tracking name helpers

### SDK APIs
- **AI helpers** (`sdk/apis/ai/helpers.ts`) - AI chat helpers, error message utilities, and workshop ID helpers
- **Onboarding selectors** (`sdk/apis/onboarding/selectors.ts`) - Onboarding state selectors
- **Connector utilities** (`sdk/apis/widgets/changes/systems/connectors/util.ts`) - Arrow normalization and connector computation utilities

### Dispatcher APIs
- **AI dispatcher types** (`dispatcher/ai/types.ts`) - AI API types and canned response props
- **Facilitation dispatcher types** (`dispatcher/facilitation/types.ts`) - Facilitation API types including laser toggle and private mode status
- **Mural dispatcher types** (`dispatcher/mural/types.ts`) - Mural API types including duplicate and inner state types
- **Notifications dispatcher** (`dispatcher/notifications/`) - Notifications API creation and types
- **Participants dispatcher types** (`dispatcher/participants/types.ts`) - Participants API types

### Addons
- **Lexical editor constants** (`addons/core/editors/lexical/common/consts.ts`) - Lexical editor default format and base features

## Changes Summary

- **191 files changed**: 290 addition

title: [NEXT-391] Migrate "critical" `src/mural` dependencies
body:
This PR is the first of a series moving ready to modularize canvas dependencies into the canvas package. This PR handles `critical` dependencies.

Dependency priority was determined by evaluating the number of times a specific file was being imported within the `src` directory. The breakdown of priority is as follows:

- **CRITICAL** (≥20 imports)
- **HIGH** (10-19 imports)
- **MEDIUM** (5-9 imports)
- **LOW** (1-4 imports)
- **NONE** (0 imports)

## What Was Migrated

### Business Logic
- **System of Record types** (`business/system-of-record/types/`) - Resource definitions and types
- **Tags types** (`business/tags/types.ts`) - Taggable widget types and utilities

### Helpers
- **AI helpers** (`helpers/ai/`) - AI chat entry utilities, token management, and preview mode helpers
- **Measure widget** (`helpers/measure-widget.ts`) - Widget measurement utilities

### SDK APIs
- **Features selectors** (`sdk/apis/features/selectors.ts`) - Feature flag selectors
- **Viewport selectors** (`sdk/apis/viewport/selectors.ts`) - Viewport transformation selectors

### Primitives
- **Mural primitive API** (`sdk/primitives/mural/`) - Mural configuration primitive moved to canvas package

## Changes Summary

- **235 files changed**: 454 additions, 475 deletions
- **Updated imports**: All consuming files now import from `@muralco/canvas` instead of relative paths
- **Added dependency**: `@muralco/optimizely` added to canvas package dependencies

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Modularizes high-traffic shared code into `@muralco/canvas` and aligns all call sites.
> 
> - Extracts and exports AI utilities (`helpers/ai/*`), `measure-widget`, taggable widget types, and system-of-record resource types from `src/mural` to `packages/canvas` with new `index` barrels
> - Adds feature flag and viewport selectors under `canvas/sdk/apis` and updates usages across UI/addons/dispatcher/tests
> - Introduces `createMuralPrimitiveApi` in `canvas/sdk/primitives`

title: [CAN-8050] Refactor `dragSelectedWidgets` logic
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This is an attempt to split the work from https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45893 (currently closed).

The motivation behind this is to remove the current flag controlling the resetting of changes before each dragging movement.

Right now the code, under the flag, would `reset` the changes on every drag move, but only re-add any duplicated widget afterwards in an attempt to recreate the initial conditions of the dragging.
However, lots of stuff can happen when we first start a dragging, and resetting should recreate them all in order to have a proper jump from the initial state to the current.

In this PR, everything that happens during initialization is now stored in an action that is re-applied after every `reset` to maintain consistency.

Given that this code is still flagged, no change in behavior is expected.

#### Reviewer Resources

title: Fixed issue with undo functionality for table Column & Rows deletion
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer


- Undo for table row/column deletion now restores the table layout through the Widget Changes API without mutating the table model in-place, so rows/columns are included in the persisted update (not just width/height).

- Added a regression unit test that runs delete-middle-row/column → undo and asserts the persisted update for the table contains the restored rows/columns.

### Case Solved

**How to reproduce:** Create a 3×3 table → delete the middle column → undo → open the mural as another editor/visitor → try changing a middle cell background color.

**Expected results:**

Undo persists the restored table layout, so collaborators see a valid table and cell background changes work consistently.

**Actual result before fix:**

Undo “looked” correct for the user who performed it, but the restored rows/columns weren’t persisted; other clients loaded a corrupted table state and cell background changes no-op’d.

### How the Change Fixes It

- sdk.widgets.changes.commit() persists by diffing the store snapshot from the first apply against the current store; only real store diffs become API updates.

- Previously, undo directly assigned table.properties.rows/columns before staging newTableChanges, making the “restore layout” update redundant at diff time; the commit ended up persisting only size changes from layout recomputation.

- The change keeps the “restored rows/columns” in local variables for calculations and only updates the table via sdk.widgets.changes.apply(newTableChanges), so commit() sees and persists the rows/columns change and prevents remote corruption.


### Reviewer Resources
-  🏷️ [JIRA](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8315) 
- 🧪  [ENV](https://can-8315.mural.engineering/)


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

title: Added role column, tooltip to license column and menu items when RBAC is enabled
body:
## Summary

This PR adds RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) support to the workspace users table. When RBAC is enabled, the table now displays a Role column and provides role management actions. Additionally, a helpful tooltip is added to the License column to explain the member vs guest distinction.

Testing Env: https://iam-2308-ws-role-support.mural.engineering/

## Changes

### New Features
1. **Role Column** (workspace-user-role-cell.tsx)
   - Displays "Admin" or "Member" based on user's `roleId`
   - Only shown when RBAC is enabled
   - Replaces "Last Seen" column when RBAC is active

2. **License Column Tooltip**
   - Added tooltip: "Members are internal users, and guests are external users. Each is entitled to different permissions."
   - Only shown when RBAC is enabled

3. **Role Management Actions**
   - New actions: `GRANT_ADMIN_ACCESS` and `REMOVE_ADMIN_ACCESS`
   - Uses `RoleActions` component instead of `Actions` when RBAC is enabled
   - Role changes handled via `updateManyRoles` API endpoint

### API Changes
- Added `updateManyRoles` method to `workspacesApi.members`
- Added `WorkspaceRoles` enum and `WorkspaceMemberRoleUpdate` type
- Added `roleId` field to `ListMember` interface

### Component Changes
- New hook: `useUpdateWorkspaceUserRoleRequest` for role updates
- New function: `getAvailableWorkspaceUserRbacActionsForSelectMenu` for RBAC-specific actions
- Modified `getWorkspaceUserColumns` to conditionally render columns based on RBAC flag
- Modified `renderWorkspaceUserActionCell` to use `RoleActions` when RBAC is enabled

## Technical Details

### Conditional Rendering
- **When `isCompanyUsingRbac === true`:**
  - Shows Role column (replaces Last Seen)
  - Hides permission columns (Create Rooms, Can Publish Templates, Can Discover Public Rooms, Admin)
  - Uses `RoleActions` component for actions
  - Shows tooltip on License column

- **When `isCompanyUsingRbac === false`:**
  - Shows Last Seen column

title: [SCQM-1564] Fix table widget child selection in ai-action summarize
body:
Card: [SCQM-1564](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1564)
Env: https://scqm-1564-summarize-table.mural.engineering/
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When a table was selected, the action version of summarize would not select its descendents (including table cells with text), leading to either an error if only the table was selected or the table's content being ignored in a summary if other items were also selected.

The bug was due to using `selectedWidgets` instead of the `summarizableWidgets` result from `getAISummarizableWidgets` in places sending the list of widgets to be summarized. The definition of `summarizableWidgets` is moved a little earlier to allow it to be used in place of `selectedWidgets` when creating the request message.

Migrates `sdk/hooks` and related utilities from `src/mural/` to the `packages/canvas/` package.

This PR refactors the hooks architecture to follow a clearer separation of concerns: each hook module now has a `create.ts` file containing the implementation (previously in `index.ts`), while `index.ts` serves as a barrel export for types only. This improves the package structure and makes the API boundaries clearer.

title: [SCQM-1544] Add AI performance tracking to mindmap functions
body:
Env: https://scqm-1544-mindmap-trackperf.mural.engineering
Card: [SCQM-1544](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1544)

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This adds calls to the `sdk.ai.performanceTracking` series of functions to the `expandMindmap` and `createMindmap` functions. This tracks the timing of the generate endpoint request to generate the new nodes. Because of the way the preview mode works for the mindmap functions, the time between the first preview and the final content is basically the same in most cases, but both are tracked. Because `expandMindmap` is called by `createMindmap` to do the actual generation, but `createMindmap` creates additional content and also starts preview mode itself, the calls to `performanceTracking` exit in both functions, with a new option passed to `expandMindmap` to stop it from doing its own calls to `performanceTracking` when being used as a sub-routine of `createMindmap`. `expandMindmap` does still call `performanceTracking.cancel` when it hits errors, because the return type is insufficient for `createMindmap` to know an error happened and cancel the tracking itself.

It also adds a new `sdk.ai.performanceTracking.markPendingAction` to allow the "AI feature" infrastructure to set a start time and other additional context prior to the actual performance tracking start and mark calls made in the function itself. This takes an `actionType` and overrides the start time and context of the next call to `start` with a matching `actionType`, and avoids needing to somehow associate a `sessionId` across the feature code and the expected function the AI chat calls. Because it just matches the next `actionType` it won't work if the AI chat doesn't call the expected function type (all mindmap functions are using an `actionType` of `mindmap`, and the feature marks a pending action of `mindmap` or `flowchart`) after clicking the Create Diagram button in the form.

title: [FEP-6419] - migrate depcheck to knip
body:
## Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

[FEP-6419](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/FEP-6419)

This PR removes the `depcheck` dependency because it's no longer maintained. The functionality provided by `depcheck` has been replaced with `knip`, which is actively maintained and offers similar features for checking unused dependencies in the project.

### Changes Made
- Removed `depcheck` from the project's dependencies.
- Updated the `muralco-depcheck` script to use `knip` instead of `depcheck`.
- Added warning message for unused dependencies found by `knip`.

The script will now throw an error if it finds any unlisted dependency or print a warning message if it finds any unused dependency.

#### Unlisted dependency

A package imported/required in code but not declared in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies, or peerDependencies). Knip flags these as missing declarations.

Example: code imports react-select, but react-select isn't in dependencies, devDependencies or peerDependencies in package.json.

#### Unused dependency

A package declared in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies, or peerDependencies) but not imported/required anywhere in the codebase. Knip flags these as potentially removable. It's less critical than unlisted dependencies since they don't break functionality, but they can bloat the project and should be cleaned up.

Example: package.json lists lodash, but no file imports lodash.

title: [CAN-8296] Refactor `afterDuplicate` hook to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR is a continuation of the work in https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46637.

Whenever we perform a duplication, we dispatch a set of hooks that can potentially alter the result of the operation.
This makes us lose control over who modifies the widgets model and where, which is something that goes against our intention for the new architecture of changes.

The work in the previous PR addressed the hook handler `beforeDuplicate`, whereas this one focuses on the `afterDuplicate` counterpart.

In the last PR, following some discussion, we actually modified the code to create a new set of `before` and `after` hooks targeted specifically to duplication by alt+dragging, which actually solved the main issue that was blocking us.
However, given that the work was already started there, and that there was only one hook handler (Smart Planner) that needed amending to comply with the new requirement, this PR finishes the work by refactoring the hook to return a list of changes instead of applying them directly.

No change in behavior is expected whatsoever.

Tests should assert that duplicating widgets using the Cmd+D shortcut or the context menu option, in general, continues working as expected, and specifically for mindmaps, tables and Smart Planners, it behaves exactly as it did before.

title: Update CODEOWNERS for agent skills config folders

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Within the last couple weeks, [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/what-are-skills) have become a [broadly adopted standard](https://agentskills.io/home#adoption) for packaging agent workflows.

Agent Skills are powerful because
1. they combine all of the existing customization vectors for agent behavior (e.g. custom prompts/commands, tools, instructions, documentation, scripts) into a single transportable folder, and
2. skills are [_**automatically pulled into context**_ ](https://agentskills.io/specification#progressive-disclosure) when the agent feels it is appropriate.

This PR updates CODEOWNERS to add ownership for agent skills and agent configuration folders.

title: Move to Package Tool : Adds support for package to package file moves (and more refactoring)
body:
## Overview

This PR extends the `move-to-package` refactoring tool to support **package-to-package moves** (moving files from `packages/` to `packages/`), in addition to the existing `src/` to `packages/` functionality. It also includes significant improvements to import rewriting accuracy and barrel file cleanup.

## Key Features

### 🎯 Package-to-Package Moves
- **New capability**: Move files from one package to another (e.g., `packages/shared/src/util.ts` → `packages/test-mocks/src/util.ts`)
- Automatically detects source package information when moving from `packages/`
- Rewrites package imports (e.g., `@muralco/shared` → `@muralco/test-mocks`) using symbol-based resolution
- Handles barrel file cleanup in both source and destination packages

### 🔍 Symbol-Based Import Resolution
- **Improved accuracy**: Uses TypeScript's type system to trace symbols through barrel files
- Verifies that imports actually use symbols from the moved file before rewriting
- Handles complex scenarios:
  - Direct symbol declarations
  - Re-exports through barrel files
  - Aliased symbols
  - Subpath exports (e.g., `@muralco/canvas/business`)
- Falls back to name matching when symbol resolution fails

### 🧹 Enhanced Barrel File Cleanup
- **AST-based cleanup**: Uses ts-morph to parse and remove individual export lines
- Removes only the specific exports referencing the moved file
- Falls back to string-based removal if AST parsing fails
- Cleans up both source and destination package barrels when moving between packages

### 🧪 Test Organization
- **Split large test file** into focused test suites:
  - `move-to-package-barrels.test.ts` - Barrel file operations
  - `move-to-package-imports.test.ts` - Import rewriting logic
  - `move-to-package-packages.test.ts` - Package name resolution
  - `move-to-package-helpers.test.ts` - Helper functions and validation
- **Shared test utilities** in `move-to-package-test-utils.ts` for consistency
- Comprehensive te

title: [CAN-8295] Refactor `beforeDuplicate` hook to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors the hook `duplicate.beforeDuplicate`, called whenever we're about to perform a duplication of widgets, to return a list of widget changes instead of a void response.
It also wraps the call within the hooks scope, which prevents any calls to `apply`, `update` or `commit` to be done within a registered handler.

This hook is defined as an async operation given that it can potentially show a modal for confirmation, therefore the proper return type has been refactored to `Promise<ActionList>`.

However, there's currently no handler registered that is actually doing any widget modification, so the change should be innocuous.

The motivation behind the change is to have better control of how widget modifications are being applied.

**UPDATE:** Following a comment in the PR, I also added a new set of hook on the `drag` namespace to have a clearer separation of responsabilities, therefore in this PR we also implement the new hook handlers `drag.beforeDuplicate` and `drag.afterDuplicate`

title: [CAN-8220] Fix undo/redo behavior when applying widget distribution
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes undo/redo behavior for widget distribution operations by joining all the changes into one single transaction that can be undone or redone by a single command instead of having to do one movement at a time.

This also fixes the selection of the widgets after the undo/redo operation: when doing any sort of distribution, if one of the widgets ended up in the same original place it was before, undoing the operation would not select it back because it was never patched in the first place.
In this PR we amend the situation by creating an explicit selection step for those widgets.
