title: [CAN-7819] Refactor widget distribution code to use the Widget Changes API - Part II
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors the widget distribution logic to properly use the `Widget Changes API`.
This is a continuation of the work started in [this PR](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46564).

The current logic (for any kind of distribution chosen) operates in the following way:
- First, we generate a children - parent map of the affected widgets
- We then proceed to orphan every widget
- Then, we generate the changes for the chosen distribution
- We apply those generated changes
- Finally, we re-parent every widget with the following condition:
  - If the top-left most widget was initially in a table cell and the table had auto-resize enabled, every widget should fall inside that cell which should expand to fit
  - Otherwise, each widget should fall wherever it corresponds according to our absorption rules

The way this was currently operating was with a mixed of manual updates and changes applied that ran systems.

In order to have a better expected behavior and a full adaptation to our current architecture, we need to make it so they only apply changes through the `Widget Changes API`.

In this second part we modify the core logic to gather all the changes first and do as few calls to `apply` as possible, and only one call to `commit`, with no `update` anywhere.

**No change in behavior is expected in this PR**. Widget distribution should continue working exactly as it did before this PR.


#### Reviewer Resources

title: [CAN-8278] Refactor widget distribution code to use the Widget Changes API - Part I
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors the entire widget distribution logic to use the `Widget Changes API`.

The current logic (for any kind of distribution chosen) operates in the following way:
- First, we generate a children - parent map of the affected widgets
- We then proceed to orphan every widget
- Then, we apply the chosen distribution
- Finally, we re-parent every widget with the following condition:
  - If the top-left most widget was initially in a table cell and the table had auto-resize enabled, every widget should fall inside that cell which should expand to fit
  - Otherwise, each widget should fall wherever it corresponds according to our absorption rules

The way this was currently operating was with a mixed of manual updates and changes applied that ran systems.

In order to have a better expected behavior and a full adaptation to our current architecture, we need to make it so they only apply changes through the `Widget Changes API`.

This first PR modifies all the distribution logic functions to return a list of changes instead of doing any update by themselves.
The main core of the function still works in an unwanted way, but will now only collect changes from the distribution logic.

The next part will modify this to do as few calls to `apply` as possible, only one `commit`, and no `update` calls.

**No change in behavior is expected in this PR**. Widget distribution should continue working exactly as it did before this PR.

title: Fixed issue with undo functionality for table reshaping and added uni…
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer


- Reshape undo/redo now records both forward and revert plans in ReshapeTableStep and registers the step before per-cell fit adjustments. Undo now replays the original table dimensions before any fit-to-content steps reflow cells, restoring size/positions; redo replays the applied plan.

- Added a unit test verifying ReshapeTableStep applies the forward plan on redo and restores dimensions on undo.

### Case Solved

**Precondition to reproduce:** Table cell auto resize has to be turned off.

**Description:** If a user shrinks a table with several widgets inside to the point where the widgets overlap with each other and the uses de undo function the table elements inside the table do not go back to its previous positions. In addition the table does not change back to its original size.

**Expected results:**

An undo of a table resizing should always preserve the previous state size and position of the table and its elements.

**Actual result before fix:**

Shrinking a table with widgets to the point that the widgets inside overlap produces inconsistent results after an undo of the resize.

### How the Change Fixes It

On resize end, reshapeTable now pushes the undo step before fitting cells and passes both forward and revert plans. The undo stack therefore has the pre-resize geometry and executes in reverse order: fit adjustments undo first, then the reshape step restores the original table size/position. Redo replays the forward plan and subsequent fits, preserving consistency even when cells overlap with auto-resize off.


### Reviewer Resources
-  🏷️ [JIRA](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8210) 
- 🧪  [ENV](https://can-8210.mural.engineering/)


### Relevant Links 🔗
- [Recorded Video of issue](https://www.loom.com/share/57a85847954e4e29944b8ececa561bd2)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: [SCQM-1388] Send tracking on AI Action events
body:
Card: [SCQM-1388](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1388)
Env: https://scqm-1388-fe-actagent-events.mural.engineering
murally PR: tactivos/mural-api#15092

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Adds event tracking on AI action starting, result success/fail (with token counts of the result), refine starting, and final accept/decline on the preview (with session-total token counts).

The events should be pretty easy to add new ones for new actions, it should be possible to do a
```
type AIActionFoobarEvent = BaseAIActionEvent<'foobar'>;
```
if there's no custom fields for the payloads, or add new payload types as needed and do a
```
type AIActionFoobarEvent = BaseAIActionEvent<
  'foobar',
  AIActionFoobarStartPayload,
  AIActionFoobarRefinePayload,
  AIActionFoobarResultPayload
>;
```
to get an `AIActionFoobarEvent` to add to the `AIActionEvent` union.

New events all include `sessionId`, `actionType` (always 'summarize' for all summarize variants), `refinementRound` (number, starts at 0 on non-refinement initial request), `widgetsCount` of input widgets, `wordsCount` of input widgets word count, an optional `refinementType` (if there is a refinement happening), and `variant` to track orchestrator version.
- On start: `ai_action_summarize_start`, also has `entryPoint: 'actionbar' | 'toolbar-dropdown'`
- On result success: `ai_action_summarize_result_success` also with token counts (of this one result)
- On result failure: `ai_action_summarize_result_fail`
- On refine start (when clicking option in refine menu): `ai_action_summarize_refine_start` with `refinementType` set (result success/failure will also have refinementType)
- On accept: `ai_action_summarize_accept` also with token counts of all results in session (and with `refinementRounds` showing total number of refinements and `refinementType` set to last refinement done)
- On discard: `ai_action_summarize_discard`, payload the same as _accept.

title: [NEXT-362] Migrate Input, Toolbar, and Core `src/register/types.ts` types to `@muralco/canvas/register`
body:
## Overview

This PR begins breaking apart the `src/mural/register/types.ts` monolith by splitting types into logical, domain-specific modules within the `@muralco/canvas` package to support the modularization of the canvas. 

## Type Migrations

### Core Register Types (`packages/canvas/src/register/types/`)

Split the monolith into three focused modules:

1. **`core.ts`** - Foundational extension types:
   - `ExtensionArrayApi<T>`
   - `ComponentExtension<TProps>`
   - `ArrayValue<T>`, `ArrayValueOrFn<T>`, `ValueMapFn<T>`
   - `NotFunctionOrArray<T>`

2. **`input.ts`** - User input handling types:
   - `KeyboardHandler` and `SyntheticMuralKeyboardEvent`
   - `MouseProcessor` and mouse event types
   - `SimpleTouchEvent`, `GestureEvent`, `TouchEventType`
   - `ContextualInformation` and `AppliesFn`

3. **`toolbar.ts`** - Toolbar-related types:
   - `ToolBarItemButton`, `ToolBarItemDropdown`, `ToolBarItemGroup`
   - `ToolBarItemMenu`, `ToolBarItemSelector`
   - `ToolBarItemSpec` (deprecated, use `RegistrableTool` instead)
   - `AIToolBarDropdownOptionSpec`

### Additional Type Migrations

- **Addon Types** → `packages/canvas/src/addons/`
  - Export selection constants (`EXPORT_SELECTION_MURAL_MODE`, etc.)

### SDK Type Migration

- **`ProperMuralMode`** → `packages/canvas/src/sdk/apis/mural/mode.ts`
  - Moved from `src/mural/sdk/apis/mural/types.ts` to the SDK package
  - Now exported from `@muralco/canvas/sdk/apis`

title: [CAN-8246] Refactor dragging hook handlers to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is the last PR in a series ([1](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46369), [2](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46413), [3](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46422), [4](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46444), [5](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46487) & [6](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46495)) that comprehended refactoring the entire logic of the Smart Planner dragging plugin to return a list of accumulated changes instead of applying them directly.
Motivation behind those changes can be found on each PR and also here below.

In this PR we first address two remaining refactors that were left over from the previous work, and then move onto the final goal of the entire effort: preventing dragging hook handlers from making changes in the widgets model directly.

The way this work is twofold:
1. We modify the dragging hook interface so that every hook now is expected to return a list of accumulated changes.
2. We add a protection to the hook handlers so that if they ever call `update`, `apply` or `commit` from within their implementation, a runtime error is thrown.

Regarding 2, it would have been amazing to be able to write something that would detect this while coding, but while TS is pretty powerful, it's not _that_ powerful.
My believe is that anyone adding a call to `apply` from within a hook handler will probably want to test their implementation, and while doing that will found the error on screen and address it properly (also, they'll be forced to return an `ActionList` through their implementation, which should hint to them that they shouldn't be applying the changes themselves).

**Note:** Every other PR in the series had no expected consequences in behavior because they were all mere refactors that moved the code around.

This is **not** the case here: there is a BIG impactful change here: Smart Planners are no longer committing change

title: [CAN-8243] [CAN-8245] Refactor `afterDragMove` and `afterDragEnd` to do one `apply` and `commit` per call
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR refactors the code for the `afterDragMove` and `afterDragEnd` hook handlers from the `KanbanBoardDragPlugin` class to minimize the number of calls to `widgets.changes.apply`. There's no expected change in behavior or logic whatsoever here, everything is supposed to be working exactly as it always did.
Motivation behind this change 👇 As part of the refactor of the code to use the `Widget Changes API` for widget updating and to run systems for side effects, we find ourselves with the task of making some business changes along the way. One of those is the fact that _dragging_ now operates in the following way: on each drag movement, we `reset` any applied change, gather all the new information for the new delta, and `apply` the new changes. This means, for the systems, that each dragging step is actually a sort of "unique atomic" movement between the **initial** position and the **current** (i.e. no middle steps). The problem with this approach is that dragging (as well as other actions in the app) can be modified on the fly by some middleware hooks that can register to specific dragging-related actions (before drag start, after drag move, etc). Given that we use an observer pattern for handling hooks, we have no control over what each handler does, and that means that a handler can potentially `apply` and even `commit` changes in our model. Once a change has been committed, it can be reset, and that represents a problem. One of the main actors here that implements such logic is the Smart Planner which does, in fact, apply and commit changes within hook handlers. Refactoring that entire code to prevent such behavior is a really big and demanding task, far too much for a single PR, and that's why you're looking now at one of the PRs that helps achieve that goal.
#### Reviewer Resources - 🏷️ [**CAN-8243**](https://mural.atlassian.net/b

title: [CAN-8241] Refactor `moveBetweenColumns` to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR refactors the code for the `moveBetweenColumns` function from the `KanbanBoardCardsApi` class to only accumulate changes and return them back to the caller, instead of applying them directly. There's no expected change in behavior or logic whatsoever here, everything is supposed to be working exactly as it always did.
Motivation behind this change 👇 As part of the refactor of the code to use the `Widget Changes API` for widget updating and to run systems for side effects, we find ourselves with the task of making some business changes along the way. One of those is the fact that _dragging_ now operates in the following way: on each drag movement, we `reset` any applied change, gather all the new information for the new delta, and `apply` the new changes. This means, for the systems, that each dragging step is actually a sort of "unique atomic" movement between the **initial** position and the **current** (i.e. no middle steps). The problem with this approach is that dragging (as well as other actions in the app) can be modified on the fly by some middleware hooks that can register to specific dragging-related actions (before drag start, after drag move, etc). Given that we use an observer pattern for handling hooks, we have no control over what each handler does, and that means that a handler can potentially `apply` and even `commit` changes in our model. Once a change has been committed, it can be reset, and that represents a problem. One of the main actors here that implements such logic is the Smart Planner which does, in fact, apply and commit changes within hook handlers. Refactoring that entire code to prevent such behavior is a really big and demanding task, far too much for a single PR, and that's why you're looking now at one of the PRs that helps achieve that goal.

body:
# Remove Remaining Dashboard Route References from v1 Cucumber Tests

## Summary

This PR removes the last remaining references to the `/dashboard` route from v1 Cucumber test infrastructure by migrating those tests to Jest unit tests and v2. All v1 Cucumber feature files that used the deprecated `/dashboard` route have been removed and replaced with Jest tests and v2.

Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/ENGAGE-1447

## What Changed

### Removed (v1 Cucumber Tests)
- ❌ `features/canvas/async/unread-notifications/last-seen-mural.feature` - Used `/dashboard` route
- ❌ `features/canvas/topbar/back/back-button.feature` - Used `/dashboard` route
- ❌ `features/learning/learning-topbar.feature` - Used "dashboard learning" route reference

### Added (Jest Unit Tests)
- ✅ `src/dashboard/common/breadcrumbs.test.tsx` - Breadcrumbs component tests
- ✅ `src/dashboard/learning/header/index.test.tsx` - Learning header component tests
- ✅ `src/mural/dispatcher/async/last-seen-mural.test.ts` - Last seen mural dispatcher tests

### Updated
- Migrated `back-button.feature` from v1 to v2 cucumber format (updated routes to `/t/${W.username}/home`)
- Updated test infrastructure mocks and step definitions

## Code Coverage

**v1 (Cucumber)**: Integration test coverage via NYC/Istanbul (`npm run test:react:cc`)
- Coverage includes all source files (`src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js}`)

**v2 (Jest)**: Unit test coverage via Jest built-in (`npm run test:unit:cc`)
- Coverage includes files imported by tests
- Provides component-level granularity

## Impact

✅ **Removed all `/dashboard` route references from v1 test infrastructure**
✅ Migrated to Jest for faster, more maintainable unit tests
✅ Improved test coverage granularity (component-level vs integration-level)

title: [CAN-8242] Refactor `updateWidgetsStatusLabel` to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR refactors the code for the `updateWidgetsStatusLabel` and `updateWidgetsStatus` functions from the `TicketModelService` to minimize the number of calls to `widgets.changes.apply`. There's no expected change in behavior or logic whatsoever here, everything is supposed to be working exactly as it always did.
Motivation behind this change 👇 As part of the refactor of the code to use the `Widget Changes API` for widget updating and to run systems for side effects, we find ourselves with the task of making some business changes along the way. One of those is the fact that _dragging_ now operates in the following way: on each drag movement, we `reset` any applied change, gather all the new information for the new delta, and `apply` the new changes. This means, for the systems, that each dragging step is actually a sort of "unique atomic" movement between the **initial** position and the **current** (i.e. no middle steps). The problem with this approach is that dragging (as well as other actions in the app) can be modified on the fly by some middleware hooks that can register to specific dragging-related actions (before drag start, after drag move, etc). Given that we use an observer pattern for handling hooks, we have no control over what each handler does, and that means that a handler can potentially `apply` and even `commit` changes in our model. Once a change has been committed, it can be reset, and that represents a problem. One of the main actors here that implements such logic is the Smart Planner which does, in fact, apply and commit changes within hook handlers. Refactoring that entire code to prevent such behavior is a really big and demanding task, far too much for a single PR, and that's why you're looking now at one of the PRs that helps achieve that goal.
#### Reviewer Resources - 🏷 ️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassia

title: [SCQM-1391] Performance Tracking
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Adds a helper class that can track the following for all AI actions:

- TTFP (Time to First Preview): Time from request initiation until preview mode starts
- TTFC (Time to First Content): Time from request initiation until first actionable chunk arrives
- TTFnC (Time to Final Content): Time from request initiation until operation completes

``` javascript
// Example API usage:
const tracker = new AIPerformanceTracker();

// Start tracking (when request initiates)
tracker.start('summarize', sessionId, { refinementRound: 0 });

// Mark preview mode start
tracker.markFirstPreview('summarize', sessionId);

// Mark first content received
tracker.markFirstContent('summarize', sessionId);

// Mark operation complete
tracker.markFinalContent('summarize', sessionId);
```

title: [NEXT-353] Add formatting to move-to-package
body: ## Pull request overview This PR adds automatic code formatting to the move-to-package refactoring tool. The tool now runs ESLint and Prettier on all modified files after moving and rewriting imports, ensuring consistent code style. It also improves git commit handling by capturing file states before/after operations and staging only the files modified by the tool. Key changes: - Adds iterative ESLint and Prettier formatting that runs until files stabilize (typically 1-2 passes) - Refactors git commit logic to use git status for change detection and selective file staging - Tracks formatting passes in the execution plan for better visibility Note: It's not a perfect solution because it *can* still lead to eslint issues if formatting happens to place the import right under where a //eslint-disable-next-line directive is Jira ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/NEXT-353

title: [CAN-8240] Refactor `removeFromColumn` to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR refactors the code for the `removeFromColumn` function from the `KanbanBoardCardsApi` to minimize the number of calls to `widgets.changes.apply`. There's no expected change in behavior or logic whatsoever here, everything is supposed to be working exactly as it always did.
Motivation behind this change 👇 As part of the refactor of the code to use the `Widget Changes API` for widget updating and to run systems for side effects, we find ourselves with the task of making some business changes along the way. One of those is the fact that _dragging_ now operates in the following way: on each drag movement, we `reset` any applied change, gather all the new information for the new delta, and `apply` the new changes. This means, for the systems, that each dragging step is actually a sort of "unique atomic" movement between the **initial** position and the **current** (i.e. no middle steps). The problem with this approach is that dragging (as well as other actions in the app) can be modified on the fly by some middleware hooks that can register to specific dragging-related actions (before drag start, after drag move, etc). Given that we use an observer pattern for handling hooks, we have no control over what each handler does, and that means that a handler can potentially `apply` and even `commit` changes in our model. Once a change has been committed, it can be reset, and that represents a problem. One of the main actors here that implements such logic is the Smart Planner which does, in fact, apply and commit changes within hook handlers. Refactoring that entire code to prevent such behavior is a really big and demanding task, far too much for a single PR, and that's why you're looking now at one of the PRs that helps achieve that goal.

title: ECOMM-277 Migrate v1 cucumber test: pay-invoice-notification.feature
body:
## Fix pay invoice notification tracking tests

Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/ECOMM/boards/572?selectedIssue=ECOMM-277

### Problem
Tests for pay invoice notification tracking were failing because the `record()` function from `@muralco/tracking-lib` wasn't consistently populating the test environment's `$trackingQueue`, which is used for test assertions.

### Solution
Added a test-specific mock in `src/test/react-new/step-definitions/tracking.ts` that wraps the `record` function to ensure `window.analytics.track()` is called directly. This ensures tracking events are captured in the test environment's tracking queue for assertions.

The mock:
- Preserves the original `record()` function behavior
- Explicitly calls `window.analytics.track()` for test compatibility
- Includes a guard to prevent infinite loops
- Is properly restored after each test

### Changes
- Modified `src/test/react-new/step-definitions/tracking.ts` to add a `sinon.stub()` for `trackingLib.record` in the `Before` hook
- Fixed TypeScript linting errors (replaced `AnalyticsPayload` with `SegmentEvent`, added proper type declarations)

### Result
✅ All 11 scenarios in `pay-invoice-notification.feature` now pass
- 6 dashboard tests passing
- 5 canvas tests passing

No production code changes were made - this is purely a test environment fix.

title: [NEXT-335] Migrates prerequisite canvas constants & helpers for `src/amp/types`
body:
### Summary
This PR is part of a series of changes preparing to migrate `src/amp/types` to a package. This PR handles migrating some shared constants and helpers commonly used across the codebase. 

### What Changed

#### New Package Exports

Added two new export paths to `@muralco/canvas`:

- **`@muralco/canvas/helpers`** - Math and geometry utility functions
- **`@muralco/canvas/sdk/common`** - SDK-level constants and configuration values

#### Relocated Files

| From | To |
|------|-----|
| `src/mural/helpers/math.ts` | `packages/canvas/src/helpers/math.ts` |
| `src/mural/helpers/closest.ts` | `packages/canvas/src/helpers/closest.ts` |
| `src/mural/sdk/consts-the-universe-must-be-aware-of.ts` | `packages/canvas/src/sdk/common/consts-the-universe-must-be-aware-of.ts` |

### Import Changes

All imports across the codebase have been updated from local paths to package paths:

```typescript
// Before
import { clamp, round } from '../../../helpers/math';
import { TABLE_CELL_SEPARATION } from '../../../sdk/consts-the-universe-must-be-aware-of';

// After
import { clamp, round } from '@muralco/canvas/helpers';
import { TABLE_CELL_SEPARATION } from '@muralco/canvas/sdk/common';
```

### Why

This is part of the ongoing effort to modularize the murally codebase for:
- **Better code organization**: Shared utilities live in a dedicated package
- **Reusability**: These utilities can now be used by other packages in the monorepo
- **Future AMP migration**: Prepares viewport manager and related code for extraction

title: Refactor Smart Planner utilitaries to reduce calls to `apply`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR refactors several utilitaries functions from within the Enhanced Kanban Board and Smart Planner code to attempt to minimize the number of calls to `widgets.changes.apply`. There's no expected change in behavior or logic whatsoever here, everything is supposed to be working exactly as it always did.
Motivation behind this change 👇 As part of the refactor of the code to use the `Widget Changes API` for widget updating and to run systems for side effects, we find ourselves with the task of making some business changes along the way. One of those is the fact that _dragging_ now operates in the following way: on each drag movement, we `reset` any applied change, gather all the new information for the new delta, and `apply` the new changes. This means, for the systems, that each dragging step is actually a sort of "unique atomic" movement between the **initial** position and the **current** (i.e. no middle steps). The problem with this approach is that dragging (as well as other actions in the app) can be modified on the fly by some middleware hooks that can register to specific dragging-related actions (before drag start, after drag move, etc). Given that we use an observer pattern for handling hooks, we have no control over what each handler does, and that means that a handler can potentially `apply` and even `commit` changes in our model. Once a change has been committed, it can be reset, and that represents a problem. One of the main actors here that implements such logic is the Smart Planner which does, in fact, apply and commit changes within hook handlers. Refactoring that entire code to prevent such behavior is a really big and demanding task, far too much for a single PR, and that's why you're looking now at one of the PRs that helps achieve that goal.
🌎 **Test env:** https://kanban-drag.mural.engineering/

title: [SCQM-1511] Handle connected and isolated cycles
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes the mermaid diagram was erroring out quite frequently when you tried to do multi direction charts ---  aka `A <--> B` that creates a loop. 

Changes:
1. In the function definition (API side), specify that any user provided multi direction arrows should be replaced by two single direction arrows. While technically mermaid supports this, it doesn't seem to work reliably and a quick google said that it is known to be inconsistent / buggy. 
2. In the UI, we were previously excluding cycles from the `depthGroups` so when you requested a diagram that only contained a cycle, `depthGroups` being empty meant the `gridLayout` was empty which meant when trying to add the widgets, there was a type error when trying to get the X coordinate from a layout element that didn't exist. 


Also I added d1fcdcc9923d22bec3fb63e6ebc2b067fbf4710e for [SCQM-1512](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1512) to allow single node "charts"

1. `create a flowchart TD start` to test the single node fix

3. `flowchart TD A <--> B A --> C B --> C`
5. `Build a diagram that must be bidirectional: A flows to B, B flows back to A, and both connect downward to C.`

title: [CAN-8121] Allow nested areas to "steal" widgets from its parent (absorption system version)
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR implements the concept of "stealing" for nested areas **when using absorption as a system**.

Whenever an area enters another, and becomes a child of the latter, if the final position of the nested area is fully containing children of the parenting cluster, it now has the ability to "steal" them from it.

This means that any widget inside an area will become child of any nested area that is added to the bigger cluster:

![Nov-19-2025 08-46-49](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87bd60b5-594a-44fa-b378-abbf2d532e3b)

**Flags needed for this behavior:**
- `FEATURES.ENABLE_NESTED_AREAS`
- `FEATURES.ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS`

This should work for all the cases where nesting can occur:
- Dragging an area inside another
- Dragging an already nested area
- Resizing an already nested area 
- Dragging an area from the sidebar onto another
- Pasting an area inside another
- Adding a nested area via the context menu
- Duplicating an area onto another
- Clicking "Absorb" from the toolbar of a nested area (this one is hard to test because you'd have to force a situation where a widget is inside a nested area but is not yet absorbed by it)


#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8121)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://areas-stealing-systems.mural.engineering)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds stealing behavior so nested areas fully containing widgets reparent them during create/drag/resize, plus numeric tolerance in change comparison.

>   - Run absorb/expel iteratively until stable; track and diff affected `widgetIds`.
>   - Refactor to use `ActionBuilder(currentStore)`; flush between steps; only return effective changes.
> - **Absorption Utilities**:

title: Improved barrel handling + subpath support
body:
### Summary

Adds support for packages with [Node.js subpath exports](https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#subpath-exports) (like `@muralco/canvas`) to the `move-to-package` tool. Previously, the tool expected all packages to have a root `src/index.ts` barrel, which doesn't exist for subpath-export packages.

### Changes

#### Barrel Export Handling
- Creates a **chain of barrel exports** from the moved file's directory up to the package root (or subpath boundary)
- For **subpath packages**: chain stops at the matching subpath barrel (e.g., `@muralco/canvas/business`)
- For **traditional packages**: chain continues to `src/index.ts`
- Automatically detects existing exports to avoid duplicates

#### Import Rewriting
- Rewrites imports to the correct subpath (e.g., `@muralco/canvas/business` instead of just `@muralco/canvas`)
- Determines subpath by matching the file's directory against `package.json` exports

#### Code Quality
- Refactored `move-to-package-barrels.ts` with clear section organization and extracted utility functions
- Added 4 test scenarios covering subpath boundary behavior, full barrel chains, deduplication, and import rewrites

### Example

```bash
# Moving a file to a subpath-export package
npx muralco-refactoring-tools move-to-package --from=src/business/helpers.ts --to=packages/canvas/src/business/utils/helpers.ts

# Creates:
# - packages/canvas/src/business/utils/index.ts (exports helpers)
# - Updates packages/canvas/src/business/index.ts (exports ./utils)
# - Rewrites imports to @muralco/canvas/business
```


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds subpath-aware barrel chaining and import rewriting to `move-to-package`, with utilities/refactors and comprehensive tests.
> 
> - **move-to-package barrels**:
>   - Add subpath exports detection from `package.json` and matching logic.
>   - Create barrel chains from file dir up to subpath boundary (or `src/index.ts` for traditional packages).

title: [CAN-8167] Organize into area keep relative stackingOrder of children
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR unifies the calls in `addWidgetsIntoClusterWithoutCheckingForConsistency` into a single `apply`. The order was affecting the system output if widgets were absorbed one by one.

With Multiple Applies
- First apply: sourceWidgetIds = [A] → affectedWidgets = [A] → only A is processed
- Second apply: sourceWidgetIds = [B] → affectedWidgets = [B] → only B is processed (A is not included)
Even though initialStore is the same, the system never sees A and B together, so it can’t sort them relative to each other. Each widget gets assigned a stacking order independently.

With Single Apply
- Single apply: sourceWidgetIds = [A, B, C] → affectedWidgets = [A, B, C] → all widgets are processed together and sorted by their original stacking order from initialStore. The fix is that batching all changes ensures all widgets are in sourceWidgetIds, so they’re all included in affectedWidgets and can be sorted together in one operation.

![pr](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e1bd6ee-723f-43e8-ae14-5d74f96b3943)

Master:

title: [CAN-7922] Enable nesting of free-form areas (absorption system version)
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR enables nesting of free-form areas within other areas, implementing support for parent-child relationships between freeform area widgets **when absorption is handled by a system instead of a business rule.**

The feature is gated behind the `ENABLE_NESTED_AREAS` and `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` feature flags.

Expectation for this work is that free-form areas should now behave as any other absorbable widget while the flags are enabled.

**Note** that [area stealing](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46156) is **NOT** implemented here, that is still a behavior only applicable when absorption is handled by a business rule and will be implemented in a future effort.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷 ️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7922)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://nested-areas-systems.mural.engineering)

title: [CAN-8179] Fix broken UX when right click and dragging with multiple selections
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

While having a multiple selection, right click and dragging in the selection's whitespace (i.e. the empty space between 2 or more selected widgets) was not working properly. Instead of dragging the canvas, it would (1) show the context menu for the canvas and keep it opened while (2) dragging would move the widgets instead of the canvas (without ever dismissing the context menu). 

To solve the dragging widgets instead of the canvas, we now only allow multiple selection dragging through left click and leave right clicks to the right-click-pan processor, however this surfaces an issue with the context menu.

To solve the context menu issue I refactored context menu logic in`src/mural/addons/core/mouse`. The problem was that multiple addons handled the context menu in a different way, some some didn't handle it at all. We now have a single addon that manages when to show the context menu.

title: [CAN-8078] Helpers that use `.every` should not be vacuously true
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This is a small PR that fix some helpers that are doing checks on arrays of widgets (typically around table cells)

From https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/every

> every acts like the "for all" quantifier in mathematics. In particular, for an empty array, it returns true. (It is [vacuously true](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuous_truth) that all elements of the [empty set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empty_set#Properties) satisfy any given condition.)

In these cases, we should ensure that sending `[]` would return false.

title: [CAN-8157] Fix orphaned sibling nested areas during resize
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes a bug reported when resizing a nested area enough to overlap another nested area within the same parent.

**Steps to reproduce:**
- Enable the `ENABLE_NESTED_AREAS` flag
- Make sure that `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag is **off**
- Create an area `A`
- Add two nested areas `B` and `C` inside `A`, one next to the other
- Put some background color on the areas to make the bug more visible
- Send `C` to the bottom (you'll still see it because it's inside `A`)
- Resize `B` enough to overlap `C`

You'll see that `C` disappears after `B` starts overlapping it.

---

The reason this happened is not related to nested areas itself, but rather to how we handle the resizing of areas in general:
When we start resizing an area, we expel everything in it and then, on each step of the resizing, analyze which widgets need to be re-added or re-removed (if they were re-added during a previous resizing step).

Now, when we re-remove a widget, we don't check if removing it means that it should be absorbed by someone else.
Why? Because of how resizing and regular absorption _used to work_ before nested areas.
Since, during a resize, we can only remove widgets that were added while resizing, we know for a fact that those widgets didn't have a different parent before.
Why? Because that would be stealing. The only way a widget that a resizing area is expelling can go to a different parent is if it had that parent before. And if it did, then the resizing area could have never own it in the first place.

Entering nested area stealing...
Since nested areas can steal widgets from a parent area, that assumption is no longer valid. Therefore, everything time we remove a widget during a resize operation we now need to check if it should go somewhere else.

This is exactly what this PR does.

title: [SCQM-1429] Fix discard expanded mind map from existing node
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to this change, expanding a mind map node via the "Create diagram" --> "Mind map" option from the widget toolbar and then discarding was not actually discarding the results *WHEN IT WAS THE FIRST THING YOU DID IN THE MURAL* aka the undo redo stack is empty.  

The issue: if the undo/redo stack is empty, the first time preview mode activates there is no transaction to bookmark so upon discarding there's nowhere to rollback to. 

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1429) to understand the context of this effort.
<!-- - Please see this  🎬 [**demo**]() of the acceptance criteria for the above ticket -->
- 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://ai-expand-mindmap-undo.mural.engineering/) to perform a smoke test. ([all testing envs](https://testing-envs.mural.engineering))
To test:
1. Create a mind map 
2. Clear undo / redo stack
3. Select a node
4. Expand the mind map via widget toolbar "Create diagram" --> "Mind map"
5. Discard the results
6. Verify the changes disappear 

To regression test verify other pathways for creating and expanding a mind map are still solid
1. Via a selected node and "Generate ideas"
2. Via the "Create diagram" in the hub

title: [CAN-8145] Defer area title selection to mouse up when another widget is already selected
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR defers area selection to mouse up when another widget is already selected by returning `false` in `shouldSuppressAndHandleAreaSelection` if the user is doing mouse down on a hint and the area is not selected.

To reproduce the bug:
1. Create an area
2. Add a sticky to that area
3. Select the sticky
4. Hold mouse down on the title of the area 
    - In the PR the area is not selected until the mouse up event
    - In master the area is selected on mouse down and deselected on mouse up

title: [NEXT-256]  Remove `setSdkContextForAmpHelpers`
body:
**[NEXT-256 Remove easy to replace functions from apm, use SDK](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/NEXT-256)**

This PR removes global variable + getter/setter for SDK context. The last call to it was inside of `onUpdateWidgetRequest`. In most cases it was easy to provide SDK, except the case `widget.patch() -> patchAmpWidget() -> onUpdateWidgetRequest() -> debouncedApplyChangesToMural(globalSdk)`. So, moved the call requiring SDK out of `onUpdateWidgetRequest` and call `debouncedApplyChangesToMural` in places where it's needed.

To detect every place where `widget.patch` is called, I added `console.trace` into it, and run tests. Then, parsed the log. There were only these 3 call sources, and all of them in a single function:
```
at updateAmpersandAndEngine (/Users/amonkin/mural/murally/src/mural/sdk/apis/widgets/changes/apply-changes/update-ampersand-and-engine.ts:35:19)
at updateAmpersandAndEngine (/Users/amonkin/mural/murally/src/mural/sdk/apis/widgets/changes/apply-changes/update-ampersand-and-engine.ts:49:13)
at updateAmpersandAndEngine (/Users/amonkin/mural/murally/src/mural/sdk/apis/widgets/changes/apply-changes/update-ampersand-and-engine.ts:48:19)
```

Added `persistChangesDebounced` to `WidgetChangesApiService` to avoid propagating full SDK into widget changes API.

Specified exact used API subsets when needed instead of using full SDK.

## Overview

title: [CAN-8120] Allow nested areas to "steal" widgets from its parent
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR implements the concept of "stealing" for nested areas.

Whenever an area enters another, and becomes a child of the latter, if the final position of the nested area is fully containing children of the parenting cluster, it now has the ability to "steal" them from it.

This means that any widget inside an area will become child of any nested area that is added to the bigger cluster:

![Nov-19-2025 08-46-49](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87bd60b5-594a-44fa-b378-abbf2d532e3b)

This should work for all the cases where nesting can occur:
- Dragging an area inside another
- Dragging an already nested area
- Resizing an already nested area 
- Dragging an area from the sidebar onto another
- Pasting an area inside another
- Adding a nested area via the context menu
- Duplicating an area onto another
- Clicking "Absorb" from the toolbar of a nested area (this one is hard to test because you'd have to force a situation where a widget is inside a nested area but is not yet absorbed by it)

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-8120)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://nested-areas-stealing.mural.engineering)

- Removed the deprecated `getIsAuthenticated` prop from `UsupportedVersion` component in favor of directly calling `isAuthenticated()`

- Fixed test patterns and expectations to align with the new authentication flow.

title: [CAN-7998] Hide Widget Tools Instead of Disabling for Improved UX
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
## Overview

This PR migrates top-level tools in the `WIDGET_FLOATING` toolbar from using `disabled` conditions to `visible` conditions. Instead of showing tools as disabled, tools are now hidden when they're not applicable, providing a cleaner user experience by reducing visual clutter.

## Tools Updated

The following tools have been migrated to use visibility instead of disabled state:

1. **Align Widgets** (`align-widgets`)
2. **Arrange Widgets** (`arrange-widgets`)
3. **Caption Toggle** (`caption-toggle-tool`)
4. **Crop Photo** (`crop-photo-tool`)
5. **Drag Tool** (`drag-tool`)
6. **Filter by Type** (`filter-by-type-tool`)
7. **Resize Tool** (`resize-tool`)
8. **Zoom to Selection** (`zoom-to-selection`)
9. **Mindmap Layout Horizontal** (`mindmaps-layout-horizontal`)
10. **Mindmap Layout Vertical** (`mindmaps-layout-vertical`)

## Tools Not Covered in This PR

The following tools are **not** included in this PR as they will be moved to the fixed toolbar in a future update:

- **Border Width** (`border-width`)
- **Border Style** (`border-style-toggle-tool`)
- **Stroke Width** (`stroke-width`) - Note: Currently hardcoded to `disabled: false`
- **Decrease Font** (`decrease-font`)
- **Increase Font** (`increase-font`)

## AI Tool Exclusion

The **AI Dropdown Tool** (`ai-dropdown-tool`) is not covered in this PR and will be delivered separately.

## Changes

- Removed `disabled` property from tool specs
- Combined disabled logic into visibility conditions
- Updated tests to check visibility instead of disabled state
- Updated tools-api documentation to reflect the preference for visibility over disabled state

## Benefits

- **Cleaner UI**: Reduces visual clutter by hiding unavailable tools
- **Better UX**: Users only see tools that are actionable
- **Consistent Pattern**: Aligns with the established pattern for top-level tools in `WIDGET_FLOATING` toolbar

title: [CAN-8108] Exclude affected widgets from stacking order lookup
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When the stacking order system gets triggered by a change in parenting we look for the highest available stacking order to assign it to the affected widget.

However, if this higher value is in the widget itself, we still increase the value creating an unnecessary gap.

In this PR this situation is addressed so affected widgets are not included in the lookup.

### How to test this?
1. Enable the `ENABLE_STACKING_ORDER_SYSTEM` flag
2. Create an area
3. Add a sticky in the canvas
4. Make not of the sticky's stacking order
  a. Given that the sticky is the last widget created, this should be the highest stacking order in the mural
5. Drag or resize the area to contain the sticky
6. Check that the stacking order of the sticky **did not change**

title: [CAN-7917] Fix resizing an area issue where it would absorb a connector unintentionally
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

- Connector absorption test now covers the “expand over arrow, shrink back in one drag” scenario and asserts the arrow gets de-parented.

- _getAllRelatedArrowIds_ includes descendant arrows; _isArrowAbsorptionAffectingOperation_ stays active when any related arrow’s parent changes.

### Case Solved

Perviously when resizing a free-form area across an adjacent arrow and then returning to the original bounds (without releasing the mouse) left the arrow parented to the area, even though the border no longer contained it. The connector absorption system stopped running as soon as the area’s width/height matched the initial values, so _findNextParentId_ never re-ran to return null, and _updateArrowParent_ never emitted _removeParent_.

### How the Change Fixes It

Arrow/connector parenting changes are now treated as an affecting operation. Whenever an area gains or loses arrow children—either via intersections, direct connections, or existing absorbed descendants—we keep the connector absorption system active until every related arrow’s parent matches the pre-resize state. 

The function _getAllRelatedArrowIds_ was extended to include descendant arrows so connectors already absorbed continue to be reevaluated, and _isArrowAbsorptionAffectingOperation_ watches those IDs for parent changes even if the area’s size snaps back to its original dimensions mid-drag. 

The regression test in _connectorAbsorptionSystem_ reproduces the exact drag scenario (grow width over the arrow, shrink back before release) and now asserts that the arrow parent is cleared.

## DOMPurify Version Update: 3.2.5 → 3.3.0

### Overview
This PR addresses feedback from [PR #46095](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/46095) by providing comprehensive documentation for the dompurify dependency update.

### Changelog & Release Information
- **Release Date**: October 13, 2025

1. **SVG mask-type attribute allowed** - The SVG `mask-type` attribute is now included in the default allow-list

**Security Considerations**:
- Resolves CVE-2025-48050 (path traversal in development script, not production-impacting)

title: [stop-presentation] set mode bug fix
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, when presentation was stopped, we always assumed we should set the mode to 'edit'. This was incorrectly assumed to be the previous mode in all cases.

Now, with these changes, we utilize the outermost closure of the dispatcher createApi function to store a reference to the previousMode. We initialize this and then reset it on start(). Then when its time to end, we revert the mode back to what it was prior to the presentation starting.

NOTE: this bug was introduced by the desire to increase the visibility of the "Present" button. Our guiding principle, from a product perspective, was to only hide the "present" button in the side bar when a presentation was active. This is a signficant and intentional UX change. We keep this UX in this fix to maintain adherence to this principle.

title: [CAN-7699] Enabled thumbnailURLs to propagate into photoURLs when editing link photoWidgets.
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Enabled thumbnailURLs to propagate into photoURLs when editing link photoWidgets. This allows a image of a photoWidget to change after editing its thumbnail.

### Case Solved

Previously, when a user pasted a link on the canvas and later manually changed the thumbnail image for that link widget, the new image would not appear on the canvas.
This issue occurred because link widgets render their thumbnail image from the photoURL property, but manual thumbnail edits were only updating the thumbURL field. As a result, the UI continued to display the old photoURL image instead of the newly entered thumbnail.

### How the Change Fixes It

The fix ensures that when a thumbnail is manually changed for a link widget, the new thumbnail URL is validated and then propagated to the photoURL field as well.

Specifically:

When setThumb() is called, the widget’s thumbURL is updated as before.

If the widget is a link(specific use case asked for the ticket) and the new thumbnail URL is valid, the same value is also applied to photoURL.

This ensures that the renderer, which relies on photoURL, immediately reflects the updated thumbnail image.

Invalid URLs are safely ignored to prevent breaking existing images.

#### Reviewer Resources
[**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7699)

title: [CAN-8110] Fix paste content with background styles into lexical
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes a bug where pasted HTML content with transparent background colors (such as content copied from Google Docs) resulted in text nodes with black backgrounds in the lexical editor (see video)
 

## Problem

We received a report that text copied from Google Docs into the lexical editor appeared with a black background. This issue was introduced in [PR #45652](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45652).

The problem occurred due to two reasons:

1. **Background color application**: When we added `<mark>` element support, we started setting the `background-color` style in `applyFormatToTextNode` . However, background colors are not supported for text content outside of mark elements in Mural (background colors apply to the widget background, not the text).

2. **Transparent color parsing**: The `convertColorToHex` function didn't handle named colors like `'transparent'`, which caused it to default to `#000000` (black) when parsing transparent background colors.

## Solution

Since we are not supporting background colors for text content outside of mark elements yet, this PR rolls back the change in `applyFormatToTextNode` to only support `color` (not `backgroundColor`).

The second issue (parsing transparent background colors) is no longer a problem for non-mark elements since we now ignore background colors entirely.

## Note on Mark Elements
Mark elements are unaffected by this change. They use a separate `highlightColor` property in Lexical's `MuralTextNodes` (not the `background-color` style), so they continue to work correctly.

Mark elements without a `background-color` attribute or with named colors will default to `#000000`. This is intentional—we do not parse HTML for mark elements, as they were designed to work with explicit background and color values. This basic implementation enables BSH to import their Miro boards to Mural.

title: [CAN-8111] Fix stacking order on area resize when stacking order system is enabled
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

There was a bug where, when an area was resized and absorbed widgets, on resize end the stacking order received an extra unnecessary update. During onResize, widgets were absorbed when they overlapped the area, and the stacking order system ran correctly using the stage's initialStore (from resize start). However, onResizeEnd called addWidgetsIntoClusterWithoutCheckingForConsistency, which set the parent again for widgets that already had it set.

title: Refactoring Tools : Add support for alias paths in move-to-package utility
body:
## Pull Request Overview

This PR adds support for rewriting aliased imports (e.g., `common/with-state`) to package imports when moving files from `src/` to packages. The move-to-package refactoring tool now resolves both relative imports and webpack alias-based imports.

Key changes:
- Adds alias resolution functionality to detect and rewrite webpack-configured path aliases
- Extends import rewriting logic to handle both relative and aliased imports
- Adds comprehensive test coverage for alias resolution and import rewriting scenarios

### Reviewed Changes

Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `packages/refactoring-tools/src/lib/aliases/loadAliases.ts` | Loads and parses webpack alias configuration from `webpack.common.js` |
| `packages/refactoring-tools/src/lib/aliases/resolveAliasImport.ts` | Resolves aliased import specifiers to absolute file paths |
| `packages/refactoring-tools/src/lib/aliases/index.ts` | Exports alias utilities |
| `packages/refactoring-tools/src/lib/aliases/loadAliases.test.ts` | Tests for alias loading functionality |
| `packages/refactoring-tools/src/lib/aliases/resolveAliasImport.test.ts` | Tests for alias resolution |
| `packages/refactoring-tools/src/tasks/move-to-package/move-to-package-imports.ts` | Updates import rewriting to support aliased imports |
| `packages/refactoring-tools/src/tasks/move-to-package/move-to-package.test.ts` | Adds integration tests for aliased import rewriting |
</details>

title: [SCQM-1437] - Fix ai-summarize preview mode undo bug
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Currently after accepting preview mode results for `ai-summarize`, there is an additional step added to the undo/redo stack for the creation of the placeholder widget used in preview mode streaming - this leads to a bug with undo/redo not working as expected and only partially undoing/redoing results.

This fixes the issue by adding a helper to create the placeholder widget using `ActionBuilder` and `.apply` instead of `addWidgets` (which creates its own undo/redo step), in order to stage the creation along with the rest of the preview mode changes until the final commit on accepting preview mode.

The fix applies to both legacy/chat and the new AiActions modes.

title: [CAN-8082] Allow expulsed widgets to be absorbed by other absorbing widgets when resizing
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When we do a resize operation that could cause an indirect expulsion of absorbable widgets from their parents (such as when we resize an area short enough to expel one of its children), we don’t do any checking to see if there’s another absorbing widget suitable to absorb the now orphan widget.

The expected behavior is that if there’s a second absorbing widget capable of getting the expelled absorbable one, it should take it.

This is something that only happens when the absorption systems flag is off so the solution is implemented for that case only.

title: [CAN-8099] Unify absorption systems into a single entry point
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

In order to achieve consistency in the way absorption logic works as a system and to have both a better control of the implications of running it as well as a more performant behavior (by gathering all the required information only once for all the related systems), we need to unify all the current different systems that apply some logic related to the absorption of widgets into one sole entry point.

This work will then be iterated to improve the experience but the initial point here is to have all systems in one place while keeping their individual behaviors (as well as their individual control flags)

To achieve this I'm introducing the concept of a "state dependent system" which is a way of gathering one or many systems that depend on one or more feature flags (independently) to be enabled.

This will allow us to have partial behaviors moved into systems in a controlled way while still having it all be "one" absorption system to the external caller.

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This pull request adds the timer tool for private mode's fixed toolbar and refactors existing timer tools.

This pull request refactors and simplifies the timer tools in the Mural application, removing legacy experiment flags and introducing a unified approach for timer tool variants. The changes improve maintainability by centralizing shared logic, cleaning up feature flag usage, and making timer variant selection explicit. Additionally, the code now supports different timer button styles based on context and feature flags.

title: [CAN-8081] Send system modified ids along to other systems
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors the `System` type interface to clarify the distinction between user-initiated changes and system-generated changes. 
In order to achieve that, the parameter `widgetIds` (representing the first set) has been renamed to `sourceWidgetIds`, and the added set has been named `changedWidgetIds`.

The new parameter is only used when needed, and while its mandatory as part of the payload object, the systems implementation can deconstruct this object and only use it if needed.

The motivation behind this changes is allowing the `stackingOrder` system, who acts over widgets changing parent, to fetch those that had the parent changed by another system without needing to perform duplicated calculation.

title: [CAN-8069] Fix areas improvements
body:
# Area Selection Behavior Update

When clicking empty space in an area with children, the area should be selected on **mouseup** via the deferred selection mechanism.  
Previously, `pendingAreaSelection` was being cleared too aggressively for all empty-space clicks in mouse mode, preventing selection.

Now, pending selection is only cleared when there's a **different pre-existing selection** (to allow canvas panning), preserving it for normal clicks to be committed on mouseup.

This **fixes the scenario** where clicking an unselected area with children did not select the area.

---

## What to Test

### Click Behavior

#### Locked Areas

##### With Children
- [ ] Hint → Selects area  
- [ ] Empty space → Selects area (nothing happens)

##### Empty
- [ ] Hint → Selects area  
- [ ] Empty space → Selects area (nothing happens)

#### Unlocked Areas

##### With Children
- [ ] Hint → Selects area  
- [ ] Empty space → Selects area (nothing happens)

##### Empty
- [ ] Hint → Selects area  
- [ ] Empty space → Selects area

---

### Drag Behavior (Mouse Down + Movement)

#### Locked Areas

##### With Children
- [ ] Hint → Start panning (should also select area)  
- [ ] Empty space → Start panning  

##### Empty
- [ ] Hint → Start panning (should also select the area, but it tries to drag the area instead)  
- [ ] Empty space → Start panning (should also select the area)

#### Unlocked Areas

##### With Children
- [ ] Hint → Start dragging the area  
- [ ] Empty space → Start panning  

##### Empty
- [ ] Hint → Start dragging the area  
- [ ] Empty space → Start dragging the area

---

title: Refactoring Tools : Move to Package Utility
body:
# Move to Package Utility

Adds a new `move-to-package` command to the refactoring tools that automates the process of moving files from `src/` into packages while properly handling exports and import rewrites. The goal of this utility is to automate moving and updating imports for files that are ready to be modularized.

Files with 0 external dependencies you can test the utility with: 
- `src/common/with-state.tsx`, limited imports (~3 - 5)
- `src/common/types.ts`, large number of imports (80+)

## What It Does

The utility performs the following operations:

- **Moves files** from `src/...` to `packages/<pkg>/src/...` using `git mv` (with filesystem fallback for untracked files)
- **Updates barrel exports** - automatically creates/updates directory-level and package-level barrel files (`src/index.ts`) to export the moved file
- **Rewrites imports** throughout the codebase - changes all relative imports pointing to the moved file to use package imports (`@muralco/<pkg>`)
- **Cleans up empty barrel files** left in the source directory if they only re-exported the moved file
- **Supports dry-run mode** (default) - preview all changes as JSON before applying

## Usage

```bash
# Dry-run (default) - preview changes as JSON
npx muralco-refactoring-tools move-to-package \
  --from=src/common/utils/helper.ts \
  --to=packages/utils/src/common/helper.ts

# Apply changes
npx muralco-refactoring-tools move-to-package \
  --from=src/common/utils/helper.ts \
  --to=packages/utils/src/common/helper.ts \
  --write

# Use directory path (filename preserved automatically)
npx muralco-refactoring-tools move-to-package \
  --from=src/common/utils/helper.ts \
  --to=packages/utils/src/common/ \
  --write

# Create commit after applying changes
npx muralco-refactoring-tools move-to-package \
  --from=src/common/utils/helper.ts \
  --to=packages/utils/src/common/helper.ts \
  --write \
  --commit
```

title: [CAN-8065] Remove call to `widgets.update` when changing stacking order
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
In our entire codebase there's only place that is changing the `stackingOrder` of widgets using the deprecated method `sdk.widgets.update` instead of the new `Widget Changes` API, and that is the business rule `changeStackingOrder`.

Luckily for us, that business rule has only one caller: another business rule called `ungroupSelectedWidgets` which, as the name suggests, handles... well, you probably got it by now.

This PR moves the logic of `changeStackingOrder` inside `ungroupSelectedWidgets` and then refactors it to use the `Widget Changes` API for all its updates.

While there's a change in logic along this (we'll have systems running now that we haven't had before), we should not expect any particular change in behavior, with one exception:

Arrows that get ungrouped inside an area were previously getting manually attached to it via `update`. That goes completely against our intended behavior for arrows and areas, which is that they should get absorbed if they're fully contained inside.
By removing that manual fix and using the `Widget Changes` API, we now get the consist behavior we should have had.

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [SCQM-1332] Prevent accept / discard when no preview mode data exists
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Currently there are some preview mode accept & discard events getting tracked that do not have an ai feature `type` in them (see the query in the ticket)

This happens when accept / discard is run but `currentPreviewMode` `data` is completely empty - which is the default state that gets reset when preview mode *ends*. So I'm using that as a gate - you shouldn't be able to accept / discard when there is no preview mode data available. 

As for *how* this is happening.... the only tangible example of this I can reproduce is if `previewMode.accept()` or `previewMode.discard()` get run **twice** for a set of changes ( accept called, which clears state, accept called again now with empty state) - which did used to happen in some of the [callbacks](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45370/commits/15c91af7e855e0bc738e748e6976abc5e7090546). But I couldn't find any other ways this could still be happening so possibly a race condition somewhere.

body:
## Update UI Toolkit: Improved Menu + Modal Focus Management & ARIA Support

This PR updates `@muraldevkit/ui-toolkit` from v4.52.3 to v4.52.4, bringing enhanced accessibility features and improved focus management.

The changes fix an underlying issue where a keyboard user loses focus if they open a modal from a menu and then close the menu. With these changes focus will be returned back to the menu trigger when the modal is dismissed instead of becoming lost. 

### Key Changes

**Accessibility Improvements:**
- Added `ariaHasPopup` support for menu items that trigger dialogs/modals
- Enhanced ARIA role support with `MenuItemRole` type for better screen reader compatibility
- Improved modal user experience and focus management based on `aria-haspopup` attribute

**Updated Components:**
- **Menu Items**: Added `ariaHasPopup` and `role` props to action definitions across dashboard & canvas
- **Tool Registration**: Updated tool API to support new accessibility attributes
- **Universal Card & Rooms & Template Actions**: Updated Actions API to support new values

Test env: http://update-uik-modal-focus.mural.engineering

How to test: 
- navigate to a menu using your keyboard (try the mural actions, room actions, or mural options menu on the canvas)
- open menu item that triggers a modal
- dismiss modal
- notice focus moves back to the menu trigger

title: [CAN-8055] Fix copied HTML content from lexical
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

## 🧩 Summary of Changes

Previously, copying and pasting a **partial selection** from the Lexical editor — especially selections containing a line break — could produce **duplicated text**.

This update fixes that issue: copying and pasting now works correctly, without duplication.

---

## 💡 Context

This regression was introduced when we enhanced the editor to support **`<mark>` elements**.
At that time, we began storing a **richer HTML representation** of copied content in the clipboard using our **custom HTML serializer**.

However, when copying only part of the document:

* `selection.getNodes()` returns a **flat, “dirty” list** of nodes — not a full Lexical document.
* Some nodes can appear **duplicated** in this list.
* Our `serializeNodes` method expects a **clean, complete document**, not an arbitrary or repeated subset of nodes.

As a result, the serializer couldn’t properly handle partial selections.

---

## 🔧 Fix

Instead of serializing the selection directly:

1. The Lexical JSON already stored in the clipboard is parsed.
2. This produces a **clean, complete node structure**.
3. That structure is then converted to HTML using **Lexical’s built-in serialization logic**.

This approach:

* Eliminates duplication in partial selections.
* Leverages Lexical’s **native serialization pipeline** for consistency.
* Adds only minimal overhead from parsing the JSON data.

---

## ✅ Outcome

* Copying and pasting **partial or multi-line selections** now works correctly.
* The implementation is **more robust**, **consistent**, and **aligned with Lexical’s intended API usage**.

body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR adds a new reset functionality to the entries in the Flags Manager: This `Reset` button will remove the entry from the local storage and restore the flag to the original value retrieved from the server. The button only appears on values from the Flags Manager that have been manually modified by the user, so those entries without it represent values straight from the back-end. Another related change is added here as well: given that we can now reset entries manually, there's no need to specify whether we want local storage or not. We store everything locally by default and if we don't want something to be there, we simply reset its value. ![Oct-29-2025 13-05-28](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c51ed4dc-8302-492f-aed5-70c0e3be214c) Because of this immediacy, the `Save` button on the window is no longer operative, the changes are now saved immediately as we set them: ![Oct-29-2025 13-04-03](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1eef3fad-b294-46d3-98ad-a76e60f6c196) #### Reviewer Resources - 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7973) - 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://flags-manager-reset.mural.engineering)

title: [SCQM-1256] Fix remove planner column undo
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Prior to these changes, a single undo request after deleting a smart planner column resulted in a broken planner.

I believe this was due to the CE undo step being attached to the remove column planner transaction, which contained a call to `deleteWidgets` which had its own separate transactions and therefore breaking on "redo" by not redoing these in one transaction. By handling the deletion of the widgets ourselves, all the changes can be associated with the same transaction.

Extra note: In the original PR, I pointed out a bug that prevented _redoing_ the _undo_ (removing the column again) that was a larger issue. With this PR, you can now undo then redo successfully... but you encounter similar bugs / a bad state if you try to undo repeatedly further back so there's still something questionable happening with the planner's undo / redo stack - I adjusted that ticket to reflect this. 

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [ENGAGE-1391] Dashboard: Remove last use of app.me. Load user directly from api
body:
### Change:
Completely remove app.me ampersand user from dashboard.

### Details:
* DashboardContainer
  * PRIMARY CHANGE
  * no longer uses ampersand and `app.me` to fetch the signed-in user.
  * the new logic to verify the user is signed-in and loaded from api is now in `RequireAuth`
  * RequireAuth will check for an existing session, refresh it if it can, call onMissionSession (ie redirectToSignIn) if needed, then load the user from api/v0/me.
* DashboardWrapper
  * now takes in a defined `User` as prop
  * this allows for old test rig v1 test pages to use DashboardWrapper directly instead of an intermediate component DashboardContainerRaw
  * once the rig v1 tests are all migrated, DashbaordWrapper can delete the `user` prop and instead get the authenticatedUser directly from useAuthenticatedUser().
* RequireAuth
  * now handles scenario where `session` isn't defined (ie. user isn't logged in)
  * new prop `onMissingSession()` callback is called when no session can be found.
  * this allows the calling code (DashboardContainer) to redirect the user to the sign-in page
* DasbhardUserStore
  * deleted
  * no longer used
  * it was added as a stop-gap to convert the app.me AmpUserModel to a api/User object.

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR creates a system, flagged by `ENABLE_STACKING_ORDER_SYSTEM`, to manage stacking orders in parent changes (absorption/expulsion). It ensures consistent order when widgets move between parents and preserves relative ordering across multiple changes.

1. If a widget is absorbed or expelled, it's new stacking order will be the highest in the mural + 1
2. If a widget is absorbed or expelled, and then back in the same parent as the initial drag, the stacking order remains the same.

title: [CAN-7872] Move table cell pasting logic out of `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` - Part 2
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This is one work split into two PRs for cleanliness and to facilitate the review.
You're currently viewing at part 2: **forcing the table cell parenting after the dropping**.

---

The main goal of this effort is to remove, from `dropWidgetsOnCanvas`, specific logic regarding pasting elements over a table cell.

The expected behavior when this happens is to find the center point of the pasted elements boundaries and, if it overlaps a table cell whose table is set to auto resize, make the cell big enough to contain everything and force all widgets to go there.

We want all this behavior to be coded outside of `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` to get a clear separation of responsibilities and to lead the way into making absorption a system.

The logic for this behavior resides in the helper `tryDropPastedWidgetsIntoTableCell`, and the goal is to move it away from the business rule. 

The wsy we'll achieve this is by moving the checking to the code that handles widget pasting (which is the action that triggers this behavior) after the widgets have been dropped into the canvas.
This means that if there was a regular absorption happening it will still occur, but if the content suggests that a table cell should parent those widget, we'll disregard the absorption and force that situation afterwards.

--- 

**Note**: There is room for further improvement here by extracting common behavior such as finding the potential table cell.

title: [CAN-7957] User nav controls A/B Experiment
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR adds a new addon to run a user A/B test composed of 3 variants:
- Control: No changes.
- Variant 1: New controls selection modal
- Variant 2: New controls selection modal + New buttons in sidebar

Short loom explaining the different variants: https://www.loom.com/share/8c04c466e7934c788702417df0245ae4

In order to achieve the required changes for the A/B test I introduced a few new features:
- Enhanced SDK's Experiments API to enable AB test data
persistence and cross-component access (Variant 2 introduces a slight change on our business rules, we no longer disable mural tools while in Move or Pan mode.)
- Sidebar button's 'order' prop: Before this change all sidebar buttons were shown in their registration order, or where manually placed as the Templates button does). Now we sort buttons by order property, with unordered buttons appearing after ordered ones
- Sidebar buttons are now using the controlledState prop, previously the state was controlled by the button itself, resulting in unexpected behaviour: Even if you had set the state to be selected based on external state (e.g. appMode is 'pan', simply clicking the button again would result in the button being unselected)

Last but not least, we need to run the experiment code AFTER the Templates modal is shown when creating a new mural, so I had to make a small modification to the `onCloseModal` function on said modal, this should be removed once the experiment is finished (About 2 weeks after this PR is merged). I created https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7957 to clean up this and the business rules changes.

title: [CAN-8023] Move table cell pasting logic out of `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` - Part 1
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This is one work split into two PRs for cleanliness and to facilitate the review.
You're currently viewing at part 1: **offsetting widgets pasted close to a table cell's border**.

---

The main goal of this effort is to remove, from `dropWidgetsOnCanvas`, specific logic regarding pasting elements over a table cell.

The expected behavior when this happens is to find the center point of the pasted elements boundaries and, if it overlaps a table cell whose table is set to auto resize, make the cell big enough to contain everything and force all widgets to go there.
Added to that, if the top left border of the boundaries falls outside the top left border of the cell, we want to offset the pasted elements so they fully fall inside of it.
**This last part is what this PR is all about.**

We want all this behavior to be coded outside of `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` to get a clear separation of responsibilities and to lead the way into making absorption a system.

The logic for this behavior resides in the helper `tryDropPastedWidgetsIntoTableCell`, and the goal is to move it away from the business rule. 

In this first PR we're moving the part that offsets the pasted widgets to do the exact same thing _before_ doing the pasting instead of afterwards.
This means that, instead of pasting them under the cursor and then moving them, we first figure out _where they would be pasted_ and if it overlaps a table cell, we offset them beforehand, so once we create the elements, they're in their final position.
The logic regarding forcing them onto a cell will be addressed in the next PR.

title: [CAN-7990] Reorder paste handlers to eliminate duplicate editor checks
body:
## Summary

The paste handlers were duplicating the check for an active editor. By re-ordering the handlers, we can use a single paste handler to check if the editor is mounted and stop the execution of the other ones. This optimization was already in place but needed to be re-ordered for better efficiency.

## Changes

### Refactored
- **Reordered paste handler chain** in `src/mural/addons/core/paste-handlers/index.tsx`
  - Moved `forward-paste-to-editables` handler to the end of the chain
  - Eliminated duplicate editor state checks across multiple handlers

### Implementation Details

The reordering ensures that:
1. Specialized handlers (like `muralRender`) process their specific data types first
2. The `forward-paste-to-editables` handler acts as a final gatekeeper
3. When an editor is active (`targetEditable: true`), the handler immediately returns `{ handled: true }` and prevents other handlers from executing
4. This eliminates redundant editor checks that were previously scattered across multiple handlers
