title: Improve RoomMock type safety with derived types
body:
## Summary

This PR improves type safety in the RoomMock class by replacing basic types with derived types from the Room interface.

## Changes

- **Type Safety**: Replace basic types (, , etc.) with indexed access types from  interface
- **Interface Compliance**: Add explicit property declarations to  class to properly implement  interface
- **Flexible Parameters**: Create  type for workspace parameter that allows additional Workspace properties
- **Method Signatures**: Update method parameters and return types to use derived types
- **Code Quality**: Fix ESLint naming convention violations and add missing return type annotations

## Key Architectural Change:  vs 

**Before**: The class used  which created inheritance
**After**: The class now uses  which creates a contract

According to the [TypeScript documentation](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/classes.html#implements-clauses), the  clause is used to verify that a class satisfies a particular interface. This is different from  which creates inheritance relationships.

### Why  is Better Here:

1. **Contract-Based**:  ensures the class conforms to the  interface without inheriting behavior
2. **Type Safety**: TypeScript will enforce that all required properties and methods are present
3. **Explicit Declaration**: Forces us to explicitly declare all properties, making the interface contract visible
4. **No Inheritance Overhead**: Avoids potential issues with prototype chain inheritance
5. **Clear Intent**: Makes it obvious that this is a mock implementation of the  interface

## Benefits

- **Type Consistency**: All types now derive from the same source of truth (Room interface)
- **Maintainability**: Changes to Room interface automatically propagate to RoomMock
- **Type Safety**: Prevents type drift between interface and implementation
- **Developer Experience**: Better IntelliSense and compile-time error detection

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When updating a mural member's edit permissions (from both the mural members view and the mural member card on canvas), the member's permissions are sanitized before being sent to the `PATCH /api/v0/mural/:muralId/members` endpoint to prevent `400 Bad Request` responses from occurring (e.g., if the mural member is a guest with a permission like `duplicate` enabled, the `PATCH` request would fail even if that field wasn't being updated).

title: [CAN-7919] Allow absorption while dragging for absorption system
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR implements the following new behavior when dragging one or more free-form areas:
- When the free-form area hovers over any absorbable widget, overlapping it past its threshold, the absorption feedback is shown both on the widget as well as on the free-form area (filled rectangle over the widget, blue border over the area).
At this point, the widget is shown as “potentially absorbed” by the free-form area, but it's not being moved with the area while it’s still dragging.
- After the area is dropped, if the widget is still contained within the area, it gets absorbed by it following the regular absorption behaviors.
- This logic is only enabled when both the `ENABLE_ABSORB_ON_AREA_DRAGGING` and the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag are **on**

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7919)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://absorb-while-dragging-for-s.mural.engineering)

### How to test this?

- Enable the `ENABLE_ABSORB_ON_AREA_DRAGGING` flag
- Enable the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag
- Create an area and a sticky (or any other absorbable widget)
- Drag the area over the sticky
  - While you're dragging it, you should see the feedback on both the area and the sticky
- Drop the area over the sticky
  - The sticky should be absorbed by the area
- Alternatively: duplicate the area using ALT+drag
- Drop the duplicated area over the sticky
  - The sticky should be absorbed by the duplicated area

Prior to these changes, when adding a profile widget via paste, the placeholder widget -- added to the "stage" of changes to be sent to the API -- was prematurely sent to the API due to some tech-debt in which a call to `sdk.widgets.update` was made. title: [SCQM-1384] Add AI Action Summarize refine menu
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR reintroduces the Refine Menu UI and adds the implementation for the new Summarize AIAction.
I say "reintroduce" and I mean it, because this menu system existed in previous AI iterations but never made it to the final product. The good thing is that the code was preserved and we can now easily add it again.

This PR can be easily followed by commits:
- Moved the Refine Menu code outside of the addons folder to where the preview mode toolbar now resides.
- Created a new `PreviewModeData` for the Summarize AIAction so it no longer shares the same logic as the current summary implementation. This meant shifting some code around for ease of use.
- Add the `RefineMenu` component back into the Preview Mode toolbar, and made the chat button visibility optional (defaulting to `true` to keep backwards compatibility with current AI features).
- Remove the old AI Clustering `RefineMenu` specs that have been unused since forever. We only kept this as reference for when the time of adding the feature again would come, and this is the time.
- Remove the `previousSummary` property since the new solution retains the context and no longer needs this.
- Add refinement rounds limit. Which required adding more customization options to the `RefineMenu` specs.
- Add basic cucumber tests, based on the legacy ones that used the old rig.

**NOTE**: While working on the tests I realized that our current streaming implementation does a poor job of handling placeholder widgets when undoing. Since this is also happening in the current production implementation, I decided to create a separate ticket to fix this in the future. (hence some oddities in the current tests)

title: [CAN-7965] Remove flag `keepStackingOrder` on widget adding
body:
## Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The business rule `addWidgets` has an option called `keepStackingOrder`.

When set to `false` we calculate a stacking order based on the max value set to the mural.

However, when set to `true` we skip this calculation and use the value already set in the provided model.

To achieve consistency in the usage of this property we need to unify this behavior.

Given that the intention is to have a system do this calculation, we need to avoid the cases where we’re setting an explicit value (unless the intention is to set an explicit value, such as when we move a widget to the front).

This means that we need to remove this option and prevent the possibility of setting a stacking order upon creation.

This PR does precisely that, by refactoring all existing use case to work seamlessly under the new conditions.

You'll find more details about what has been affected here below.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7965)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://keep-stacking-order.mural.engineering)

## What changed

The following behaviors were directly affected by this change.

### Unaltered behavior
These behaviors were refactored in their implementation but their behavior was not modified at all:

#### Drawing connectors:
When we draw a connector, we expect it to be always on top. 
The original code would find the max available value, set it and force it to be kept.
This new code does not make any assumption and let the regular code run, which coincidentally does the exact same thing.

#### Grouping widgets
When we group 2 or more widgets we want the stacking order of the group to match the highest value from its members.
The original code would calculate the value, set it on the `GroupWidget` to be and force it to be kept.
This new code does the same calculation, but creates the widget with no particular specification and does an update

title: [SCQM-99] Use `withFeatures` to determine delete activities triggered by AI, not user
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

**Historical context**: 
`withFeatures` was added for backend tracking a few months ago to track events that ai could trigger on the user's behalf like deleting widgets or starting voting sessions. The goal was to make it generic so that it's extensible to any "features" that take action on the user's behalf. Right now it is only ever a string 'ai' but in the future it could be 'someOtherIntegration' or a delimited list containing multiple features that worked together like 'ai | jira'.

**For this ticket**: 
Adding withFeatures to an ActivitySummary so that on the front end in the Activity Log ui, we know when AI has deleted a widget. "Alyssa deleted a sticky with AI"

**For the future**: 
Since we're going to be hiding many ai capabilities beyond widget updates, none of this is in the immediate future....
By adding this field directly to an activity summary it is very easy to extend this to other actions that the AI can currently trigger but isn't getting credit for in the activity log. So long as the action utilizes the withFeatures for tracking, it should be straight forward to display them as ai triggered in the activity log. For example, if we want voting sessions triggered by AI to be noted in the Activity Log, all we'll have to do is add op.withFeatures [here](https://github.com/tactivos/mural-api/blob/add/with-features-to-activity-summary/api/src/core/dispatcher/handlers/start-voting-session.ts#L16).

title: [CAN-7823] Click + drag areas improvements
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR implements the new area selection logic that determines when to start marquee selection vs drag the container, based on the area's state and content.
- Empty areas: Drag container (no marquee)
- Areas with content: Start marquee in empty space
- Zoomed areas (borders outside viewport): Always start marquee regardless of content
- Locked areas: Always start marquee anywhere in the area
- Behavior Details:
   - Empty areas without children → drag container
   - Areas with children → marquee selection in empty space
   - Areas zoomed so borders are outside viewport → always marquee (even if empty)

title: [bug][profile-widget][placeholder] restore apply() for placeholder creation
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, we were adding the profile widget to the mural directly using the engine. The benefit of this approach was that it allowed us to ensure that the activity log captures the final version of the widget, not the placeholder version, when it takes a snapshot of the "create-widget" event.

However, the drawback for this was that we no longer benefited from the UX consistencies which occur when adding a widget to the canvas using ` apply()`. For example, updating the stacking order when a widget is added in the same coordinate space as an existing widget. We correctly assume this new widget was added "on top" of the existing widget.

So now, with these changes, we restore the call to apply() when adding a placeholder widget. This re-introduces the bug associated with the activity log, (https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/PLAY-467) but it is a preferable problem to having a placeholder widget which has the wrong stacking order.

title: [ENGAGE-1327] WorkspaceSettings: block changes to Join settings for all users (even globalAdmin)
body:
### Bug:
globalAdmin users were able to change the `discoverable` setting on workspaces that are configured as a company's default workspace.
Default workspaces need `discoverable=auto` to ensure that new users can actually join the workspace and start using the product immediately.

### Fix:
Calculate `defaultWorkspaceEnforcedByCompany` based on the workspace's company.defaultWorkspaceId, not by checking the user's companyDefaultWorkspaceId.

This should have no affect on users, but will prevent Mural globalAdmins from being able to update the Join settings for default workspaces.
The company can still configure a different workspace (or none) and then the workspace's Join settings can be updated again.

title: [CAN-7918] Allow absorption while dragging free-form areas
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR implements the following new behavior when dragging one or more free-form areas:
- When the free-form area hovers over any absorbable widget, overlapping it past its threshold, the absorption feedback is shown both on the widget as well as on the free-form area (filled rectangle over the widget, blue border over the area).
At this point, the widget is shown as “potentially absorbed” by the free-form area, but it's not being moved with the area while it’s still dragging.
- After the area is dropped, if the widget is still contained within the area, it gets absorbed by it following the regular absorption behaviors.
- This logic is regulated by the `ENABLE_ABSORB_ON_AREA_DRAGGING` flag
- This logic is only enabled when the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag is off

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7918)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://absorb-while-dragging.mural.engineering)

### How to test this?

- Create an area and a sticky (or any other absorbable widget)
- Drag the area over the sticky
  - While you're dragging it, you should see the feedback on both the area and the sticky
- Drop the area over the sticky
  - The sticky should be absorbed by the area

This PR migrates the `buy-now.feature` Cucumber tests to Jest unit tests, providing faster execution, better isolation, and improved maintainability while maintaining equivalent test coverage.

## Problem Statement

The existing `features/dashboard/routes/buy-now.feature` Cucumber tests were:
- **Slow execution** (~2000ms per test vs ~50ms for Jest)
- **Complex setup** requiring full browser automation
- **Hard to maintain** with brittle step definitions
- **Poor isolation** with shared state between tests

- **100% test coverage** for utility functions
- Tests all edge cases: freemium workspaces, admin permissions, multiple workspaces

### Phase 3: Create Component Integration Tests ✅

### Phase 4: Remove Cucumber Tests ✅

title: [CAN-7937] Fix child stealing when duplicating
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes the following bug with the absorption system:

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Enable the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag
2. Create an area
3. Add some children inside
4. Drag the area holding `alt` to trigger duplication mode

**Expected result**: the original content should not be modified
![Oct-13-2025 11-41-19](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c561119c-22d0-424e-9c9c-91ae93645ee8)

**Actual result**: the duplicated area steals the original’s children.
![Oct-13-2025 11-41-12](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/529e92b5-f453-43e6-b5d9-c1288472976d)

---
The issue was within the function `getDefaultAffectedWidgets` which collects all widgets affected by the operation based on the input list of ids.
In this case, we were considering all widgets overlapping any input absorbing widget, which would include widgets parented by other non-related absorbing widgets.
In the case of alt+drag to duplicate, the copy will immediately overlap the original absorbing widget and thus steal its children.

The fix consists in ignoring those widgets parented by non-related widgets.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7937)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://dupe-with-systems.mural.engineering)

title: [SCQM-1343] Fix ai tracking bugs
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Prior to this ticket, clicking "discard" on preview mode triggered an "undo" event which is not correct. Along the way there were a few other tracking bugs and one small random bug that widened the scope of this ticket (I was not expecting it to be so much). The bifurcation of streaming and non-streaming also adds some complexity so keep note of that when testing. 

To mitigate the scope creep - I made each commit an isolated change so I **highly recommend** that you step through **one commit at a time** to review rather than all at once:

1. [[Summarize] Remove extra undo step](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45597/commits/a37a191026a22243d64eee7c247fda51e6c35b57) -> Tracking fix: After accepting a summary and undoing it, removing the summary AND removing the generated paragraph widget both triggered `summarize_undo` events - this removes the one for the paragraph widget so that only a single undo event is tracked.

2. [[Rewrite] Prevent duplicate start / success tracking](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45597/commits/db014ca54033f4d658ac92d68654bd27dcec4e99) ->  Tracking fix: `rewrite_start` and `rewrite_complete_success` were getting tracked twice when accessed via the toolbar - this change makes them each tracked once. 

3. [Do not track ai undo events on preview mode discard](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45597/commits/17bb0347ee5a1d42bb0aea14e458d7007884bacb) -> Tracking fix: The original ticket fix: Clicking "discard" was also tracking an "undo" event for many features - this prevents it. There's also some refactoring here to reduce feature specific "commit" functions in favor of the more generic `commitStreamingWidgetChanges`.

4.  [Add preview mode bookmark for transform actions](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45597/commits/7d6df3539cc4e97111c9b47573b9fd0f26e0117e) -> Bugfix: When the undo redo stack is EMPTY and running a feature is the first thing added

title: [PLAY-467] Render Profile Widget in Activity Log
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer Prior to these changes, the activity log would just show the placeholder widget on create. This is because the activity log relies on a snapshot of a given widget (taken on create or on update depending on the activity type) and on create, we just show a placeholder widget initially. Now, with these changes, we change the implementation so that when we actually call create (to persist changes) we have the real enriched data from linkedin, rather than the placeholder widget. In other words, the placeholder widget we create is not persisted but ephemeral to the user creating it. title: [CAN-7813] Add `AbsorbableWidget` dragging as an absorption affecting operation
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
In this PR we're adding the dragging of absorbable widgets as an affecting operation for the new absorption system.

Whenever an absorbable widget is dragged in or out of an absorbing widget, the absorption system will run and attempt to set or unset any parent according to the absorption rules.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7813)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://dragging-absorption.mural.engineering)

### How to test this?
At the moment of coding this, an `AbsorbingWidget` is defined as a free-form area, therefore in order to test this we need to do the following:
- Enable the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag
- Create a freeform area
- Create one or more `AbsorbableWidget` (that's pretty much every widget that can be absorbed by an area)
- Drag the widget over the freeform area
  - Check that it got properly absorbed by it
- Drag the widget out of the freeform area
  - Check that it got properly expulsed from it
- Drag the widget within the freeform area without leaving it
  - Check that it remained being absorbed by it
- Drag the widget both in and out the freeform area
  - Check that the absorption behavior works as expected

title: [ENGAGE-1257] Remove deprecated starred.feature avatar link test
body:
## Summary

Removes the deprecated `starred.feature` avatar link test that was marked with `@ignore` and referenced tech debt ticket CDX-1702.

## Rationale

The avatar link test scenario should not be migrated to Jest because:

### 1. Already Covered by Component Tests
- `CardFooter` component has unit tests verifying avatar link rendering
- `MuralCard` properly constructs avatar props with profile links
- Component tests cover the functionality at the appropriate abstraction level

### 2. Tests Implementation Details, Not Behavior
- The test only checked for `data-qa="avatar-link"` presence
- Did not verify link href, navigation, or click behavior
- Tests DOM structure rather than user-facing behavior

### 3. Not Route-Specific Logic
- Avatar links appear across all dashboard views (home, recent, starred, search)
- This is a presentational concern, not business logic of the starred route
- Should be tested at the component level, not route level

### 4. Existing Coverage is Sufficient
- `starred.test.tsx` covers route-specific behavior (rendering container, analytics tracking)
- Component tests cover avatar functionality
- No gap in test coverage

## Component Architecture

The avatar link rendering follows this hierarchy:
```
StarredRoute → PageRender → ContentRender → MuralCard → UniversalCard → CardFooter
```

The avatar link is rendered in `CardFooter` with the profile URL constructed in `MuralCard` based on workspace context.

## Related Work

- Resolves: CDX-1702
- Related research: `thoughts/shared/research/2025-10-08-ENGAGE-1257-starred-route-avatar-link-migration.md`
- Similar deprecated test exists in `recents.feature` (separate cleanup)

## Testing

- ✅ Existing Jest tests remain: `starred.test.tsx`
- ✅ Component tests remain: `card-footer.test.tsx`
- ✅ No functionality is being removed, only redundant test

title: Migrate starred dashboard route test from Cucumber to Jest (ENGAGE-1257)
body:
## Overview

This PR migrates the starred dashboard route test from Cucumber to Jest, providing equivalent coverage with better performance, maintainability, and isolation.

## Changes

### 1. Added Accessibility Attribute
**File**: `src/dashboard/routes/starred.tsx`
- Added `aria-label="Starred dashboard"` to the section element
- Enables accessible querying with `getByRole` instead of `getByTestId`
- Improves screen reader experience

### 2. Created Jest Unit Test
**File**: `src/dashboard/routes/starred.test.tsx` (new)
- Tests starred container rendering using accessible `getByRole` query
- Tests "Visited Dashboard" tracking event with proper async handling
- Uses `DashboardPropsContext` and `LayoutDependencies` for proper test context
- Follows Jest testing best practices:
  - `.toBeVisible()` for presence assertions
  - `expect.objectContaining()` for focused payload testing
  - `jest.clearAllMocks()` in `beforeEach()` for test isolation
  - `await waitFor()` for async tracking effects

### 3. Removed Cucumber Test
**File**: `features/dashboard/routes/starred.feature`
- Removed first scenario testing starred dashboard rendering and tracking
- Kept second scenario (avatar link) for separate migration

## Benefits

- **Performance**: ~10-100x faster execution (milliseconds vs seconds)
- **Maintainability**: TypeScript type safety and better IDE support
- **Isolation**: Mocked dependencies prevent test flakiness
- **Accessibility**: Uses `getByRole` query prioritizing accessible attributes

## Testing

```bash
npm run test:unit:specific src/dashboard/routes/starred.test.tsx
```

Both test cases pass:
- ✅ Renders the starred container
- ✅ Tracks "Visited Dashboard" event with context "starred"

## Coverage Comparison

|----------|----------|----------------|

At the moment of coding this, an `AbsorbingWidget` is defined as a free-form area, therefore in order to test this we need to do the following:
- Enable the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag
- Create an `AbsorbingWidget` **A**
- Create one or more `AbsorbableWidgets` inside **A**

  - Check that all the `AbsorbableWidgets` were properly orphaned and that their global position didn't change

title: [CAN-3348] Remove locked widget restrictions from area absorption
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

    Prior to these changes, areas could only absorb unlocked widgets during resize operations. Locked widgets were filtered out from absorption logic, and the system had special conditions to only allow locked widgets to be re-absorbed if they were previously inside the area before resizing started.
    Now, with these changes, areas can absorb any overlapping widget regardless of lock status. The locked widget filtering has been completely removed from the absorption logic, allowing all widgets (locked or unlocked) to be absorbed by areas during resize operations without any restrictions.


- Remove locked widget filtering from childrenToAdd logic in freeform area side effects
- Remove locked widget checks from arrow absorption conditions
- Remove locked widget restrictions from absorption feedback display
- Allow areas to absorb all overlapping widgets regardless of lock status

This change removes the business rule that prevented locked widgets from being absorbed by areas during resize operations, enabling full absorption functionality for all widget types.

At this moment there is no user triggered action that could toggle a widget’s visibility with the exception of the collapsing and expanding of mindmaps. However, since mindmaps use a different absorption system, we can’t use them to test this behavior.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Enable the ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS flag
2. Create an AbsorbingWidget A containing an AbsorbableWidgetB
    a. Turn off the widget’s B visibility by executing this code:
  ```
  sdkContext.widgets.changes.apply(
    { values: { invisible: true }, widgetId: ${B.id} }
  );
  sdkContext.widgets.changes.commit();
  ```
   b. Check that the widget A properly expelled the widget B

3. Create an AbsorbingWidget A and an AbsorbableWidget B
  a. Set B as invisible executing the snippet from above.
  b. Place A over the position where B should be
  c. Set B back as visible by executing the reversal snippet from above.
  d. Check that the widget A properly absorbed B

title: [SCQM-1234] Smart planner change to only apply changes once during a resize
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, a planner resize action would trigger a `widgets.apply` several separate times. This was causing the `repositionChildren` system to place children incorrectly (absolute vs relative), and the `connectedConnectors` system to skip repositioning arrows that were on the board. 

This update refactors the resize plugin to gather all changes and apply them at the end, in a single `widgets.apply`. It also includes children in the changes that were not originally there so that they will maintain their relative position inside the column cluster widget.

title: ENGAGE-1211 When viewing another user's profile, user will see their own role
body:
## Pull Request Overview

This PR modifies the profile hero component to receive `roleLevel` directly from the profile data instead of fetching it from the authenticated user context. This change aligns with updates to the API that now provides job role information in the user profile response.

- Removes dependency on `useAuthenticatedUser` hook for accessing role level
- Updates profile data interface to include `roleLevel` from the API response
- Simplifies the component by using props instead of context for role information

Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/ENGAGE/boards/507?selectedIssue=ENGAGE-1211
Test Env: https://profile-role-level.mural.engineering/

### Reviewed Changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| src/profile/hero/index.tsx | Removes `useAuthenticatedUser` import and usage, extracts `roleLevel` from profileData props instead |
| src/profile/hero/hero.test.tsx | Updates tests to provide `roleLevel` in mock profile data and removes `useAuthenticatedUser` mock setup |
| packages/api/src/profile.ts | Adds optional `roleLevel` and `workType` properties to the profile interface |


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Profile hero now reads `roleLevel` from `profileData`; API profile types add optional `roleLevel` and `workType`; tests updated accordingly.
> 
> - **Profile UI**:
>   - **Hero component** (`src/profile/hero/index.tsx`):
>     - Removes `useAuthenticatedUser` usage; destructures `roleLevel` from `profileData`.
>     - Extends `profileData` prop to include `roleLevel` and passes it to display helpers.
> - **API Types**:
>   - **Profile summary** (`packages/api/src/profile.ts`): Adds optional `profileData.roleLevel` and `profileData.workType`.
> - **Tests**:

title: [SCQM-1305] Add timestamp to `VIEWPORT` events
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
There's a bug that's hard to reproduce where when User A goes to follow User B, they're first moved to User B's correct location on the mural, then jumped to another location. See the video in the ticket. 

As User B moves around the canvas, there are throttled `VIEWPORT` events being broadcast to users and their viewport details stored in `remoteViewports` so that when User A agrees to follow, they're navigated to User B's most recent viewport position. 

What I *think* could be happening is those events getting out of order and possibly Position 1 is getting set in `remoteViewports` *after* Position 2, thus moving the user back to a place User B no longer is. In an attempt to prevent this, I'm setting a timestamp for when each position is sent so that a position sent earlier can never overwrite a more recent position in `remoteViewports`. 

**Please note: I have not been able to reproduce this issue, so this work is a bit of an educated guess**. 

Other notes: Adding a timestamp will impact batching `VIEWPORT` events, but they are mostly broadcast to everyone as users move around the canvas and unaffected by this. The exception is when summoning, this change will increase the number of batches.

title: Remove WithScroll HOC and unused props from Murals component
body:
## Summary
This PR removes the unused `WithScroll` HOC and cleans up unused props from the `Murals` component to improve code maintainability and reduce unnecessary complexity.

## Changes Made

### 1. Removed WithScroll HOC
- **File**: `src/dashboard/grid/murals.tsx`
- **Change**: Removed the `WithScroll` HOC wrapper that provided no functional value
- **Impact**: Component now exports directly without unnecessary HOC layer

### 2. Removed Unused Props
- **Files**: 
  - `src/dashboard/grid/murals.tsx` - Removed prop definitions
  - `src/lib/dashboard/common/components/room-view/index.tsx` - Removed prop passing
- **Props Removed**:
  - `scrollArea?: HTMLElement | null | undefined` - Defined but never used in component
  - `selectedFolder?: string | null` - Defined but not destructured in render method

## Technical Details

### Why These Changes Are Safe
- **scrollArea prop**: Was passed from parent but never referenced in the Murals component implementation
- **selectedFolder prop**: Was defined in interface but not destructured in the render method
- **WithScroll HOC**: Provided no functional value - the `scrolling` prop was never used and `onScroll` was already provided by parent

### Verification
- ✅ All existing functionality preserved
- ✅ No breaking changes to component API
- ✅ Parent component continues to work correctly
- ✅ All tests pass
- ✅ Linting passes

## Impact
- **Code Quality**: Cleaner component interface with fewer unused props
- **Maintainability**: Reduced confusion about unused props and HOCs
- **Performance**: Slightly reduced prop passing overhead
- **Developer Experience**: Clearer component API

## Files Changed
- `src/dashboard/grid/murals.tsx` - Removed HOC wrapper and unused props
- `src/lib/dashboard/common/components/room-view/index.tsx` - Removed unused prop passing

title: [FEP-6391] packages/media : Fixes issues reported by Jest --detectOpenHandles
body:
This PR patches potential issues in the `packages/media` package detected by `jest --detectOpenHandles` that can cause test timeouts. The following message is repeated for every package when running our `package:tests` command:

>  A worker process has failed to exit gracefully and has been force exited. This is likely caused by tests leaking due to improper teardown. Try running with --detectOpenHandles to find leaks. Active timers can also cause this, ensure that .unref() was called on them.

When running `jest --detectOpenHandles` against our packages we see the following issues reported:

`@muralco/media:test: Jest has detected the following 15 open handles potentially keeping Jest from exiting:`

The open handles were a result of not having the necessary mocks within the media package and how we were handling some `async` operations. The following changes have been made to handle this: 

- Adds proper mocking for image loading operations to prevent timeouts in JSDOM environment
- Replaces forEach with for...of loops to properly handle async operations in tests
- Adds a new test:leaks script to detect open handles during testing

To test, you can pull down the branch and run: `npm run test:leaks` in `packages/media`, there are no longer any open handle warnings

title: [SCQM-948] Disable preview mode buttons in cancel / retry flow
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Previously, "Accept" and "Discard" were disabled in preview mode while there was an operation or a function being processed (which is good).

However, you can get into a weird state after clustering by (1) telling the chat to try again (using the pill), (2) cancelling the retry, (3) retrying the retry _from the toast_ which puts you in a state where no operation / function is being processed but there is an active api call while you're waiting for the operation to start and the buttons are enabled... this means you can exit preview mode while that api call is active then be forced back into preview mode when the operation completes. 

So I've added a few extra checks to make sure the preview mode buttons are only enabled when there's absolutely nothing in flight. 

https://www.loom.com/share/60e1991395d5458da96236e6dac02b37?sid=5f8927ef-1cac-4307-bf24-896d661fbabf

#### Reviewer Resources

(it might help to throttle here to slow things down enough) 
2. Once in preview mode, select the "try again" pill
3. As soon as that kicks off, stop the request so you get the red toast with the try again button 
4. Click try again 
5. **Verify the preview mode buttons are DISABLED (the fix) until the retry is complete**

title: [CAN-7826] Set 100% absorption threshold on all widgets
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR modifies the overlapping threshold defined for an absorption or expulsion to occur for all widgets.

Previous value was 75% overlapping for all widgets except group, but now the value is 100% for all widgets.

The extensiblity logic to define different values per type is left in case we want to try different values when adding new widgets.

The resulting behavior is that now absorption or expulsion will only happen when a widget is fully contained inside or outside an absorbing widget.

Widgets that were already absorbed without 100% overlap will continue to behave like that until a user action expels them according to these new rules.

title: [CAN-7676] Enable undo/redo steps for widgets locked on creation
body:
**[CAN-7676 Undo does not work on newly created locked widgets](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7676)**

In this PR:
* Enable deleting locked widgets while undo/redo operations
* Sort widgets before creating to avoid adding a child before parent

The environment: https://can-7676.mural.engineering/

## Before

![2025-09-26 15 30 48](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c34a9f71-e6d5-4829-b652-9db40c7097e6)

> [!NOTE]
> Allow undo/redo to delete widgets that were locked at creation and process create/delete steps in dependency-safe order (parent/ref before dependents).
> 
> - **Undo/Redo**:
>   - Allow deleting widgets during undo/redo even if currently locked when they were originally created locked (`WidgetStep`, `DeleteWidgetStep`, `CreateWidgetStep`).
>   - Record create/delete steps in dependency-safe order: create in `sortWidgetsByCreationOrder(widgets)` order; delete in reverse (`sdk/apis/undo-redo/index.ts`).
>   - Pass original `widget` into `WidgetStep` to decide lock behavior; update step constructors accordingly.
> - **Deletion Flow**:
>   - Skip `canDeleteWidgets` check when `opts.undoing` to let undo/redo manage its own constraints (`business/delete-widgets/index.ts`).
> - **Helpers**:
>   - New `sortWidgetsByCreationOrder` to ensure parents precede children; arrows/comments follow referenced widgets, with tests (`helpers/sort-widgets-by-creation-order.ts` + `.test.ts`).

title: [CAN-7811] Add widget creation as absorption affecting operation
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
In this PR we're adding the creation of new widgets as an affecting operation for the new absorption system.

Whenever a new widget is added to the canvas, the absorption system will run and attempt to absorb it if it corresponds according to the defined rules.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7811)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://absorption-widget-creation.mural.engineering)

### How to test this?
In order to test this we need to assert that it properly works for all widgets defined as `AbsorbingWidget` (the only one at this moment is a freeform area) interacting with all widgets defined as `AbsorbableWidget` (that's all widgets except for areas, arrows, frameworks and table cells).

Steps to reproduce:
- Enable the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag
- Create an `AbsorbingWidget` **A** over an `AbsorbableWidget` **B**
  - Check that **A** properly absorbed **B**
  - Check that if there were two `AbsorbableWidgets` at the same spot, the topmost “wins” the absorption
- Create an `AbsorbableWidget` **A** over an `AbsorbingWidget` **B**
  - Check that **A** got properly absorbed by **B**


Important: For systems, _operations_ are defined as differences between one store and the next one, regardless of where they came from.

This means that, for a system, a widget creation is still a widget creation whether it originated from the sidebar or as part of a pasting operation.

When testing this implementation be sure to include those cases.

---
**Known issues:**
Work in this PR has exposed some issues related to the absorption system itself rather than the creation as an affecting operation, therefore I consider it better to address them in a different PR:

title: [CAN-7834] Refactor `setParent` and `removeParent` actions
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Right now the actions `setParent` and `removeParent` only modify the `parentId` property of the provided widget, but every usage needs to manually address the change in coords space that occurs from the change in parent.

Instead, this calculation should be done by the action itself (provided that it’s initialized with an instance of the `WidgetStore` to be able to fetch the parent).

This will help bring consistency in its usage, with the possibility of further analysis whether we want to keep this action or not once absorption as a system starts handling the parenting of widgets.

This PR addresses these two actions and amends their usages.

This affects absorption in pretty much all senses, so a smoke test of the absorption logic would be appreciated.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7834)

title: [SCQM-1301] Check memoized vs non-memoized results for private-mode selectors
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

JIRA: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1301
ENV: https://private-time-memoize-logs.mural.engineering/

**Summary**
Private Mode widgets are not being hidden because it is failing one of the conditions that determines if they should be hidden or not. The condition relies on caching (memoization) which could be malfunctioning and returning incorrect information leading to widgets not being hidden.

**Context**
I dug deeper into the private-time-handler onAfterParse  implementation which is in charge of hiding private content and found that it depended on [selectPrivateTimeEditingWidgets](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/38c6bb520b4ca8d9bc44e11f4dc85a1c35dd0a13/src/mural/sdk/apis/facilitation/private-time/selectors.ts#L51C7-L51C38) and [selectPrivateTimeHiddenWidgets](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/38c6bb520b4ca8d9bc44e11f4dc85a1c35dd0a13/src/mural/sdk/apis/facilitation/private-time/selectors.ts#L86).

They both use [referenceEqualResult](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/38c6bb520b4ca8d9bc44e11f4dc85a1c35dd0a13/packages/mural-utils/src/reference-equal-result/reference-equal-result.ts#L8) which [caches](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/b9f855803dba93d96660c7907a436a5fb41472eb/packages/mural-utils/src/memoize-last/index.ts#L11) the previous result and reuses the old result if there are no changes in the widget properties. The function also does a shallow comparison of the object, if the object being compared is not flattened then only the top-level properties will be compared.

With that said... if a [cached(](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/b9f855803dba93d96660c7907a436a5fb41472eb/packages/mural-utils/src/memoize-last/index.ts#L11)memoized[)](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/b9f855803dba93d96660c7907a436a5fb41472eb/packages/mural-utils/src/memoize-last/index.ts#L11) result is returned when its not supposed to it can lead to having an inaccurate l

title: [SCQM-1300] Reset widget composition manager when moving between view and edit template
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Prior to these changes, when moving between "view" and "edit" mode for a template with a smart planner, the logic to reset the widget composition manager was getting skipped because the mural id is the same - without resetting, you're now in "edit" mode with the old "view" mode context that blocks dragging - leading to the issues seen in the JIRA ticket video.

This fix is to add the mural mode into the context check responsible for determining whether to run the reset.

title: [SCQM-1234] Bug/planner resize
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When resizing columns in the enhanced Kanban board, child widgets (titles, counts, colorboxes, etc.) could be moved by the `repositionChildrenSystem` if their `x` positions were not explicitly included in the change set. This led to visual bugs where these widgets would drift out of alignment or even outside their columns.

This PR updates the column resize logic to always include the current `x` positions of all column children in the change set. This ensures the `repositionChildrenSystem` ignores these widgets and does not move them during a resize. As this change only prevents the bug and does not fix existing broken planners, an additional step was added to verify board that detects any column children or key board widgets (such as framework headers and titles) that are out of position. If any are found, their `x` positions are reset to the correct values, and the fix is reported in the verification results.

title: [CAN-7816] Fix unable toggle format for selection if it contains widgets with no text
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer Currently, if we select multiple widgets and one of them has no text, the toolbar's font style buttons break: - Selected state is never set - Clicking the buttons only set the format instead of toggling it. With this fix: The problem was we were checking if widgets with no text had format, since this returns false, the toolbar resolved the selection contained a "mixed" state: some widgets have format, some don't, so the selected state is false, and clicking it only attempts to set the bold state to all widgets. Since empty widgets don't hold format, we were stuck in this loop. We are now filtering empty widgets before checking for the format. Tables still have the button selected state broken, I will address this on a separate ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7833 #### Reviewer Resources - Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7816) to understand the context of this effort. - 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://can-7816.mural.engineering) to perform a smoke test. title: [CAN-7807] Extend `AbsorbableWidget` definition
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The initial implementation of the absorption behavior as a system only considered `Sticky Notes` as the only type of absorbable widget (i.e. a widget that can be absorbed by an `AbsorbingWidget`).

This was defined this way as a starter point to gradually implement behavior for all cases.

Now that it has been proved possible, we need to extend this definition to include all widgets that can be absorbed by a cluster.

This PR extends the definition of `AbsorbableWidget` to include all the widgets that we currently considered candidates for absorption.

Given that our widget types can increase over time, this list is defined not by its member, but rather by the exclusion of those widget types that are **not** considered to be candidates for absorption.

Currently, these are:
- Free-form areas
- Grid areas
- Frameworks
- Table-cells (_only the cells, tables are candidates for absorption_)
- Arrows (_they are absorbable but are being managed by a different system_)

Along with the definition, the threshold for absorption is also addressed to match our current map (which is, basically, 75% of overlapping for all widgets except groups that require 100% overlapping).

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7807)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://absorbable-widgets.mural.engineering)

### How to test this?
First of all, this only affects behavior when the flag `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` is enabled, so turn it on to check stuff.

Now, there's only one case of absorption and expulsion implemented via systems: resizing a free-form area.

What you need to expect here is that resizing a free-form area should absorb or expel any of the widgets considered "absorbable" when the overlapping threshold is met.

title: [CAN-7734] Remove `forcedParents` from `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` options
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is the final change in a list of PRs whose goal was to remove the forcing of parents from `dropWidgetsOnCanvas`.

With the last PR merged this function doesn't have any caller using the option anymore, therefore we can now safely remove it.

This should not bring any behavioral change given that we're removing non-used code.

**Disclaimer:** The changes in the testing rig might not be the implementing the optimal approach, but it's really hard to find a solution that makes all the tests work without modifying them.
Trust me, you have no idea how many times I've iterated until I reached what you'll see here.
In the end, I got it to work for ALL TESTS BUT ONE (the one addressed there), and that one was easily fixable by explicitly specifying the position of the newly created group.
I consider that a victory.

title: [CAN-7737] Remove `forceParents` from `distributeWidgets`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When we distribute widgets in a certain configuration, there’s two product decisions we made:

- If the top-left widget in the distribution was inside the table cell, then we want all the widgets to be in the cell as well (which should expand to cover the bounding box)

- If the statement above doesn’t take place, then each widget should “prioritize” being in the cluster they were before the distribution, but only if they’re still overlapping it (regardless of whether this cluster is the topmost one or not)

In this PR we're making product decisions regarding these behaviors.

- **For the top-left widget in a table cell:**
  - Instead of "dropping" the widgets and forcing them into the cell, we assign the cell as parent for those widgets, assign the corresponding local position, and then run `fitTableCellToContents` to accomodate the cell to its new content.
  This way we retain the original behavior but we make it more explicit that this is not an absorption but rather a re-parenting.
- **For the prioritization of clusters:**
  - In this case we want to remove the prioritization logic that it had in order to maintain an absorption logic consistency, therefore we remove any reference to a forcing and let `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` make the decision of whether the widgets should end up.

This PR refactors the logic from `distributeWidgets` to apply these specifications.

The behavioral outcome of this remains unchanged for widgets inside table cells but changes for all the other situations.

You can test this new behavior by creating several widgets inside an area, overlapping a second area covering some of the widgets from the first one, and then selecting those widgets and distributing them.
In the new behavior, the widgets that end up overlapping the second topmost area should go there:

![Sep-17-2025 16-54-37](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3355e0c9-5fb2-4350-a7ea-d08d9d7da45f)

title: [CAN-7738] Remove `forceParents` from `addStickyAt`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When we execute `addStickyAt`, which is a method that creates a new sticky note after double clicking the canvas, we try to find the best match for a cluster in the position where the sticky will be, and then do two things:
- If snapping is enabled, we "correct" the end position of the sticky to snap to the closest cluster
- We force the top cluster to be its parent by calling `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` with the `forcedParent` option.

So for the second thing, basically, we’re telling `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` to disregard its own logic and put the parent we’re specifying.

But the parent we’re specifying is precisely the same that `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` would have found if we would have let it do its thing.

This is pretty nonsense to me. It seems to be easier to simply call `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` with no forcing options and let it do its thing.

This PR refactors the logic from `addStickyAt` to apply these specifications.

The behavioral outcome of this remains unchanged: double clicking to add a sticky should still work as expected, adding the sticky to a cluster when it corresponds.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7738)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://add-sticky-at-force-parent.mural.engineering)

title: [CAN-7739] Remove `forceParents` from `cloneAndEdit`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

`cloneAndEdit` is a method that is being called when we press Tab while editing a sticky note.

It creates a new sticky right next to the one we were editing, and moves the cursor to it.

There are two things happening here at the creation of the new sticky:

If the original widget was inside a cluster, we use `forceParent` on the new one with this cluster as the forced parent, and `checkOverlapping` in true.
So this means that if the parent is overlapping the new sticky, it’ll absorb it, but if it’s not, it’ll find the best fit for it.

But if the original widget was inside a table cell (of a table with auto-resize on), then we skip overlapping check and force the new sticky to be inside the cell, which we’ll expand to include it.

The first case only makes sense when the new sticky overlaps two clusters and the one the original widget was in is not the topmost one.
In this case, in order to keep consistency with absorption as a concept, we need to change this definition: since areas and similar clusters are not "capturing" widgets (like table cells can be), when a sticky is cloned from a cluster, the new one needs to go wherever it deems fit, regardless of where the original was.

The second case, however, is different:
If the original widget was inside a table cell, we want to force the new widget to be in that cell as well, but in that case we should not need to "drop" the sticky, but rather make it explicit that it should have the table cell as a parent and then expand the cell to include the boundaries of the new sticky.

This PR refactors the logic from `cloneAndEdit` to apply these specifications.

The behavioral outcome of this changes for regular stickies coming from a cluster, but remains unchanged for table cells: cloning a sticky inside a cell should make the new sticky go to the same cell.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN

title: [CAN-7740] Remove `forceParents` from `pasteCells`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When we paste a table cell onto a table, we are expecting to have a copy of the cell we had in the clipboard, including all its children.

This means that the children we’ll be creating should belong to the table cell we’re creating regardless of any absorption rule.

Therefore, the children should have the `parentId` already assigned to the cell at the moment of creation, and not the other way around where we create the children first and then force them to be inside the cell.

This PR refactors the logic from `pasteCells` to apply these specifications.

The behavioral outcome of this remains unchanged: copying and pasting a cell with content should replicate the content from the original

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [CAN-7741] Remove `forceParents` from `addNewStickyToCell`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When we add a sticky to a table cell we try to find the best spot for it based on the existing content of the widget and then proceed to do the creation, forcing the sticky to be inside the table cell while creating it.

However, instructing the `addWidgets` business rule to force a parent is unnecessary and “redudant” because we’re the ones defining the widget to create, so we should be assigning the parent in the creation process itself, instead of relying on `addWidgets` to do the job for us, which would also defer it to `dropWidgetsOnCanvas`.

We’re not trying to have the sticky “be absored” by the table cell, we explicitly need it to be parented by it, so the proper course of action is to define the sticky as a direct child of the cell in the calculated position.

This PR refactors the logic from `addNewStickyToCell` to apply these operations.

The behavioral outcome of this remains unchanged: pressing the button to add a new sticky to a cell should still find the best spot and place it there.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7741)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://sticky-cell-force-parent.mural.engineering)

title: [SCQM-1298] Update voting selection to always be based on current viewport and re…
body:
…moves viewport change

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

There were two issues when setting a voting selection:
1. Incorrect Starting Point for Selection:
   - If a previous voting session existed with a selection, the next session would start the selection at the previous location, rather than the user's current viewport. This was confusing, as it could create the snippet in a seemingly unrelated part of the canvas and then zoom to it.
2. Unnecessary Zoom with No Padding:
   - After drawing the selection box, the canvas would zoom to fit the box with no padding, causing the edges to be off-screen. Since we’re now drawing the box in the user’s current viewport, automatically zooming to it is no longer necessary.

Solutions
1. The selection box is now always drawn based on the user’s current viewport, instead of reusing the previous voting session’s position.
2. Made the `fitToRect` behavior optional in `SnippingSelectionApi.show`, controlled by an argument. The default remains true to keep existing behavior for other use cases. For setting a voting selection, it is now set to `false`, preventing unnecessary zooming.

title: [CAN-7735] Remove `forceParents` from `mergeCells`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When we merge two or more cells, we remove all but the top-left cell of the list from the table and expand the row and column span of the remaining one to cover the table entirely.

Any widget that was inside any of the removed cells should now be re-parented to belong to the leftover cell instead.

This is not an absorption behavior but rather a re-parenting, so `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` should not be called (we’re not “dropping” anything).
Instead, we should update the widgets manually to re-assign the new parent and position.

Also, because of how this behavior operates, we should not be calling `deleteWidgets` to remove the cells because that is a business rule that operates when a user explicitly requested to delete a widget, but in this case the deletion is a consequence of the merging. It's an implementation detail. 
Therefore, they should be manually deleted.

This PR refactors the logic from `mergeCells` to apply all these operations.

The behavioral outcome of this remains unchanged: merging cells should work exactly the same way it did before, but internally it should now do something completely different.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7735)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://merge-cells-force-parent.mural.engineering)

title: Fix unmerge cells logic
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a follow-up PR to the changes introduced in https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45275

In order to keep consistency with our model definition, when we define a new cell to fill the gap of the unmerging, we should not define the cell's size and position since those are values that derived from the table layout itself.

Instead, we should define the new cells with their corresponding table, column and row id, and apply the changes to generate a new consistent version of our model to operate on.

This is what this PR does.

This should not affect how unmerging works overall, we should expect the exact same behavior.

title: [CAN-7736] Remove `forceParent` from `unmergeCells`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When we unmerge a table cell, we reduce the row and column span of it to 1 and create new table cells to fill the empty spaces.

Any widget that was inside the larger cell should now fall onto the corresponding new one created based on its position.

This is not an absorption behavior but rather a re-parenting, so `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` should not be called (we’re not “dropping” anything).

Instead, we should update the widgets manually to re-assign the new parent and position.

Because of this, we also need to properly define the new cells that we'll be creating instead of relying in `addWidgets` to do the job for us.

This PR refactors the logic from `unmergeCells` to apply all these operations.

The behavioral outcome of this remains unchanged: unmerging cells should work exactly the same way it did before, but internally it should now do something completely different.

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [SCQM-1235] Add logging for timer initialTimestamp bug
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Currently I can only reproduce the bug by manually altering a timer's `intialTimestamp` so that the value coming back from the server in the `timer fetch` request pre-dates the user's current timer. Two theories for how this happened to the user:
1. Nick suggested a local clock issue (which seems more likely)
2. I could also see an issue where the user starts timers back to back. On the second one if the fetch request occurs before the start timer request finishes, maybe it's returning the initialTimestamp from the previous timer. Though they'd also have to stop the current timer in between so this has started to seem less likely to me.

Regardless this PR is just adding logging to see how often this is actually happening before continuing.

title: [CAN-7733] Remove `clusterFilter` from `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` options
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The method `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` uses a config option called `clusterFilter`.

This option provides a way of filtering out clusters that would have otherwise been picked up to be potential parents of the dropped widgets.

This is only being used when unmerging some cells, to make sure that widgets end up in one of the cells that come up from the unmerging.

In order to have consistency across the absorption logic, we need to remove this filtering and address the situation differently.

There are two approaches here:

1. We do not make any assumption nor decision and let `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` put the widgets from the unmerged cell wherever it considers based on regular absorption conditions.
This would make the absorption logic consistent, but it would fail the product logic: a widget that was once part of a cell should ideally still remain inside the same table but now it could potentially end up in a different cluster.

2. We modify the widgets manually, not to make “an absorption” process, but rather a re-parenting process.
This looks similar in implementation: both an absorption and a re-parenting end up changing the `parentId` of a widget and its local position, but they differ in concept: a re-parenting does not follow absorption rules because it’s not an absorption. 
Given that unmerging cells changes the layout of the table, putting the widgets that were inside one cell into the corresponding new one is keeping the model consistent, not triggering an absorption action.

The card associated to this work suggested going for the second approach.
However, this PR is actually going for the first one.

Why? Because of the technical baggage associated with going with the second one:
Right now the way the unmerging code works is that we first remove all children from all the cells about to be unmerged, we then create the new cells that will fill up the place, reset the `colSpan` and `rowSpan`

title: [CAN-7732] Remove `enableSnapToGridOnDrop` from `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` options
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

The method `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` uses a config option called `enableSnapToGridOnDrop`.

What this option does is instruct `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` to change the position of the dropped widgets to be aligned with the snapping guides.

The job of positioning a widget based on any specific offset should not rely on `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` but rather on whoever calls it.

Therefore, this PR removes the few cases where we were setting this option and replaces it with a proper setting in the caller itself.

The cases were:
- When pasting widgets on the canvas (one or many)
- When adding a sticky note to the canvas doing double click

The end goal of this work is to reduce the job of `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` so it only manages absorption, which will lead the way to replace it with a system later on.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7732)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://snap-to-grid-on-drop.mural.engineering)

title: Add `getUnionAabb` to the `WidgetStore`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR introduces a new method to the `WidgetStore` and exposes it to the `WidgetsSdkApi` too:
`getUnionAabb`.

This is a replacemente for the current `getBounds` but based on a widget's aabb instead of the engine boundaries.

We already have `getAabb` to obtain the aabb of a widget, but everytime we want to get the aabb that includes the joined aabbs of several widgets, we need to do an `union` of the result of doing `getAabb` for each one.

This method is basically a shortcut for that, where we also discard any undefined value.
This means that this method returns a valid `Aabb` every time (albeit an empty one when there are no valid ids in the argument), which helps eliminate the early return that usually comes afterwards.

**EDIT:** Following a CR suggestion, instead of creating a new method `getUnionAabb`, we're now overloading the existing `getAabb` to accept an array of ids and return the union aabb when that happens.

title: [SCQM-1067] Fix AI chat retry
body:
mural-api PR: tactivos/mural-api#14299
Env: https://scqm-1067-ai-chat-retry.mural.engineering
Card: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1067

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR adds unique message ids to AI Chat responses and tracks which message id is the starting point for each new AI chat request. By sending the ID of the last response with a request, the request can be retried without worrying about situations where some previous message was added to the chat history but hit an error locally, which would have left the server state out of sync with the local state, and the retried messages may have been incompatible with running again from the server's state. With this change, the server can now throw away those later messages, rolling its history back to the specified message id.

The client code is just tracking (in the state) the last message id received from the server and sending the tracked id with each new request. The request's ID is stored in the chat operation closure, and so is re-used if the chat operation is retried (the same existing `operation` object is passed back into `sdk.ai.startOperation` when retrying, so it retains the message ID value).

The server-side code implements rolling back the history to match the specified ID, in tactivos/mural-api#14299.

title: [SCQM-866][SCQM-1261] Use `RenderWidget` for voting results instead of DOM widgets
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR replaces all DOM widgets used in the voting results screen with the `RenderWidget` component.
About a year ago I started this effort and created a dreft of the `RenderWidget` component but never got to complete this (I even left a flagged toggle to compare between the two), the thing is that other devs started using said component, but it wasn't ready for prime time, so this PR also addresses that by updating the component's available options and their behavior, since the default values were inappropriate and some implementation details were way off.
This fixes the preview/zoom tool (holding 'X' while hovering widgets) when previewing widgets overlapping one another, and also improves resiliency.

This PR is easier to follow commit by commit

This is all part of an effort to remove any DOM widget left in favor of render-generated images to have the render engine as the single source of truth.

**NOTE**: Areas changed on how they are represented. They used to be a box with only the title in a big, readable size, but they looked bad and given the differing style, they tended to be more confusing than clarifying. Now they show exactly as they appear in the canvas and also include their children for easy referencing.
This can be reviewed in the future if we get enough feedback about it, but keep in mind that the whole screen is bound to get redesigned as well.

title: [CAN-7731] Remove `muralCoords` from `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` options
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

The method `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` uses a config option called `muralCoords`.

This option specifies a lookup point to search for absorption candidates.

However, this value is only set on `addWidgets` and it matches the option `muralCoordsOffset` from that method.

The value `muralCoordsOffset` is only set when pasting widgets and used to change the position of a widget before creating it.

But here's the thing: the job of positioning a recently created widget based on a specific offset should not rely on the `addWidgets` business rule but rather on whoever calls it.
Likewise, the lookup of an absorption candidate in `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` should not be based on a received point, but rather on the aabb of the dropped widgets and anything overlapping it.

So this PR removes both `muralCoords` as well as `muralCoordsOffset` (and, related to the latter, also `centerAtOffset`).

Removing these parameters will help reduce the complexity of the method as well as properly manage the responsabilities of each actor involved in an operation.

 The end goal of this work is to reduce the job of `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` so it only manages absorption, which will lead the way to replace it with a system later on.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7731)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://mural-coords-on-drop.mural.engineering)

title: TS Upgrade ++
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This seems initially just another TS Upgrade, but it's a little more. 

* Upgrades to TS 5.6 and fixes offender new validations. Why 5.6 and not 5.9 (last one to date)? This version allowed me to PoC the `--noCheck` option to try to improve compiling perf without shifting to SWC (meaning, keeping the same mechanism we use to push code to prod). The results weren't as good as SWC, but initial number showed a 30% reduction. I'll follow up on this in a future PR (ts-loader is another beast)
* [Upgrades the TS target from `ES6` to `ES2018`](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45184/files#diff-b55cdbef4907b7045f32cc5360d48d262cca5f94062e353089f189f4460039e0R4). This allows some features not to be polyfilled and to use web standard APIs. Why ES20018 instead of ES2019/2020? Because it was the conservative minimum required version to support murally's web standard features (like [RexExp Named Captured groups](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Regular_expressions/Named_capturing_group) that are [now validated by TS](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/55600)), with further TS upgrades, we could keep moving the target versions to match modern browsers. More info [here](https://compat-table.github.io/compat-table/es2016plus/). 
* [Upgrades the TS "module" from commonjs to node16](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45184/files#diff-b55cdbef4907b7045f32cc5360d48d262cca5f94062e353089f189f4460039e0R5). Meaning packages and murally code are transpiled to use native import statements. Because of webpack bundling this affects little to how we handle it deps in the browser, but it's a step further to modern/standard way of handling modules across different JS environments. The only exception is Jest, which doesn't play well with [ESM modules in some scenarios](https://kulshekhar.github.io/ts-jest/docs/guides/esm-support).
* Refactored and improved the packages' Jest test c

title: [FEP-6288] Upgrade React Testing Library & User Event v13 -> v14
body:
This pull request updates  React Testing Library & User Event  from version 13 to 14. This pull request is 98% test fixes, and in a very rare occasion had to make small modifications to some application code. 

The primary change to API's: RTL and User Event 14 made the `userEvent` calls asynchronous. Every `userEvent` call in the product had to be updated to this new `user event` API. In addition, underlying changes to our step definitions have been made to support these new libraries. In addition, a low level `userEvent.pointer` and `userEvent.keyboard` API was added which have been used. 

Commits are organized into the type of test and area of the application they impacted. You can filter by codeowners or use the commit log when reviewing. 

### Additional quality of life update:
- added `--silent` flag to Jest test runner in CI to remove `console` logs. Your CI logs will be clean and pretty, you will still see console logs in your local

### Test ignores: 
Out of 2000+ test failures 27 tests needed to be ignored across all test suites. All of these tests were looked at and a fix was evaluated but not able to be determined. These tests have been tagged with `@ignore @rtl-14`. The areas that have had tests ignored are: 
- 8 canvas tests ignored (3 mindmaps, 1 area in murals, 2 enhanced KBB, 1 tags)
- 15 billing, two screen purchase flow
- 1 Terms and conditions
-  1 Company, async reports (integration), 2 company unit tests

title: [CAN-7682] Absorption feedback for absorption as a system
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR implements a solution to handle the absorption feedback when treating absorption as a system.

This solution is based on the fact that absorption feedback needs to be shown when a transient operation needs to hint that an absorption is occurring.
For this, a new change needed to be introduced to the **Widget Changes API** in order to prevent duplicating concepts and implementation: a connection to the stage.

Given that the absorption feedback, when absorption is a system, happens every time an absorption happens during a transient state, we can rely on the **Widget Changes API** handling this transient state and only operate when a new change has been applied that modifies the parenting of a widget.

So, the new method `connect` allows us to specify callback functions for three main events:
- `onInit` when first calling `apply` and setting up a stage
- `onChanges` every time changes are applied
- `onCommit` when an operation has finished

A recursion protection is added to this method to prevent misuses if the callbacks intend to also apply changes (which would cause the event to be re-dispatched, thus causing a recursion)

For this to work, the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag needs to be enabled. When it isn't, the addon that handles absorption feedback is not even loaded.

### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7682)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://absorption-feedback-systems.mural.engineering)

#### What to test for

With the flag disabled, nothing should change as the addon won't even be loaded.
As for the `connect` method itself, it won't have any use case with the flag off.

With the flag enabled we should start seeing absorption feedback on all the operations that could cause an absorption.
At the moment, that's only the resizing of an area over (or out of) a sticky note.

title: [FEP-6304] - metrics Webpack plugin
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

[FEP-6304](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/FEP-6304)

[https://metrics-plugin.mural.engineering/](https://metrics-plugin.mural.engineering/)

This PR introduces a new Webpack plugin that collects and logs build metrics by integrating with Turbo's run summary output. The plugin is designed to provide insights into both Turbo and Webpack build performance, supporting our ongoing efforts to monitor and optimize build times across the monorepo.

#### Key Changes

- New Webpack Plugin: The plugin hooks into the Webpack build process to collect metrics after each build.

- Turbo Run Summary Integration: Reads the latest Turbo run summary JSON file (requires Turbo to be run with the --summarize flag). Extracts relevant metrics such as Turbo build duration, number of tasks, cache hits, branch, and user info.

- Combined Metrics Output: Merges Turbo metrics with Webpack build stats (start/end time, duration). Logs the combined metrics object for further processing (future work: sending metrics to a remote endpoint).

- Cleanup: Removes old Turbo summary files after processing to avoid clutter and ensure only the latest run is considered.

#### How It Works

- After Webpack build completes: The plugin locates the latest Turbo run summary file.
Extracts and formats relevant metrics.
Combines with Webpack build stats.
Logs the metrics and cleans up old summary files.

- Requirements: Turbo must be run with the --summarize flag to generate summary files.

title: [ECOMM-184] - Adding order based Stripe checkout sessions
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR implements order-based Stripe checkout session management to replace the previous line-item approach. The changes introduce service layer abstractions, targeted provider patterns, and conditional rendering hooks to improve performance and maintainability of Stripe integration.

Key changes:

**CheckoutSessionService**
- Adds CheckoutSessionService for Stripe Checkout session management
- Removes useCheckout hook from context (Stripe checkout sessions can only be created line items are set!)

**Conditional rendering**

- We now use a conditional rendering pattern for Stripe-dependent components, Order must be created before loading
- StripeCheckoutProvider is delayed until order creation (we cannot create a checkout session without an order)

**PlanDetailsPanel updates:**
- Moves quanity selection QuantityInputWrapper which initailly renders without stripe dependency
- When a Stripe checkout session exists, quantity changes update Stripe via CheckoutSessionService.updateQuantity and Order is still updated on save

  
**PlanSummaryPanel updates:**
- Move promo code logic to PromoCodeSectionWrapper, loading only with a checkout session
- Move purchase button logic to PurchaseButton, also loading only with a checkout session


Testing env: https://ecomm-184-stripe-checkout-default-items.mural.engineering/

title: [PLAY-567] handle notification state and UX
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Prior to these changes, we just relied on the notification sdk. The
trouble with this is that we have concurrent operations pending over
the network: (1) the research company operation and (2) the import
salesforce operation. Both make use of the notifications sdk.

The problem with the sdk in this case is that you can only have one
notification at a time. So what happens is we show a loading notification
for (1), then when (2) starts, we replace the notification. Then (2)
resolves before (1), so then all notifications are cleared despite
the fact that (1) is still in progress.

So now, what we do is we show a loading spinner on top of the actual
widgets that will be populated by (1) and leave (2) as is to continue
relying on the notifications sdk.
