title: [SCQM-1247] Fix ai large request toast
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The goal is to maintain consistent messaging / style in the toast. 

Previously:
1. Request a retro
**"Working on it..."**
2. AI determines `createWorkshop` should be called so it sends the **create workshop** operation, token count is large so toast goes to 2 lines
**"This may take a minute"**
**"Creating a workshop..."**
3. Results come back, operation is a success, we send results via **chat** operation, token count is small for chat operation so toast reverts
**"Creating a workshop..."**

With this change: 
1. Request a retro
**"Working on it..."**
2. AI determines `createWorkshop` should be called so it sends the **create workshop** operation, token count is large so toast goes to 2 lines 
**"This may take a minute"**
**"Creating a workshop..."**
3. Results come back and we store the token count from the operation that just succeeded 
4. Send results via **chat** operation but utilize the token count we just store to keep consistency until action is complete
**"This may take a minute"**
**"Creating a workshop..."**

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [CAN-7689] Refactor `Widget Changes API` to use dependency injection
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
In order to improve the modularity of the **Widget Changes API** as well as to facilitate its usage in unit testing, we need to remove all the external dependencies that the API has.

In this PR I'm implementing a dependency injection pattern which will really benefit our intention as well as keep the logic untouched.

The goal for this PR is to be able to load up the real API in a test environment in order to have a reliable way of testing how changes are applied onto our local model.

A nice side effect of this would be the possibility of moving the API to a package in the future, but that's beyond the scope for now.

This PR has no behavioral effect, thus nothing should change.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7689)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://changes-api-deps.mural.engineering)

title: [SCQM-1161] Add property filtering to several AI functions
body:
Test Env: https://reduce-widgetrepr-tokens.mural.engineering
Card: [SCQM-1161](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1161)
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
An optional property filtering argument has been added to the `getWidgetRepresentationForAI` and `getWidgetsRepresentationForAI` (plural / widget array) helper functions, to allow results returned from AI function calls to cut down the properties returned to ones specific to the function itself. If not set, and especially as used by the AI-called `getSelectedElements`, it still returns the full set of properties as before.

The helper functions now take an optional array of property names to show. A base set of properties, `id`, `type`, `x`, and `y`, are *always* included in the returned values, whether a filter is given or not, and whether any of those base properties are included in the filter or not. If no filter is given, the full original list of `WIDGET_PROPS_FOR_AI` is used.

AI Function calls / features changed to filter properties:
 - generate ideas now returns `text`
 - summarize now returns `text`
 - mindmap (create and update) now returns `text` (these results do not include the arrows, so there is no connection / hierarchy information lost)
 - sentiment-classification now returns `text` and `backgroundColor` (but also includes a function-specific list of widget ids that are positive, negative, etc.)
 - suggest-title now returns `text` (only the areas are returned, and `text` is the new title)
 - summarize now returns `text`
 - translate now returns `text`
 - create-shapes now returns `shapeType`, `text`, `width`, `height`, and `color`
 - create-tables only uses `width` and `height`, but that's just for the outer table widget, the cells are handled separately as before (with their own focused list of properties)
 - create-text now returns `text`, `height`, `width`, and `fontSize`
 - add to outline now returns `text`, `height`, `width`, and `backgroundColor` of

title: Fix focus trap panel issue
body:
Fixes issue in `MrlFocusTrap` where it could steal focus from an element outside the focus trap. If a non focus trapped element was focused and the focus trap got "destroyed", then focus would be move from the element back to the focus trap and become lost.

This issue can be reproduced in production if you click on a widget from a panel and begin to type, the typing will be interrupted by the autohide behavior because focus is lot. 

Testing env: http://focus-trap-panel-fix.mural.engineering

This fix adds checks to ensure we only move focus "on destroy" if:
- the actively focused element is within the focus trap
- the actively focused element is the body (I.e. focus is lost, and we won't be stealing it from somewhere)

title: [SCQM-1195] Add agentsTrace
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR adds `agentsTrace` support to the new agents endpoint call and messages received so they can be routed as needed and shown in the client when debugging.
This also adds a minor UX change to the AI Chat Inspector dev panel.

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**]() to understand the context of this effort.
- 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://scqm-1195-agents-trace.mural.engineering/) to perform a smoke test. ([all testing envs](https://testing-envs.mural.engineering))
Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes
1. Enable the Agents flag in the flags manager.
2. Open the AI Chat Inspector
3. Send any message in the AI Chat and wait for the response

title: [CAN-7680] Move `delete` action from the catalog to the `ActionBuilder` prototype
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This is a bit of a follow-up from [this PR](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/45059) where we replaced the `SingleWidgetActions` for actions within the `ActionBuilder`.

While the replacement of `create` and `recover` goes directly to a function within the `ActionBuilder` prototype (`new ActionBuilder().create()`), the deletion goes through the catalog (`new ActionBuilder().for(widget).delete()`).

This is counter-intuitive for a couple of reasons:
1. The intention of the catalog is to provide readable actions that work over a provided widget altering one or more of its properties.
   - In this sense, `delete` doesn't quite fit the category because it doesn't alter any property, it simply deletes the entire thing.
2. Actions in the catalog work over a widget, not over an id, whereas deletion doesn't need the widget at all, only the id.
3. Because of this, if we want it to continue working only with an id, we are forced to provide an instance of the `WidgetStore` to the `ActionBuilder`.
   - This is because, as mentioned, the actions in the catalog work over a widget, and when using an id as accessor, we need to have a way of fetching the widget from the id.
   - This is an overkill case for a deletion: we'd be providing an instance of the `WidgetStore` in order to fetch a widget by its id, only to then use just the very same id.

For these reasons, the easiest (and also cleanest) thing to do is to move `delete` to the `ActionBuilder` prototype, along `create` and `recover`.

This changes the usage from the quite complex case of:
```ts
const store = sdk.widgets.getStore();
const actions = new ActionBuilder(store)
  .for(myWidget.id)
  .delete();
```
to the easiest:
```ts
const actions = new ActionBuilder().delete(myWidget.id);
```

No behavioral change is expected at all, given that the generated change from both the catalog and the prototype actions are exactly the same.

title: [CAN-7678] Remove `SingleWidgetActions` in favor of using the `ActionBuilder`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

The `SingleWidgetActions` interface provides three methods: `create`, `delete` and `recover` that are nothing but a shortcut for generating a `WidgetCreateChange`, `WidgetDeleteChange` and `WidgetRecoverChange` respectively.

Originally, we conceived the `ActionBuilder` as a way of managing the accumulation of all updates that can be applied to an existing widget, and therefore we needed a way to easily generate the changes required for creating, deleting and recovering widgets.
Since those operations shouldn't really "accumulate", they weren't part of the `ActionBuilder`.

However, we changed that idea. While you usually don't want to accumulate a creation of a widget with an update of the widget (if you're gonna update something you just created, you should simply create it with the new property already in there), you probably do want to accumulate a creation of a widget with an update _of another widget_.

Therefore, the `ActionBuilder` now supports creation and deletion.

Because of this, we no longer need the `SingleWidgetActions` for this. And if we move `recover` there, we can remove them entirely.

#### What this PR does

Don't be confused by all this explanation. This PR doesn't _do_ anything, really.
It changes all instances of `SingleWidgetActions.create` for `new ActionBuilder().create`, instances of `SingleWidgetActions.delete` for `new ActionBuilder().for(widgetId).delete` and instances of `SingleWidgetActions.recover` for a new `new ActionBuilder().recover`.

The result is exactly the same, those methods return the exact same `WidgetChange` object. The only difference is that they are now cumulative with any other change we want to pile.

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The logic for repositioning children of a resized absorbing widget is currently split into two systems: one handling widgets with the `ALL_OR_NOTHING` strategy and one handling the rest of the cases (a.k.a. the `DEFAULT` strategy).

However, there's no real reason for splitting this that way. When an absorbing widget is resized every child should be repositioned to compensate the difference in relative position, regardless of its absorption strategy.

This PR, therefore, refactors this into one system that runs outside the context of absorption and independent of any strategy.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7669)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://reposition-children-system.mural.engineering)

### What to test?
This is unflagged code, meaning that it will affect every behavior.
Ideally there should be no change whatsoever, so what you should test for is the resizing of any absorbing widget (area, table, etc) containing children, specially when resizing from the top or left, which is what generates a change in the absorbing widget position.
The `repositionChildren` system should compensate this change, making the children seem immovable while resizing.

body:
In the near future there will be various demos introducing Muralistas to Copilot Instructions and encouraging broader contribution.

This carries some risks that should be controlled for with proper review:
- Copilot instructions **can and do** negatively interact with each other without proper targeting and optimization
- There is currently no way to automatically test the expected performance of instructions, so these negative interactions can happen silently and be very difficult to debug

Further reading: https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/master/.github/instructions/copilot-instructions-files.instructions.md

title: [SCQM-1171] Fix tags input auto focus
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Bug: When opening the tags menu, the input gets focus and then it immediately blurs. 
Fix: Added a timeout before focusing the input which prevents `MrlTooltip` from stealing focus on its initialization. This ensures the input reliably receives focus after the tooltip is rendered. Also implemented `forwardRef` to ensure input focus is controlled by the parent component instead of being managed by both parent and child components.

title: [SCQM-968] Replaces ai canSelects with selectors for better performance
body:
# [SCQM-968] Convert AI validation functions to performance-optimized selectors

## Problem
The AI validation functions `canSummarize`, `canAIAutoCluster`, and `canClassifyBySentiment` are computationally heavy and impact app performance when users interact with AI features, particularly when opening the widget toolbar repeatedly. These functions perform expensive widget filtering operations without any caching mechanism.

## Solution

- Refactored AI clustering, summarization, and sentiment classification utils to use selector-style utilities with reselect for improved performance and memoization.
- Updated import statements to include reselect and relevant selectors in affected modules.
- Replaced direct function calls like getAIClusterableChildren, getAIClusterableWidgets, and getAISummarizableWidgets with selector-based equivalents (e.g., selectGetAIClusterableChildren, selectAISummarizableWidgets).
- Enhanced canAIAutoCluster and canSummarize to use new selector-based logic, including stricter validation (e.g., requiring at least 2 clusterables for AI auto-clustering).
- Introduced selectAISentimentClassifiableWidgets selector and updated canClassifyBySentiment to use it.
- Added selectFilterWidgetsAndChildren and related selector helpers in src/mural/sdk/primitives/widgets/selectors.ts for filtering widgets and their descendants in a memoized way.
- Improved documentation and code comments, especially around the new selectors and their usage.
- Minor cleanups and consistency improvements in function parameter ordering and code structure.

## Benefits

- **Performance improvement**: Memoized calculations prevent redundant widget filtering
- **Better UX**: Faster AI widget toolbar interactions and responsiveness
- **Maintainable architecture**: Centralized AI validation logic in selectors
- **Backward compatibility**: All existing functionality preserved without breaking changes

title: [CAN-7631]  Fix Mouse Event Handling in EmptySpaceCaretPlugin
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This pull request refactors the caret positioning logic for the empty space caret plugin in the Lexical widget editor. The main improvements include extracting caret calculation and movement into dedicated utility files, simplifying event handling, and improving test coverage. These changes enhance code clarity, modularity, and maintainability.

Before this changes, the plugin was broken.

**Caret Positioning Logic Refactor:**

* Extracted the caret position calculation into a new utility file `calculate-caret-position.ts` with improved documentation and logic using `Aabb` for center calculation.
* Extracted caret movement logic into a new utility file `move-caret-to.ts`, providing a clear API for moving the caret to the start or end of the editor.

**Plugin Component and Event Handling Simplification:**

* Reimplemented the main plugin component in `index.tsx`, using a new custom hook for event handling and integrating the new caret utilities, resulting in more readable and maintainable code.
* Simplified and clarified mouse/touch event handling, with improved hit testing and keyboard interaction management.

**Testing Improvements:**

* Added dedicated tests for both caret position calculation (`calculate-caret-position.test.tsx`) and caret movement (`move-caret-to.test.ts`), ensuring robust coverage of the new utilities. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-43236b8870f2d8fa09ca2cc86f54c6b14cf7abe1ab7c4846409a57cfbfb11afbL3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ba846b676382cc2ef3f66483d59e453747a3fc318805ec1e01b844614d027f75R1-R57)

**Code Cleanup:**

* Removed the old monolithic `empty-space-caret-plugin.tsx` file, splitting responsibilities into smaller, focused modules.

title: fix: Activate EmptySpaceCaretPlugin only for mobile browsers
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

    Prior to these changes: The EmptySpaceCaretPlugin was rendered on all platforms . This caused the plugin to intercept mouse events on desktop and other non-mobile platforms, preventing users from dragging widgets because the plugin would prioritize moving the text caret instead of allowing drag interactions to occur.

    Now, with these changes: The EmptySpaceCaretPlugin is only rendered on mobile-web devices. This preserves the critical caret placement functionality where it's most needed (mobile browsers with touch interfaces), while restoring proper widget dragging behavior on desktop and other platforms where mouse-based dragging is the primary interaction pattern and the caret plugin was interfering with expected user workflows.

title: [CAN-7628] Fix format buttons out of sync when no text is selected
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

    Prior to these changes, format toolbar buttons (bold, italic, underline) did not reflect the current format when selection was empty (collapsed/caret only). The `$getSelectionFormat()` function would return `null` for collapsed selections due to a guard that checked if `selection.getTextContent() === ''`, preventing the MuralIntegrationPlugin from reporting the current format and color at the caret position.
    
    Now, with these changes, the toolbar buttons accurately reflect the formatting at the caret position even when no text is selected. The function now reads format information from collapsed selections, ensuring the plugin properly reports the current format state and providing users with an accurate visual representation of the formatting that will be applied when they start typing.

title: [CAN-7597] Fix format on editing selected text
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer


    Prior to these changes when a user wrote text after selecting a mixed formatted content, only the first letter inherited the format
    Now, with these changes, all the text gets the format of the selection start. 

This was a fix that already had existed but it was removed in the  [QuickEdit PR](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/44025)

The origin of the bug comes from Lexical itself and is still happening.
What we are doing here is a workaround for [Select All does not populate Selection.style / format correctly](https://github.com/facebook/lexical/issues/6407).

In this PR I'm adding a test to check that the workaround works and another one to check if is still needed. 
So whenever we update Lexical, the test will validate that the bug is still happening an the workaround still works.

title: [CAN-7576] Absorption system for freeform area resizing
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR introduces the first version of the `DEFAULT` absorption system.

This system will handle the absorption logic for all widgets with a `DEFAULT` strategy. 
As of right now, this means widgets that do not follow an `ALL_OR_NOTHING` logic (i.e. mindmaps).

**Keep in mind that all this code is behind the flag `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS`**

This first approach will only handle one specific use case: resizing a free-form area over or out of a sticky note.

The intention with this first approach is to extend the existing logic for `ALL_OR_NOTHING` in a way that can be re-used for the `DEFAULT` strategy, and having a simple use case to begin with allows for an easy testing of the changes.
If all works fine and as expected, we can then expand the restrictions step by step until we cover all cases.

In order to accomplish the following changes are introduced:
- We already had an interface for defining functions used by the core absorption logic. This remains the same but is renamed as a `service`, because that's more accurate to what they represent.
- The service is then adapted to be a class that's initialized with the required parameters. This way we can use the same instance for all the sub-systems that compose the absorption logic.
- By providing the system arguments to the service we can have the core logic consume it without caring about the internal requirements of each function.
- The method that asserts if we're dealing with an affecting operation has also been translated to the service
- With all these changes adapted and seamlessly for the `ALL_OR_NOTHING` strategy, we're ready to implement the `DEFAULT` version.
- The core logic is now agnostic of strategies and internal requirements, so the `DEFAULT` strategy simply needs to implement its own service.

## Pull Request Overview

This pull request improves the Copilot instructions by refining coding guidelines to be more flexible and practical. The changes shift from strict requirements to recommended practices, making the guidelines more developer-friendly while maintaining code quality standards.

Key changes:
- Relaxed JSDoc documentation requirements from mandatory to recommended for exported functions
- Enhanced event handler naming conventions with clearer prop vs. handler distinctions

- Added styling guidelines emphasizing design system usage over custom styles

For future optimization, the domain-specific contents of this file should eventually be broken up into their own `*.instructions.md` files with appropriate `applyTo` targeting.

This top-level, always-in-context `copilot-instructions.md` is probably best used for:
- Repo-level documentation — project overview, tech stack, directory structure, command line scripts

title: [CAN-7622] Fix: prevent editor re-initialization when format changes in Lexical plugin
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer


    Prior to these changes, the Lexical editor would re-initialize and reset user content to the initialText whenever the format prop changed, causing users to lose their typed content when text formatting was applied. (For quick-editions)
    
    Now, with these changes, the editor preserves user content when format changes occur by excluding the format prop from the useEffect dependencies that control editor initialization, preventing unwanted content resets while maintaining proper format handling.

This pull request improves the stability of the `MuralIntegrationPlugin` in the Lexical editor by ensuring that changing the `format` prop does not unintentionally reset the editor content. It also adds a test to verify this behavior.

**Testing improvements:**

* Added a test to `plugin.test.tsx` to confirm that changing the `format` prop does not reset the editor content to `initialText`.
* Imported `$createParagraphNode` and `$createTextNode` to support the new test.

**Bug fix:**

* Updated the dependency array of the effect in `plugin.tsx` to exclude `format`, preventing unwanted re-initialization of editor content when `format` changes.

title: [CAN-7575] Refactor copy/paste with absorption
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes a weird bug when enabling the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag:
Copying and pasting any widget (wether there was an area involved or not) would cause the pasted widget to be placed in a random place:

![Jul-22-2025 15-06-20](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14202a0c-03e2-483f-a693-f97de7937d4d)

The reason this happened is because a function called `fixPositionToBounds` was early returning when the flag was enabled.

**But what is this function? And what is it for?**

`fixPositionToBounds` is triggered every time we copy a widget.
Its job is to normalize the widget position in relation to the mural, so the entire bound of selected widgets always start at (0, 0) instead of where they were originally placed in the mural.

We assumed the flag was needed because it's doing some parenting assigning, but here's what that assignment is for:
When we copy an absorbed widget and don't include the parent in the clipboard data, we need to normalize the position based on its global coords instead of the relative it has, because it won't have the parent anymore when pasted.
And when we do include the parent, since the parent will already have a normalized position and the widget will keep its parenting relationship, we don't need to do anything, the position it already has in the model is good enough.

The reason we added this early return there is because the code was a bit hard to follow in its intention and the way to accomplish it, so in this PR I'm removing the unnecessary early return but I'm also cleaning the function up so it's more easy to understand what it's doing.

The expected outcome of this is that the copy/pasting should behave exactly as it does when the flag is disabled (because nothing changed there), and when it's enabled it should copy and paste everything correctly, but should not generate any new absorption or expulsion behavior.

[SCQM-729] Remove users vote if not successfully broadcast to all users
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
We believe an underlying issue with voting where the optimistic front end update sometimes gets out of sync with the backend's persisting / broadcasting of that vote. 

This means there are occasionally bugs where the voting session appears to have different vote counts across different user UIs in the same voting session.  It is hard to reproduce and we think would require a large investment in voting to truly fix / voting needs much more robust error handling. 

So this solution is just to try to avoid the issue altogether - by looking at the vote count returned by the backend we can tell if it was not broadcast and remove the optimistic update & let the user know there was an error at a high level.

title: [CAN-7344] Remove `afterAbsorption` hook
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The connector's `afterAbsorption` hook handler that we're removing in this PR had one job: to send all the connected connectors to the front when the widgets they were connected to were getting absorbed into an area.

In plain english: every time there is an absorption of widgets, this code would check for any arrow connected to what was getting absorbed, and was sending those arrows to the front of the stacking order.

Now, we have already in place a system that manages this exact same thing: the `stackingConnectorsSystem` will check, upon any update, if any arrow involved with the updated widgets are connected to widgets in an area, and in such case, will bring those arrows to the front.

Same thing, except that this ones run as a system upon any update and the other was a handler hooked to the absorption behavior.

However, the absorption behavior that would trigger this hook are using the `changes` API to perform the action, so the system _is_ running and handling the situation before it reaches this handler.

Therefore, the handler is not needed.

This was, incidentally, the only handler registered for the `afterAbsorption` hook. So without any reason to exist, the hook is removed as well.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7344)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://after-absorption-hook.mural.engineering)

### What to test for?
Basically, you should test that arrows never get behind an area **when they are connected to widgets that are inside said area** (this is important... you could still potentially get an arrow behind an area if they are not connected to any widget, and that's expected).

title: Play 485 widget spacing for AI Org Chart
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

[Jira Ticket](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/PLAY-485)
[Loom](https://www.loom.com/share/8d986579826f4d9e877d3f1f0246a465)

This pull request introduces a new "org chart" layout mode to the grid computation logic for rendering widgets in the `mermaid` addon. It also includes enhancements for widget placement and rendering logic. The most significant changes are the addition of the "org chart" layout, modifications to handle LinkedIn profile widgets, and improvements to widget height preservation.

### Grid computation enhancements:
* Introduced a new "org chart" layout mode in `computeGridLayout` to support parent-anchored layouts with adaptive spacing based on subtree widths. This includes logic for positioning root nodes, calculating subtree widths, and handling multiple children with appropriate horizontal and vertical spacing (`src/mural/addons/mermaid/compute-grid.ts`).

### Rendering logic updates:
* Added detection of LinkedIn profile widgets in `mermaidRender` and enabled the "org chart" layout mode when such widgets are present. This ensures that LinkedIn profile nodes are rendered using the new parent-anchored layout (`src/mural/addons/mermaid/render.ts`). title: [CAN-7605] Deprecate `widgets.update`
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer With the `Widget Changes API` now fully documented and actively working, we need to slowly begin the movement of the code from the `widgets.update` approach to the new `widgets.changes.apply` (and `commit`) one. The first commit moves the register params into a single object and updates the existing ActionRegistrations

title: [CAN-7568] Prevent wrong behavior when duplicating multiple times
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a continuation of the work done in https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/44666.
The reported issue there was that duplicating a mural by double clicking would create two copies and make the last one unusable.

The fix attacked the action that triggered the bug, but not the actual root cause of it.

So here's the deal:

The TL;DR version of what happened is that the function that uploads any widget creation or modification to the backend, which is based in Ampersand, uses an instance of the `SdkContext` that is specifically initialized for all ampersand leftovers functions (the infamous "amp helpers").
What was happening here was that this instance was nullified, and thus we couldn't execute any persisting action on the widgets.

Now if you want to know _why_ this happened, then let me welcome you to the amazing labyrinth that is the loading of the `MuralRoute`.

I'm not gonna get too deep into the details, because I ignore them myself, but this is what happens when we load a mural, in a nutshell:
We start off by loading a `Preview` component, which does the actual loading while showing us a snapshot.
When the loading is finished, we call a function named `onEnterMural`.

This function will fetch the user and the workspace, and after that's done it will render the `MuralRoute` component.
The mounting of the `MuralRoute` component will initialize the `SdkContext` and set it for the amp helpers.

Here's where it gets interesting: the fetching of the workspace executes this call: `setSdkContextForAmpHelpers(undefined)`, which is totally fine because the `MuralRoute` component will afterwards set it with an actual value anyway.

Except when we load two murals at once and start a really annoying race condition.
Since fetching the workspace is an async operation, loading the first mural will fetch the first workspace, null the sdk, load the `MuralRoute` and set the sdk back again.
But

title: [CAN-7573] [CAN-7574] Refactor resize to work on local coordinates
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR fixes two bugs at once, both of them only reproducible with the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag enabled: _This PR:_
Resizing a widget inside an area Resizing multiple widgets inside an area
_App:_
Resizing a widget inside an area Resizing multiple widgets inside an area
--- The reason both these bugs happened was related to two main concepts that the resizing is based on: 1. Every widget is removed from its parent before the resizing starts 2. The only exception is when the parent is also part of the selection These two premises are true with the flag disabled but lose their veracity when we enable it. The problem is that the code is not _checking_ for this conditions, it's assuming them to be true and act upon that premise. This means that it's using global coordinates without checking if they are truly global or local, and even worst, since widgets are expelled before resizing starts, it uses the information of whether a widget has a parent or not as confirmation that the parent is also part of the selection. So instead of patching things up to be aware of this situation, what I'm doing here is refactor the code to not rely at all on these premises. The code will no longer assume stuff but rather base its behavior on the model data alone. This means that: 1. Instead of getting global coordinates and use that assuming that they match local v

title: [CAN-7488] Conditionally set `confirmDeleteParentWithContent` in widget step
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR hacks its way through the `deleteWidget` method in the undo redo `WidgetStep`. When undoing the deletion of an area or framework, we will always delete the container. It was deleting everything before.

Tables do not have a problem because they are always deleted with all the content inside. 

The proper fix would be to refactor `deleteWidgets`. The reason this is happening is because we're using the same business rule for deleting widgets and redoing a deletion, which is not correct, and the `deleteWidgets` business rule needs some love because it's very hard to follow. Ideally we shouldn't be running systems on undo/redo, we should be storing the changes in the undo stack, but doing it requires a whole other effort to cleanup `deleteWidgets`.

Unfortunately I can't seem to get the `undo/redo` to work properly in the testing rig.

The proper test to write is:

```
Scenario: undo deleting an area only with content
    Given a selected area A
    And an arrow ARROW in A
    When pressing [Delete]
    And clicking the [Area only] button in the modal
    And executing an undo
    And executing a redo
    Then the widgets count is 1
    And the arrow ARROW at properties.parentId is null
```

However the widget count is 0 only in the rig, in fact in the previous test clicking the `Area only` button works fine, which leads to think that the `redo` step is the problem.

title: [ENGAGE-953] Remove unused state from room
body:
## Primary:
Replace usage of old `Item` and `MenuItem` with new card actions `Action`.

### Secondary: 
Refactor RoomV2/index and RoomView components to have _two_ methods for handling the opening of modals. One for mural modals and one for room/dashboard modals. 
Reasoning: As I started replace `Item` with `Action` the only single method `handleOpenModal()` was complicating the logic to set modals because the modal param could be an Action object _or_ a string modal name.
While trying to make sense of the logic, I realized that it would be clearer if there were two separate functions.... one for handling the "open" of a mural modal which always takes an Action and a muralId....and one for handling the open of room modals that only takes the string modal "name".
Additionally, I realized that there were some fields/func thats were typed for a string that "magically" working even when an Action was passed because the logic was casting `modal: Action | string` as a string :yikes:

#### Other cleanup:
* Removed unused class component state fields and/or objects
* Removed two old PropType definitions that were only used to define the type for a `context` prop in dashboard/grid/murals.tsx. 

Note:
Commits are fairly ordered and can help make sense of the PR as a whole

and the engine for measuring dynamic elements like the height of the
text. This resulted in very slight discrepancies between what murally

title: Remove `sdk.widgets.updateMultiple`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
We've created `updateMultiple` some time ago as a first step towards what became the `Widget Changes API`.
The intention was to provide a way of updating multiple widgets at once in one call.

However, before we could tell the world about this method and push for people to implement it, we started really using the changes api, which offers the possibility of updating multiple widgets at once right out of the box.

Therefore, this method died before it was even born.

However, some minor usages got to be implemented, not that many.

So in order to really impulse the usage of the `Widget Changes API`, we first need to remove these small cases and delete `updateMultiple`.

The only change this will bring is that the cases where this was being used will now run the set of systems after the update, which should have no negative impact.

But just in case, you should try out the following actions:
- Set a theme to a set of widgets, both grouped and ungrouped
- Use AI to do a spell check in the text of some widgets

That's it 😄 if both those things work, then everything should be good

🌎 **Test env**: https://update-multiple.mural.engineering/

title: [CAN-7577] Fix quick text edition breaking the widget migration
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR prevents the quick text edition from breaking the widget migration process (from plain text to rich text)

The rationale behind this PR is that we used to mount the editor on _selection_ (aka pre-edition) to be ready for the caret position query once the editor is mounted (i.e. the next click);

This logic has now changed (https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/44685) and this now happens within the editor itself.

This means that there are no longer any reason to prematurely mount the editor, which fixes this issue and homogenize the edition flow between quick and legacy edition.

title: [CAN-7572] Areas not resizing when absorption flag is on
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes the resizing of areas when the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag is enabled.

The reason this didn't work was that we were preventing the `ResizeFreeformArea` business rule from executing entirely when the flag was enabled.

This business rule handles both the absorption of widgets into freeform areas as well as the proper resizing of the area itself.

The fix consists in moving the code that does the resizing outside the business rule and run it unflagged, but some extra adjustments needed to be done because we were wrongly handling absorption of arrows within this `ResizeFreeformArea` business rule, which should not happen because we have an unflagged system for that.


#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7572)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://area-resize-flagged.mural.engineering)

**What to check for:**
- Make sure the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag is enabled.
- Create an area and try to resize it.
- Don't mind the fact that it won't absorb or expel anything, that's expected at this point. It should, nonetheless, resize properly.

title: [ENGAGE-953] Replace use of old Item type with new card-actions Action type.
body:
## Replace usage of `../ui/callout/menu Item` type in Dashboard's cards with `../universal-card/card-actions/card-actions Action` type.

This is originally for consistency, so that all consumers of CardActions can use a single type, instead of a different types that _happen_ to overlap.

Additional benefit.... now that CardActions component no longer references code from the main `src/` tree, it will be able to move to a package in a future pr.

Another benefit... the old action definitions (room-actions and template-actions) were unnecessarily, and confusingly, defining an `icon` property for each action. This property was ignored by the underlying CardActions component as it uses the `label` property to do a lookup in a the `SvgLookup` map. While it might be nice to have the definitions define the icon directly, this PR removes the currently unused code. When we refactor in the future, we'll benefit from not having to figure out _which_ icon is used.

### Templates Note :
There we some tests that expected the `icon` to be part of object passed to `modal.open()`. This PR removes those icons from the definition and from the test assertions.

### Not in this PR
There's probably other refactoring that we could do in this code to simplify or more more readable. I saw some things as I changed the types but decided to keep this PR focused only the type change. Additional refactorings can happen in future PRs

title: [CAN-7472] Change group/ungroup stacking order behavior

**Important**: while this PR is divided in such a way that each commit moves one interface at a time, review will be much easier if we just take a look at the final diff instead of analyzing each individual change.

---

This PR moves the typings for the `RenderEngine` to a package called `canvas-engine-types`.

This only moves the definitions we use across the entire murally codebase from the `sdk` folder to their own package.

title: Move `asset-management` library to a package
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR moves the entire `asset-management` library to a package. There's not that much to say, the library was already modularized in such a way that it had no external dependencies other than other external libraries, so the movement was pretty straight-forward.

The reason for this is that the `RenderEngine` types have a reference to this library, and in order to move that into a package we first need to isolate this one.

Given that this had several files, the movement is being done one file per commit, addressing the references needed on each commit to keep the code consistent at all times.

You can either review this commit by commit or by looking at the differences, it's pretty much the same.

I would suggest looking at the diffs directly because it'll be far easier.

🌎 **Test env**: https://asset-management-package.mural.engineering

title: [CAN-7525] Evolved navigation callouts scheduler
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer [Jira](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7525) [mural-api](https://github.com/tactivos/mural-api/pull/14039) This PR adds "version" property to the `User Controls` and integrates it across the codebase to support the "Navigation Improvements" feature. It also includes tracking events, and callout handling for this feature. ### New Feature: Navigation Evolved * Added a `version` property to the `Controls` interface, defaulting to `null`, and updated all relevant configurations and normalization logic to include this property. * Introduced a new callout, "navigation evolved". Applying changes will set the user to the new controls version to `v1`. Postponing will trigger a callout the next calendar day. * Introduced a new callout, "navigation how did it go". Reverting will downgrade the user's version and trigger a callout on the next monday. ### Callout Scheduler! * Added a callout scheduler SDK API that manages timed navigation callouts by persisting scheduled dates in user storage and automatically triggering them at the specified times. It provides methods to schedule callouts for next Monday at 9AM, next day at 9AM, or 3 seconds from now, with built-in functionality to check scheduled callouts every 5 seconds, queue them when their time arrives, and automatically remove them after triggering. title: [CAN-7369] Refactor absorption strategies
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR focuses on the absorption system logic that we already have for widgets following the `ALL_OR_NOTHING` strategy and refactors the code in order to generalize the algorithms that handle the absorption per se so they don't rely on any specific strategy.

The way we do this here is by abstracting the functions that change depending on the strategy from the implementation itself.

So... basically... we implement a strategy design pattern.

This is only about moving things around and abstracting concepts.

No logic or behavior changes whatsoever.

This shouldn't affect anything but the absorption of mindmaps (and, truth be told, it shouldn't affect that at all, really)

title: [ENGAGE-978] Move Duplicate, Info, and Insights mural modals into ActionsManager pattern.
body:
## tl/dr 
Move the definitions and click events for mural card actions to new files that define ActionManager registrations.
Add new dashboard event pub/sub mechanism to allow for Duplicate action to broadcast MURAL_DUPLICATED after the api is called, thus enabling each page to do their own special handling (eg tracking and navigation)

Duplicate Registration - moved out of src/dashboard/grid/mural-actions.tsx and in to it's own file `src/apps/web/dashboard/mural-actions/duplicate-menu-registration.tsx`

Insights Registration - moved out of src/dashboard/grid/mural-actions.tsx and in to it's own file `src/apps/web/dashboard/mural-actions/insights-registration.tsx`
* While moving this, I discovered that `handleToggleMuralInsights()` was longer duplicated on every page that renders mural cards. We now only have on location for this logic (in insights-registration.tsx)

DashboardMuralEvents store for a decoupled way to communicate changes.
(More on this down in the dependency change section)
This store allows for components in the dashboard to broadcast events (with payload) to any other components that wish to listen for the event. This is a lightweight pub/sub pattern that is exposed to dashboard components from the DashboardMuralEventsStore.Provider in DashboardContainer.

title: Remove `dispatcherForChristsSakeDontUseThis`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
You see that PR title? You can surely understand why we needed to do this, right?

Historically, we were sending an instance to the `MuralDispatcher` everywhere where we needed it, regardless of whether that complied with our expected architecture or not.

At some point in time we stopped and thought: "wait, this is not ok".
So we tried to fix most of the cases, but some of them were too complex.

To avoid spreading the problem even further, we thought about renaming the wrong export to `dispatcherForChirstsSakeDontUseThis`, a name that should, at first glance, make you think twice before using it.

We currently have just two use cases for that accessor: one is in the testing rig (which can very easily be replaced with a call to a business rule) and the other one... oh God, the other one.

---

So, here's the deal: the other case is a call inside the method `ampPatchWidget`, a method that is being executed upon _**doing anything at all with any widget**_.

Yeah...

Now, within that method, we do have some extra conditions before using the dispatcher: the update must have a property called `text` with some content.

This is, of course, really old legacy code that nobody ever touched.
Why am I saying this? Because we have almost no widgets with the `text` property anymore.

This used to affect all text-based widgets, but most of them now use the `htmlText` property, not `text`, and nobody ever complained about any of this not working.

Why is that? Well because the only thing we're doing here when a `text` property is updated is toggling the private time feedback.

But we also do that as part of the effects computation when we update the engine through the engine bridge.
So this works exactly the same regardless of that call. We still toggle the private time feedback when needed.

But don't believe me, try it out yourself in the testing environment.
This should only affect `TitleWidge

title: [FEP-5822] React 18 Upgrade
body:
## React 18 Upgrade 🥳

Test env: https://react-18.mural.engineering

![arresteddevelopment-its-happening](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ca4a321-f1ca-4ecf-958e-1bda22e582aa)

This PR **finally upgrades** `murally` to React 18 — along with its associated dependencies — and fixes the resulting destruction that ensued. 

### Dependency Updates 🥇

The following dependencies have been updated in all `package.json` files:

- `react`: `17.0.2` → `18.2.0`
- `react-dom`: `17.0.2` → `18.2.0`
- `@testing-library/react`: `12.1.5` → `13.4.0`
- `@testing-library/react-hooks`: _removed_ (now built into `@testing-library/react`)
- Associated type packages for all of the above have been updated

### Fixing the Fallout ☢️

To make `murally` compatible with React 18, the work breaks down into the following areas:

- Upgrade of project and package dependencies
- Update of existing components to use React 18 types
- Code modifications to align with changes to React APIs
- Test fixes (more on that below 👇)

Many of the changes involve updates to type interfaces — specifically, ensuring any component that expects `children` now explicitly uses `PropsWithChildren`.

### Tests!!! 🧪

A significant portion of this PR is dedicated to fixing test failures caused by the React 18 upgrade. React 18 introduced changes in how concurrency is handled — particularly [automatic batching of state updates](https://react.dev/blog/2022/03/29/react-v18#new-feature-automatic-batching). This required many tests to be updated to correctly account for asynchronous behavior.

- **Unit tests** (~100 failures):  
  Mostly fixed by updating how async behavior is handled — switching `screen.getBy` to `await screen.findBy`, using `waitFor`, or wrapping assertions in `act`.

- **Test Rig 1** (~78 failures):  
  Fixed primarily by updating Cucumber scenarios for async correctness.

- **Test Rig 2** (~1200 failures):  
  - ~400 tests fixed by updating step definitions

title: [CAN-7512] Fix arrow flashing when resizing over an area
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes the following bug:

1. Create an area
2. Add some arrows
3. Select all the arrows
4. Resize the selection

**Expected result**: The arrows should be resized smoothly
**Actual result**: A nasty flashing appears on each resizing step

---

_Fixed version (this PR):_
![Jul-15-2025 16-05-00](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a0652d4-f650-44b4-927e-5eb05cd99e10)

_Master version:_
![Jun-30-2025 14-55-22](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0eaa5bea-4748-45f6-a5d9-bfba0e20b7e9)

---
The reason this happened was due to how we handle the concept of resizing and absorption when it comes to arrows.

For regular widgets, whenever we resize something that is absorbed, during this transitional resizing step we expel the widget from its parent, and then, if it corresponds, re-absorb it back after it's dropped.

However, arrows work differently. Since the absorption for them is handled by a system, there's no such a thing as a "transitional resizing state". If an arrow needs to be absorbed, it will be.

So, during this resize, we were going back and forth through a situation where we treated the position as global and relative over and over again, causing in a flashing of the arrow being moved out and into the area.

The proper solution will come after absorption works the same way for all widgets, but for now we address the situation by excluding arrows from that initial logic and making sure that we always treat their positions as relative.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7512)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://arrow-resizing.mural.engineering)

title: [CAN-7511] Fix arrow duplication inside areas
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes the following bug:

1. Create an area
2. Draw an arrow inside the area
3. Drag the arrow holding down `Cmd` to duplicate

**Expected result**: The arrow should get duplicated
**Actual result**: Nothing happens

---

_Fixed version (this PR):_
![Jul-15-2025 12-35-07](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd1b5bd5-0634-4b9f-ba83-908eb55d00c8)

_Master version:_
![Jun-30-2025 14-48-40](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/294bd642-b2b6-4f62-8d47-584015f2c5ed)

---
The reason this happened was due to the arrow absorption being implemented as a system.

The code for duplicating a dragging widget is prepared to sanitize the duplicated widget in a way that it ends up being orphan, and then it selects the duplicated widget by filtering those added widgets that don't have a parent.

This code started failing for arrows because, even if we create an arrow as an orphan widget, the mere creation inside an area will make the system absorb it, so it won't be orphan.
By not selecting it the duplication ends up being cancelled, and that caused the problem.

This is something that, eventually, will end up affecting all widgets after we move absorption to be a system on all cases.
When that time comes the entire flow of how duplication from dragging works should need to be refactored, but for now we can simply manually add the arrows to the selection with a comment that explains why.

---

I also took this opportunity to migrate the suite of tests for this that were part of the rig 1 to be run in the rig 2

---

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7511)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://arrow-duplicating.mural.engineering)

title: Rename `action-builder` folder to `actions`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a simple one commit PR for one specific purpose: renaming the folder `action-builder` inside the `WidgetChanges` SDK API folder to `actions`, and the `index.ts` in that folder to `action-builder.ts`.

The reason for this change is related to an ongoing effort to document the entire API and its parts.

The folder `action-builder` contains a catalog of multiple widget actions and then an entry point where the `ActionBuilder` class is defined.
However, although we use the actions and the action builder in conjunction, the actions are, by themselves, pure functions that translate a user intention into a set of widget changes, and they do conform the vast majority of the content of that folder.
The `ActionBuilder`, however, is a mere tool to chain and group actions together, and is only defined in the `index.ts` file.

For that reason, it makes more sense if the folder itself is called `actions`, and the `ActionBuilder` is defined in it as one of the provided tools for the usage of actions.

Every single change in this PR is related to this renaming, so the only thing you'll see here, besides the change in the folder's name, is the fixing of all the imports to the new path.

* Refactored the test for confidential rooms to use `createMockRoomFromFieldsWithOverrides` and `renderWithOverrides`, maintaining consistency across tests.

title: Small "here and there" refactors on the `changes` api
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR, while it looks like it's a massive thing, it's actually a really simple and small refactor.

We're doing two things here:
1. Removing and cleaning up options and types that we never used in the `changes` api.
2. Move all the code related to the `WidgetChange` object inside the `changes` api.

This last change is what makes this look massive, because it affects a lot of files, but all the changes there are only about the path of an import.

The reason for this is twosome:
1. Keep all the code that's actually defined and related to the `changes` api in one place for when we move this into a package.
2. Allow for a complete documentation of the api and all its parts by putting them all in one place (coming up)

No changes are expected whatsoever because we're only removing unused code and moving things around.
If it compiles, we're good.

title: Add new Import Types (svg/zip) flagged
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This pull request introduces support for importing new file types (SVG and ZIP) in addition to PDFs, contingent on a feature flag. The changes include updates to the file import logic, user interface, and utility functions to handle these new file types.

⚠️ Disclaimer ⚠️ : The code allows the new types but without any fancy client-side validations (ie, is a valid SVG or if the ZIP is not encrypted, etc). It's just opening new formats to be available for selection.

#### Feature flag and file type support:

* Added a new feature flag `enableImportNewTypes` to the `FeatureFlags` interface in `workspaces.ts` to control the availability of importing SVG and ZIP files.
* Created a new utility function `isSupportedImportFile` to replace the previous `isPdfFile` function, enabling checks for multiple file types. This function uses a newly defined constant `SOURCE_FILE_SUPPORTED_TYPES` (`pdf`, `svg`, `zip`).

#### Updates to `PdfImportModal`:

* Modified the `PdfImportModal` component to dynamically adjust file type validation, drag-and-drop behavior, and input acceptance based on the `enableImportNewTypes` feature flag. This includes changes to file input handling, error checking, and user interface text. 
* Updated the `isPdfFileEncrypted` utility to use the new `isSupportedImportFile` function for file type validation.

#### UI enhancements:

* Updated the "Import from PDF" menu option in the dashboard sidebar to reflect the new supported file types when the feature flag is enabled.

### Reviewer Resources
Closes: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CWI-1919
TestEnv: https://new-import-types-ff.mural.engineering/

title: [CAN-7520] Potentially fix flaky tests
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
You know how it is with flaky tests... can you really say that this is _"a fix to a flaky test"_?

This PR contains some bits and modifications that aim to reduce the flakiness of some reported tests that are making the top 20 that nobody wants to be proud of.

So here's what I found so far, and what I did:

1. `Add immediate throttle on table tests`
All the files in the folder `features/canvas/widgets/table/copy-paste/` had a fail or two on almost every CI run, so I couldn't say that there was _one_ flaky test.
After some analysis, the thing that they all have in common is that, since they test the copy-paste operation, pretty much all of them are clicking a table cell to select it and make it the destination cell for a pasting.
Now, the selection of a table cell by clicking goes through the custom mouse processor that the `table` addon has.
This mouse processor uses a throttled logic to only listen to mouse events every 60 fps.
So... without the testing rig mocking the `throttle` to be immediate, we were risking some clicks to be lost every now and then.
This is what this commit addresses.

2. `Add default zone to initialization mural`
When we define a new mural in the rig, we don't assign any particular `zone` to it.
However, the code for pasting a widget from the clipboard is checking wether the mural's `zone` matches the encryption data in the clipboard widget. And to generate this encryption data, we use the mural's `zone`.
So, in this case, you would think that, by not setting it, both values should match to `undefined`, right?
Right?
Wrong, because the code for copying a widget is setting a default value when the mural has no `zone`. So this is no longer a comparison of `undefined === undefined`, but rather a comparison of `undefined === [default_value]`.
By not passing this condition, we enter a strange piece of code with async promises that may or may not be fulfilled on time, who k

title: ENGAGE-951 Use ui-toolkit- Replace old Card Actions Menu with ui-toolkit MrlMenu
body:
This pull request introduces several changes to the `dashboard` and `legacy-ui` packages, focusing on simplifying the codebase, improving maintainability, and updating tests. Key updates include replacing the `MuralLocationPositionWrapper` with a new `MuralLocationCardContextWrapper`, removing unused components, and enhancing the test suite for better coverage and accuracy.

Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/ENGAGE-951

Test Env: https://universal-card.mural.engineering/

![Screenshot 2025-07-08 at 5 32 25 PM 1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4982f0f1-4a31-4326-8605-a9f18adea627)

![Screenshot 2025-07-08 at 5 32 51 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c3a6a85-dd6d-462b-97e8-fe3371bdb878)

![Screenshot 2025-07-08 at 5 42 44 PM 1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62d93bce-2269-410b-adb9-43dc10cd53b8)

### Component Refactoring and Simplification:
* Removed the `MuralLocationPositionWrapper` component and replaced its functionality with the new `MuralLocationCardContextWrapper`, which simplifies the logic for rendering the `MuralLocation` component. 

### Dashboard Menu Updates:
* Updated the `Action` component to remove the `allowsOver` prop and related hover behavior, replacing it with a `popover` prop for rendering contextual overlays. 
* Adjusted the `MenuItem` interface to support the new `popover` prop and removed the deprecated `allowsOver` property. 

### Test Suite Enhancements:
* Updated test cases in `template-card.test.tsx` to replace `toBeVisible` assertions with `toBeInTheDocument` for better compatibility with the latest testing-library practices. 
* Removed redundant test cases in `card-actions.test.tsx` to align with the updated component logic. 

These changes collectively streamline the codebase, reduce unnecessary complexity, and ensure the test suite is up-to-date with modern practices.

title: [SCQM-1033] - Unremovable columns in planner fix, update verify-board tool
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes a customer bug where columns in a planner they created showed up in the info panel and took up space in the. board after being deleted, and could not be 'deleted' further. The issue was caused by a mismatch in column data likely caused by a race condition between the various delete functions - the column widgets themselves had been deleted, but they were not deleted from content extension data, causing the board to still act as if they were part of the board. 

The fix involves three pieces:

1. Removing some circular logic from the column delete flow. We were calling `deleteWidgets` in `handleColumnDelete` in order to kick off the delete flow, but then `deleteWidgets` was being called again later in `column-delete`. The update calls `column-delete` directly from the delete button click, simplifying the flow and removing the duplicate call to `deleteWidgets`.

2. Adds a new check to the `verify-board` tool, in order to check that every column represented in the board's content extension data corresponds to an actual widget - this case should not happen often at all, but this will ensure that users can unblock their boards if there is a condition where the content extension data for columns needs to be cleaned up after a column delete (and will also allow the user to fix the particular board the bug was raised for).

3. Adds a new layout recalculation to `verify-board`. This essentially triggers a manual resize without actually changing the size of the board, which will cause the compute/calculate layout functions in the ekb resize plugin to run, ensuring the board's dimensions are correct. In the example of this bug, this step will fix the board width, which was not updated after the columns were partially deleted, but this will also be a nice add-on to fix any other potential layout bugs.

#### Reviewer Resources
JIRA Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1033
Test env:  ht

title: [CAN-7531] Telemetry for partOf - delete, drag and edit
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR adds `partOf` to the tracking of deleting widgets, when dragging stops and when widgets are no longer being edited.

These events are:
 - `deleted_widget` in which I only added the `partOfType`
 - `editing_widget_ended` 
    - Triggered when a widget is being edited and it stops, for example writing text in a sticky note or a mindmap node
 - `dragging_widget_ended` which is triggered when widgets are dropped from a drag
    - Sends a payload with the widget type and the number of those widgets being dragged
    - Also has a `widgetCount` property that sums up all the widgets being dragged
    - For specific `partOf` cases, I used the `type:partOfType` format for the key.

title: [CAN-7518] Collapse handler zoom behavior fix
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR updates the collapse handler so that it remains in widget space coordinates. As a result, it will appear smaller when zooming out and larger when zooming in. In contrast, the create child handler retains its current behavior, maintaining a fixed size regardless of the zoom level.

The visual distance between the node and the create child handler should remain consistent across all zoom levels. The same applies to the distance between the collapse handler and the create child handler.

There is a minor visual glitch when crossing the one hundred percent zoom level in either direction, but we are comfortable accepting it for now.

title: [SCQM-965] - AI Chat performance - Add in progress context messages to chat hub/notifications
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Updates the AI Chat Hub and in progress notifications to show contextual progress messages for function calls. This is an improvement for perceived performance, giving users more context into what is happening as they are waiting for AI operations to complete.

This is done by creating a new assistant chat entry in the chat when the AI makes a function call and replacing the current cycling messages ('Working on it', etc.) in the notification toast with a more specific context message mapped to the current operation ('Finding selected elements...'). Right now, this mapping is simply hardcoded in a helper file, but it could potentially later be returned from the AI along with the function call response. Additionally, only one context message is shown per function call, to avoid situations where the same message is shown for similar chained function calls- for example, if the AI response has five calls to `updateElements`, only one message will be shown for the group.

Also adds an intro message - `Sure! I can help with that.` to replace the current initial `...` message.

title: [CAN-7500] Move `computeGridLayout` into a system
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

_Disclaimer: Please don't hate me for what you're about to review._

---

As part of an effort to move the logic related to how grid areas operate out of business rules and onto our new paradigm, we need to do several operations that can be too much for one PR:
1. ~Unify code related to how grid areas operate.~ ([#44470](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/44470))
~We have different apis handling logic related to how a grid area show placeholder widgets in the engine. In order to be able to move that we first need to unify them as much as possible so the process much straight forward~

2. Move placeholder logic to a derivative
The placeholder ghost widgets that we show when dragging a widget onto a grid area reflect the final position that a widget would have if dropped. This is a transient state that creates a widget that should never be persisted. Because of this, a derivative is a nice place to put this logic so we don't have to call it everytime we need it.

3. ➡️ **Move layout computation to a system** _(this PR)_
Everytime a grid area obtains a new widget or loses one, it needs to accomodate itself and its content to mantain a grid configuration. This is an indirect side effect of the operations a user can do, and thus it fits very well to be a system.

---

So, you will probably notice that I'm doing the 3rd step before the 2nd, and there's a very good reason for that, let me give you a bit of context:
I'm not gonna go deep into how grid areas work (or _should_ work, because they became quite unreliable over time), but the important thing is that we have two particular effects we want to show when any action involving grid areas happen:
1. If we're dragging a widget over a grid area, we want to show a placeholder of where the widget would end up if dropped
2. In any case (including that one), we want all widgets already within the grid area to self-arrange in a grid at all times.

The goal here is to migrate the collapse handler for mindmaps from the `engine`, [this PR](https://github.com/tactivos/mural-render/pull/1385) is also part of the same effort, to `murally`. The goal for doing this is to have more control over it because the engine states don't behave as we thought they did.

The collapse handler:
- Is never part of the exports
- We'd like to control how it behaves regarding the zoom

   - We are also closing https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7487 with this PR 

The problem of using custom handles in the engine is that you can check if it exists, but you can't get its location, so we have to calculate it for the tests in cucumber. Does this suck? Yes, but the effort was a lot smaller than modifying the engine and all the usages.

title: [CAN-7483] Implement undo/redo functionality for mindmap expand/collapse actions
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This pull request introduces undo/redo functionality for collapsing and expanding nodes in mind maps. It includes the implementation of a new undo/redo step, integration with the mind map processor, and comprehensive test coverage for the feature.

### Implementation of Undo/Redo Functionality:
* Added the `CollapseExpandUndoStep` class to handle undo and redo actions for collapsing and expanding mind map nodes. This class tracks the affected widget, the action performed, and applies or reverts changes accordingly. (`src/mural/addons/mindmaps/expand-collapse/collapse-expand-undo-step.ts`, [src/mural/addons/mindmaps/expand-collapse/collapse-expand-undo-step.tsR1-R63](diffhunk://#diff-a0413282c181b269d8f76cfe7507357010c610ad45c81ae8587b2a4042ee7495R1-R63))

### Integration into Mind Map Processor:
* Integrated the `CollapseExpandUndoStep` into the `mindmapExpandCollapseProcessor`, ensuring that collapse and expand actions are appended to the undo/redo stack. (`src/mural/addons/mindmaps/expand-collapse/index.ts`, [src/mural/addons/mindmaps/expand-collapse/index.tsL67-R79](diffhunk://#diff-4113982db8b419051150a8ea8add7d19a5fda24482962de6e9d0cc3c8c6fdef2L67-R79))

### Test Coverage:
* Added unit tests for the `CollapseExpandUndoStep` class to verify its behavior for undo/redo operations, including scenarios where no changes occur or the widget is deleted. (`src/mural/addons/mindmaps/expand-collapse/collapse-expand-undo-step.test.ts`, [src/mural/addons/mindmaps/expand-collapse/collapse-expand-undo-step.test.tsR1-R108](diffhunk://#diff-3e22787440e036f1d0a54fe88e0a403fc6d089caf09084bdd2fc868d5722f6b5R1-R108))

* Extended feature tests to cover undo and redo scenarios for collapsing and expanding nodes in mind maps. (`src/test/react-new/features/canvas/widgets/mindmaps/collapse.feature`, [src/test/react-new/features/canvas/widgets/mindmaps/collapse.featureR66-R114](diffhunk://#diff-392fd962c8644ad7f7abfcfb5f

title: [SCQM-1048][SCQM-879] Add Preview Mode to AIRewrite and remove Preview Mode's feature flag
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR adds Preview Mode support to the AI Rewrite feature, and for that I needed to have the widgets' update operation within a single Undo transaction. Which, to be fair, undoing all rewrites in a single operation seems like a better experience.

This also updates the response messages sent to both the user and the AI. Mostly because the "partial update" scenario (when some elements couldn't be rewritten by things like being locked) was looking really off: The message sent back to the user was ambiguous (`"Content has been rewritten. Remember to review it [...]. Some content could not be updated"`) and the message to the AI wasn't very specific on which elements weren't updated, so it would still list all the rewrite responses regardless.

Also removes the `feat-mu-ai-preview-mode` feature flag.

This can be followed by commit:
- `Add Preview Mode to AI Rewrite`: Adds preview mode to the Rewrite, although I missed a couple of things I added in the last commit.
- `Fix AI including rewritten text for elements that failed`: Fix Rewrite response for partial update scenarios.
- `Remove AI_PREVIEW_MODE feature flag`: Remove the Preview Mode feature flag and include the missing `previewModeMsg` to Rewrite and remove the toast notification since it's now handled by Preview Mode.
- `Add Preview Mode early accept/decline execution`: Improves the interaction with the accept/discard options of Preview Mode so they apply immediately instead of having to wait for the AI to call their corresponding functions.

title: [CAN-7498] Refactor grid area related code
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
As part of an effort to move the logic related to how grid areas operate out of business rules and onto our new paradigm, we need to do several operations that can be too much for one PR:
1. ➡️ **Unify code related to how grid areas operate.** _(this PR)_
We have different apis handling logic related to how a grid area show placeholder widgets in the engine. In order to be able to move that we first need to unify them as much as possible so the process much straight forward

2. Move placeholder logic to a derivative
The placeholder ghost widgets that we show when dragging a widget onto a grid area reflect the final position that a widget would have if dropped. This is a transient state that creates a widget that should never be persisted. Because of this, a derivative is a nice place to put this logic so we don't have to call it everytime we need it.

3. Move layout computation to a system
Everytime a grid area obtains a new widget or loses one, it needs to accomodate itself and its content to mantain a grid configuration. This is an indirect side effect of the operations a user can do, and thus it fits very well to be a system.

This PR should have no effect in how grid areas work, there's little to no change in logic.
The only relevant logical change is in the fact that we're now considering placeholders everytime we do a recomputation, and we're not considering them when assigning a new stacking order to the grid area children.

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [PE-5529] Adds git to test image build stage.
body:
This change fixes a problem where a CI job for stable-fix backmerges fails, leading to a release train error message sent to slack that confuses devs. 

The underlying problem is that git is required by `@dorny/paths-filter` action for certain types of CI trigger events. This action is used by a job that detects when `package.json` has changed but `package-lock.json` has not changed.

Unfortunately we can't measure the impact on build time right now, however I believe it will be negligible.

More details in the slack [thread](https://mural.slack.com/archives/C07T0HZTZSL/p1748901273232159).

title: [SCQM-1064] Fix mindmap invalid widget error
body:
### Relevant Links 🔗
- [**API PR**](https://github.com/tactivos/mural-api/pull/13906)

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Currently the steps to create a mindmap are:
1. In the front end, generate a root node
2. Using **widgetIds**, make **multiple** requests to `generate-ideas` to build out the tree
3. Each `generate-ideas` request returns a single set of child ideas, which the front end creates widgets out of, then uses their widgetIds in the next set of requests

The problem is that on the worker side, it's relying on widget ids to get the topics to generate more ideas from and we keep running into an error where a widget created on the front end has not yet persisted on the backend when the worker queries it. 

The solution is to move generating layers from the front end => worker. 

The new steps are:
1. In the front end, generate a root node
2. Using the **text** from that node, make a **single** request to `generate-ideas` to build out the tree
3. IN THE WORKER, each `fetchGptJSON` request returns a set of child ideas (text), which it will use to make the next set of requests
4. The entire mindmap is returned to the front end where it can parse the text and generate all the widgets at once - removing the dependency on any single widget being persisted to build nodes off of it

title: [CAN-7428] Refactor setting arrow references after absorption to the systems
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is the last PR in a series of (more than I would have expected) pieces of work regarding arrows and their absorption capabilities.

The previous work moved all the logic regarding the absorption of arrows to a new system, but there were still pieces of code trying to address the arrow start and end reference when an absorption ocurred.

Basically, the rule is: if an arrow is absorbed by a widget, it can't be connected on both ends to it too.
There are more specifications and edge cases to this, but that's the golden rule.

This PR handles the consequence of an absorption or an expulsion in regards of an arrow's references.

**Important distinction:** this **does not** handle all the cases where an arrow should change its referenced widget.
This is only about sanitizing the references when there was an absorption or an expulsion so we don't have a case of an arrow both pointing to an area and parented by an area when it shouldn't.

This is why the code is within the absorption system itself. Because this is logic related to the absorption side-effect, not to the regular arrow connection.

What you need to expect from here, first and foremost, is that arrows continue working as expected when interacting with an absorbing widget, whether they are connected to other widgets or not.
That's basically saying "this PR did not break existing behavior".

As to what this PR actually introduces: you should now see that an arrow that has a `parentId` assigned to a widget does not have the references also pointing to the widget.
You can see that using the widget inspector.

#### Reviewer Resources
