title: [CAN-7478] Always notify the engine when a widget will be selected
body:
# Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

## 🧠 Context

- The engine has multiple layers, including:
  - `parser` (stateless): transforms widgets into drawable primitives
  - `selection` (stateful): renders selection visuals like blue outlines, resize, and rotate handles
- Parsers support conditional rendering via a `state` (e.g. shadow when dragging), but this isn’t real state — just input context.

---

## 🪲 The Bug

- We added **collapse and expand handlers** to mindmap nodes.
- **Requirement**: the **expand handler** (the one with the number of collapsed descendants) must be included in **exports**.
- Exports are handled only by the **parser layer**, as the **selection layer is not active** during export.
- The **collapse handler** should **not** appear in exports — it only shows when a node is selected.
- Problem: when widget props change, the stateless parser forgets the `selected` state, so the collapse handler disappears.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11338c7e-6e1b-4657-adc7-934048eed91b)

---

## ✅ Preferred Solution (implemented here)

- On every `computeEngineUpdateEffects`, re-notify the engine of selection state (not just on selection change).
- The engine skips redundant renders, so performance impact is minimal.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4a6fa1c-6c2b-4eb2-a584-aa51060eabed)

---

## 🧪 Alternatives Considered

1. **Split rendering responsibility**
   - Collapse handler in selection layer or `murally`
   - Expand handler in parser (for exports)
   - 🚫 Creates unclear ownership and inconsistent logic:
     - Why is the collapse here?
     - What defines “collapsed”?
     - Should there also be an expand?

2. **Manually show collapse handler from `murally` via `engine.widgets.show(hint)`**
   - 🚫 Doesn't work — parser has no memory of `selected` context

3. **Always draw collapse handler, hide it on load**
   - 🚫 Makes the handler appear in exports

title: Arrow absorption fixes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR has a couple of (hopefully) small changes regarding how we're handling arrow absorption now as part of a system.
This is leading the way for the work to come regarding fixing the arrow references when an absorption or expulsion has occurred, but before we can have that ready, we need to address this set of issues.

In this PR I'm fixing the following stuff:
- **Missing absorption case**
The rules that define when an absorption should occur for an arrow were missing one case: an arrow that has a tip connected to an absorbing widget (i.e. an area) and the other tip is inside the area but not connected nor absorbed by it.
When we encounter that use case and we execute an affecting operation, we want to have the widget absorb the arrow. This change ensures that.

- **Missing exclusion case**
This is a case where, under the new rules, we should expect an absorption to occur, but we actually _don't_ want it to happen: when an arrow is connected on one end to an absorbing widget, _but on the border of the widget_.
From a user point of view, if the arrow is connected to the border, it means that it's _pointing at the widget_, so we need to interpret that as such and prevent absorption to happen on cases like if the other tip ends up inside the same widget.

- **Fix recalculation of position after an absorption or expulsion**
The rest of the commits fix this particular case: if we delete a widget containing an arrow, and we make it explicit that we only want to delete the widget and not everything inside (like when we delete an area only, and not an area and its content), we now have a case of an arrow that needs to null its parent and compensate its position, but since the area no longer exists, it can't fetch it in order to find out its global position.
This fix consists in checking the initial store for that situation.

🌎 **Test env**: https://arrow-absorption-revisit.mural.engineering/

title: [SCQM-1060] Make function responses non-abortable
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR makes function call response operations non-abortable to avoid breaking the chat history due to missing function call response entries.
To this end I've renamed the recently added `abortable` property to `showProgressToast` which is more accurate, and I've added a new `nonAbortable` property to the `AIOperation` definition. This new prop avoids sending the `onAbort` callback to the progress toast notification, which now replaces the "Stop" button with an "X" button so the use can close it at will (the alternative would be the notification auto-closing, which would mean the feedback would get lost).

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-1060) to understand the context of this effort.
- 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://scqm-1060-dont-abort-function-responses.mural.engineering) to perform a smoke test. ([all testing envs](https://testing-envs.mural.engineering))

Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes:
1. When the a function call response gets sent to the backend, the toast notification should change to have an "X" (close) button instead of the regular "Stop" (abort) button.
2. If a request would trigger a sequence of function calls, it you close a notification, it should appear again on subsequent steps (an example could be to select multiple stickies and prompt to "change the selected elements background color to a rainbow pattern but explain every step in between")

### Required Checklist for Author

- [ ] No new cucumber tests were added

title: [CPT-2234] Fix object links
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Prior to this change:
- A user was not able to copy a link to an object in a template.
- If a user copied a link to an object in a mural and pasted it into the same mural and then duplicated the mural, the link in the duplicated mural would point to the original mural and not the new mural
- If a user had copied a link to an object in a mural, pasted it into the mural, and then published the mural as a template, the link in the template would point to the original mural
- If a user had copied a link to an object in a template, pasted it into the template, and saved, the link would point to that area of the template.
    - If a user had then created a mural from that template, the link in the mural would point to the original template
    - If the owner of the template had created a public link after the object link had been added to the template (and the link had been added when the template was a workspace template), the link would still point to the workspace link and not the public link, so although the template could be shared publicly, users who accessed the template from outside of the workspace would have hit a Page Not Found when clicking the link
    - If the owner of the template had revoked the public link after the object had been added to the template (and the link had been added when the template was a public template), the link would still point to the public link and anyone who clicked on the link in the template would have been taken to a Page Not Found.

After this change:
- Users are able to copy a link to an object in a template
- If a user copies a link to an object in a mural and pastes it into the mural and then duplicates the mural, the link in the duplicated mural will point to the new mural and not the original mural
- If a user copies a link to an object in a mural and pastes it into the mural and then publishes the mural as a template, the link in the template will point t

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

[FEP-6243](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/FEP-6243)

[https://remove-react-masonry-component.mural.engineering/](https://remove-react-masonry-component.mural.engineering/)

This PR removes the `react-masonry-component` dependency from the codebase. It's a dependency that presents some issues with React 18 and is not actively maintained anymore. This component was only used in the Adobe Creative Cloud image tab. The other image libraries are using the `MasonryLayout` component, a component that was created to provide an accessible grid navigation implemented in `MkitGridNavigation`. This PR replaces `react-masonry-component` with `MasonryLayout`. 

Given that the Adobe Creative Cloud integration presents some challenges for local development. The items input was mocked during development with items taken from the images web search tab. The changes in this PR don't affect business logic just how items are rendered in the masonry layout.

title: [CAN-7458] Prevent arrow absorption on non-affecting operations
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

We used to have the code handling arrow absorption spread everywhere, but [this PR](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/44241) modified that to have one only entry point for this: the absorption system for arrows.

Because of this, we now run this logic on every model update done using the `changes` api. And that includes some operation where we probably _don't_ want absorption to happen, such as when dragging an area over an arrow.

This PR amends that situation by defining a strict set of affecting operations where we want the system to run.

title: [CAN-7411] Fix mindmap utils to avoid bugs related with extra arrows
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer `getMindmapParent` and `getMindmapNodeDirection` used a the following code to traverse the mindmap: ```ts const arrow = store.getArrowsByStartRefId(widget.id)[0]; ``` In the case of a mindmap that have extra connector attached to the nodes, depending on the order, the queried arrow would end up being the extra one, resulting on a incorrect result of the function. This utilities are updated to fix the reported bug in `beforeCopy` in `src/mural/addons/mindmaps/clipboard.ts`: ``` const newMindmapSelection = selectedTopNodes.flatMap(node => assignNewMindmapId([ forceRoot(node), ...getMindmapDescendants(ctx.widgets.getStore(), node, { includeArrows: true, recursive: true, }), ]), ); ``` In this snippet, `getMindmapDescendants` might return incorrectly a node that is connected with an extra arrow as a root node (depends on the order that the connectors are in the document) To fix this issue, I'm replacing the call to `getArrowsByStartRefId` with `getNodeUpwardsArrow` which have all the mindmaps related checks.

title: [CAN-7437] Refactor `dropWidgetsOnCanvas` to run systems
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
[83%](https://how-i-met-your-mother.fandom.com/wiki/83) of our absorption logic happens on the function `dropWidgetsOnCanvas`.
Almost every action we do on a mural that could possibly result in the absorption or expulsion of one or more widgets end up calling this method to handle such behavior.

As part of our current effort of using the `changes` api to do updates on our widget model, this function was one of the big milestones.
Every update in this function was being done using `sdk.widgets.update`, which meant that our set of systems would not run.

In this PR the code is completely refactored to use `apply` to perform local changes, and `commit` to persist.

However, this one is taking it one step further.

Given that the theoretical job of this function is to handle absorption or expulsion as a side effect of a user action, it should not be committing any changes, because "commit" means that the action has finished and the changes are ready to be persisted, and this function does not necessarily represents the "end of the line".

This is why in this refactor the function will only `apply` changes but not `commit` them at all.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7437)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://drop-widgets-systems.mural.engineering)

Given that this affect the main entry point for absorption and expulsion, you will need to test this behavior in full.

title: [CAN-7438] Refactor `detachWidgetsFromCluster` to run systems
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
We currently have a lot of functions regarding absorption that are becoming quite legacy but are still among us.
Given our intention to move towards using systems as the way to handle side effects, we need to make sure that most of the user actions can trigger this set of systems.

In order to achieve that, we need to make sure that the updating of the widget model happens using the `changes` api (via its methods `apply` and `commit`) instead of doing a simple `widgets.update`.

This PR focuses on a specific function, `detachWidgetsFromCluster`, which, as the name implies, handles de-parenting a set of widgets from their current parent.

We're not here to analyze whether that method is good or bad. What we want to do here is make sure that every update to the widgets model occurrs using the `changes` api.
**We also won't care here if we're doing the minimum number of calls to the api**, that's out of the scope here. Again, we want to make sure that every behavior that used this function continues working as expected, but that all updates go through the `changes` api in order to be able to trigger our set of systems.

Here are some of the most relevant operations that we need to check for, based on who's calling the function:
- Deleting a cluster containing widgets, which should be properly detached from it
- Undoing the deletion should restore the widgets back to the cluster
- Resizing any widget inside a cluster should remove it during the resizing process. This is only visible through the widget inspector because the regular behavior is to re-add it after the resizing is done.
- Resizing a freeform area such that widgets end up out of the area's bounds
- Merging two or more cells containing widgets should move all the widgets to the one remaining merged cell.
- Unmerging a cell should move all the widgets to the cells they belong based on their positions.

title: Fix invalid color error
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR solves a reported bug where users were facing a JS error when trying to set a color from a list containing an invalid custom color.

There are three main changes here that should address the situation:
1. A validation function has been added to define whether a string represents a valid color or not.
2. The function to fetch a color's name is now using the validator to return a string even if the color is not valid.
3. The function that sets a user custom colors will now filter out any value that does not pass this validation.

There are not many ways you can test this since this is defensive code, but one thing you could do is put this in the console and check that the value sent to the backend does not contain the invalid colors (and that the app doesn't crash because of this):
```ts
sdkContext.user.customColors.set(['invalid-color', '#ff0000', 'rgb(123,123,123)', '#ZZZZZZ']);
```

🌎 **Test env**: https://invalid-colors.mural.engineering/

title: [CAN-7439] Refactor `absorbWidgetsIntoCluster` to run systems
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
We currently have a lot of functions regarding absorption that are becoming quite legacy but are still among us.
Given our intention to move towards using systems as the way to handle side effects, we need to make sure that most of the user actions can trigger this set of systems.

In order to achieve that, we need to make sure that the updating of the widget model happens using the `changes` api (via its methods `apply` and `commit`) instead of doing a simple `widgets.update`.

This PR focuses on a specific function, `absorbWidgetsIntoCluter` that is currently being called only by `dropWidgetsOnCanvas`.

This method analyzes the provided list of widgets to see which ones of them are suitable to be absorbed by the provided cluster, and performs the absorption by calling `addWidgetsIntoClusterWithoutCheckingForConsistency`.

We're not here to analyze whether that method is good or bad. What we want to do here is make sure that every update to the widgets model occurrs using the `changes` api.
**We also won't care here if we're doing the minimum number of calls to the api**, that's out of the scope here. Again, we want to make sure that every behavior that used this function continues working as expected, but that all updates go through the `changes` api in order to be able to trigger our set of systems.

Since this method is called by our main entry point for absorption, we need to do a quick check that everything still works as expect when it comes to interacting with absorbing widgets.

Here are some of the most relevant operations that we need to check for:
- Grouping a selection of widgets: the group should be formed as expected
- Grouping a selection of widgets that are inside a cluster (like an area): the group itself should end up inside the area
- Ungrouping a group inside a cluster: the widgets should end up inside the cluster after the ungrouping

In order to achieve that, we need to make sure that the updating of the widget model happens using the `changes` api (via its methods `apply` and `commit`) instead of doing a simple `widgets.update`.

This PR focuses on the last member of the absorption chain, a method called `addWidgetsIntoClusterWithoutCheckingForConsistency`.

This method, as its detailed name implies, handles parenting of a set of widgets with a cluster without doing any sort of checking on whether there is overlapping or not, or if it obeys the rules for absorption.

We're not here to analyze whether that method is good or bad. What we want to do here is make sure that every update to the widgets model occurrs using the `changes` api.
**We also won't care here if we're doing the minimum number of calls to the api**, that's out of the scope here. Again, we want to make sure that every behavior that used this function continues working as expected, but that all updates go through the `changes` api in order to be able to trigger our set of systems.

There are, luckily, a very reduced number of operations that call this function, so here's what we need to check for:
- Grouping a selection of widgets: the group should be formed as expected
- Grouping a selection of widgets that are inside a cluster (like an area): the group itself should end up inside the area
- Ungrouping a group inside a cluster: the widgets should end up inside the cluster after the ungrouping
- Replace a widget inside a cluster: the new widget type should end up inside the cluster too
- Freeform area resizing: should absorb widgets that end up inside the area after the resize is d

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR refactors the the AI dispatcher's `sendChatMessages()` logic to take a single chat entry instead of an array. This can be done now that canned responses are gone, but it required updating suggestion pills, which still supported a canned function call of sorts.

This PR can be followed by commit:
- The first commit refactors suggestion pills to only support single string messages instead of the entries array.
- The second commit implements the `sendChatMessages()` refactor, which it turn required refactoring the `AIChatQuickAction`'s `onClick`'s `sendMessagesHandler` in a similar fashion.

This should reduce AI Chat complexity and improve robustness and serves as a precursor to other upcoming refactor efforts.

**NOTE**: Keep in mind that with these changes we add back the roundtrip call to AI required for some suggestion pills and quick action buttons because they won't be able to call a feature or function call directly anymore. title: [FEP-6238] Migrating react-color to @uiw/react-color in Color Picker
body:
Updates `react-color` to `@uiw/react-color` as a part of the React 18 migration. `react-color` is an unmaintained project that doesn't support React 17 or React 18. This project has been forked by the people at `@uiw` and this library can act as a replacement for the existing `react-color` library. 

Test env: https://react-color.mural.engineering

This pull request refactors the `ColorPicker` component to replace the `react-color` library with `@uiw/react-color`, improving maintainability, performance, and accessibility. Key changes include library migration, accessibility enhancements, and updates to the color picker logic and styles.

### Library Migration:
* Replaced `react-color` with `@uiw/react-color` in `package.json` by removing `react-color` and adding `@uiw/react-color`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R103) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L155)
* Updated imports and utilities in `src/common/components/color-palette/color-picker/index.tsx` to use `@uiw/react-color` functions and types, such as `hsvaToHex` and `hexToHsva`.

### Accessibility Enhancements:
* Removed `tabindex` attributes from `@uiw/react-color` components to prevent conflicts with custom keyboard interactions.
* Improved keyboard navigation for saturation and slider controls by simplifying event handling and ensuring proper value normalization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a02984179152943a379ae0d27ef6d9a0313a292803ece6027642adadbda79dc4R200-R243) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a02984179152943a379ae0d27ef6d9a0313a292803ece6027642adadbda79dc4L243-R313)

### Color Picker Logic Updates:
* Added type guards (`isHexColor`, `isHslaColor`, `isRgbaColor`) to validate color formats.
* Introduced a new `normalizeHex` utility to standardize hex color inputs into the `ColorState` format.
* Simplified and modernized the `handleColorPickerChange` function to update color states using `hsva` val

title: [SCQM-871] Fix 'AI Create Mindmap with Ideas' - Only root node is created
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

The issue is happening because `generateNodes` was running into a race condition where the code is trying to add layers to the `rootNode`, but `rootNode` is not fully created in the backend yet. With  `sdk.hooks.register.widgets.remoteCreation( remoteWidgetCreationPluginForMindmap...` we'll wait after the `rootNode` is created to add the new layers and not run into the following error:

```
ERROR: Function 'createMindmap' failed with Error: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'T', \"The elemen\"... is not valid JSON.\nIt might be that the function is not implemented or the arguments are wrong.
```

Note:
This only checks for the rootNode, we _may_ run into the same issue for the childNodes of layer 2, etc..
If the same issue occurs to the child nodes we can apply a similar strategy.

title: [CAN-7435] Make arrow's absorption system the only entry point for absorption
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a continuation of the work started in [this PR](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/44197).

The first iteration consisted in refactoring our current absorption system for arrows to implement the defined rules for absorption in a cleaner and maintainable way.

The entirety of the work was focused exclusively on the system itself and the way it operates.

This PR focuses on the other part: everything else in the codebase that is currently handling arrow absorption on their own.

In order to have the system run a consistent and unique set of rules for absorbing widgets, we need to make sure that nobody else can mess with that adding their own rules.

In this PR every piece of code that was touching arrow absorption, whether that is directly by checking if a certain widget is an arrow and operating in consequence or indirectly by applying absorption behavior to any widget, was modified to exclude arrows from the calculation.

This means that absorption is now controlled entirely by the system.

It's important to notice that we're talking here about **arrows exclusively**. Any other type of widget absorption is still handled by the regular code.
It's also important to notice that this is **only about the absorption** and not about updating the references of the arrow as a consequence of the absorption. That is going to be handled in a different PR, so you can expect here some rather inconsistent behavior where an arrow is both parented and referenced by an absorbing widget.

The only use case left where a parenting is assigned to an arrow outside the system is when grouping and ungrouping. This is because that is not a case of absorption perse, but is contained enough to be possible to deal with in a different PR if needed.

Given that this affect absorption for arrows, you basically need to test that arrow absorption still behaves as expected as per the rules defined in the previous

title: [CAN-7402] Exclude invisible widgets from QuadMap
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR excludes widgets with `invisible: true` from the visual calculations. Given the `QuadMap` is a tool, we decided to exclude them when creating it inside the `WidgetStore`.

- `get`, `getAabb` and `getObb` return information we need them to return the invisible widgets
- `getVisualAabb` returns visual information, therefore invisible widgets shouldn't be returned

This will be used for expanding and collapsing nodes in mindmaps and keep consistency with the engine. There's not much to test here because we don't have any invisible widget yet. An example to test would be that creating a couple of mindmap nodes, making one invisible, changing layout and making them visible again still works as expected, but you'd need to this via the console using `sdkContext.widgets.changes.apply({ values: { invisible: true }, widgetId: 'id' })`

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [CAN-7401] Add `invisible` property to widgets
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR adds the `invisible` property to the root of the `Widget` type. It also creates an `effect` so we can tell the engine how to react when this property is changed. We also added a validation in the engine to not parse widgets with `invisible: true`, but that's not enough, because we still need to add them to the engine in order to update their visibility back.

To test this, create a sticky note, remember its `id`.

In the console run `sdkContext.widgets.update('the-id', { invisible: true })`, the widget should disappear. A refresh should still not show it. Doing the opposite, `sdkContext.widgets.update('the-id', { invisible: false })` should show it again.

title: Fix `Duplicate mural` model taking long time to load
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When the user attempting to duplicate a mural is a member of many different workspaces, the modal that shows up when we choose to duplicate the mural we're in can take a long time to load.
This is because we're fetching the list of workspaces and including the member count in that query. But the modal does not need this value at all, so the PR fixes it by using `fetchWorkspaces` instead of `workspacesApi.list()`.
Both calls are equal, except the first one sends `includeCounts` in `false` to avoid that expensive calculation.

The way of testing this is creating (or joining) several workspaces in the test environment, then creating a mural in one of them and attempting to duplicate it.
We should see all the workspaces listed and available to place the duplicate.

🌎 **Test env**: https://duplicate-workspaces.mural.engineering/

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR changes the way AI features are added to the widget toolbar dropdown in favor of a register so other AI features can be added from outside of the addon. That also means that the way the options were being sorted had to be updated.
It's easier to follow by commit:
- The first commit adds the new registry (`register.ai.toolbar`).
- Followed by 11 commits that migrate 1 AI feature toolbar option each, with the last one cleaning up the helpers used during the transition.
- The last commit removes the sorting array in favor of relying on registering the options in a specific order. Although this is less explicit, it is more flexible and allows for devs to use the register sorting helpers if needed.

title: [FEP-6237] Remove react-clipboard.js & update copy button to use native
body:
As a part of of React 18 migration, this pull request replaces the `react-clipboard.js` library which is no longer supported, with the native Clipboard API across the codebase. 

The changes improve performance, reduce dependencies, and ensure better compatibility with secure contexts. The most important changes include removing the `react-clipboard.js` dependency, refactoring components to use the native Clipboard API, and implementing fallback mechanisms for legacy browsers.

title: [CAN-7429] Remove `memoize` on `TablesStore` functions
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The `TablesStore` has an overriding in its constructor to make each method use `memoize` to cache the result, so each call to the same instance would return the value without any calculations.

The reported bug found that there was a problem within the `TablesStore`, because the methods are calling `getTable` inside the same instance, and that was causing a circular reference that would throw a stack overflow error.

This PR removes the memoizing of those functions until we find a better performance improvement.

Since the `TablesStore` instance is attached to the `WidgetStore`, and this one is immutable, the cases where `memoize` was improving performance where not that many, so it's not something that would affect the behavior in any impactful way.

title: [CPT-2320] Fix create revoke link bug
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes if you created or revoked public template links if you immediately tried to edit the template content you would be redirected to the previously most generally available link the template had. If you just revoked the public template link, you would be redirected to the public template link and end up in a not found page.

Now, with these changes, when you create or revoke public template links state in the app is updated accordingly so that when you try to edit the template you use the updated most generally available link for the template. 

^ applies for both the canvas (template route) and template cards in the dashboard.

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CPT-2320) to understand the context of this effort.
- 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://create-revoke-link-bug.mural.engineering/) to perform a smoke test.
- Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes
- To test that this change is working you will need a workspace template that you own and to follow the steps in the canvas and in the dashboard:
      1.  Open the share template modal and create a public link for the template.
      2. Without refreshing the page select the option `Edit template content`
      3. Verify that the redirection to the public template link + `/edit` is made correctly (it should look something like this: `/template/:templateId/:publicHash`)
      4. Go back to step 1 in the original page (canvas or dashboard) and refresh the page
      5. Open the share template modal and revoke the public template link
      6. Without refreshing the page select the option `Edit template content`
      7. Verify that the redirection to the workspace template link + `/edit` is made correctly (it should look something like this: `/t/:workspaceId/template/:templateId`)

title: [CAN-7416] Refactor arrow absorption system
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is an effort split into two PRs to separate responsabilities and make review easier.

The current system in charge of handling arrow absorption was getting confused to read and was not covering all the cases where we want an absorption to occur, so this PR refactors the code to both make the code easier to follow as well as implement the proper set of rules for what we consider an absorption when it comes to arrows.

The next PR will handle the effects of the absorption on the arrow references, because we want to change our current behavior so an absorbed arrow does not connect to its parent anymore.

According to the recently defined rules, an arrow should be absorbed by a parenting widget P if:

- `P` is not a `GroupWidget`, a `GridAreaWidget` or a `TableWidget`.
  - Unless the arrow was already inside a `GroupWidget`, in which case it should remain unmodified
- **And**…
  - One tip is connected to a widget inside `P` **AND** the other tip is not connected but is inside `P`
- **Or**…
  - Both tips are connected to widgets inside `P`
- **Or**…
  - One tip is connected to a widget inside `P` **AND** the other tip is connected to `P`
- **Or**…
  - Both tips are connected to `P`
- **Or**…
  - Both tips are `undefined` **AND** both tips are inside `P`

#### Reviewer Resources

title: Fix ampersand updating on the `changes` api
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This simple one-liner fixes a nasty situation that was hard to reproduce but very likely to happen:

On the `changes` api, whenever we process a list of updates on widget, we send the list to the method `updateAmpersandAndEngine` that proceeds to apply those updates on the ampersand widget models.

The error we had is that when we iterate the list of updates, if one widget is not found, we were stone cold returning the entire function instead of doing `continue` and moving onto the next update.
This is something that came from moving the original code from `sdk.widgets.update` (which dealt with a single update at a time) to this new approach.

How can we possibly trigger an update on a non-existent widget?

If we send the following set of changes to `apply`:
```ts
sdk.widgets.changes.apply([
  SingleWidgetActions.delete('widget-to-delete'),
  { values: { x: 100 }, widgetId: 'widget-to-delete' },
  { values: { width: 200 }, widgetId: 'completely-unrelated-widget' },
]);
```
We'll process the delete first and the updates later. So when we try to update `widget-to-delete`, we find that we have already deleted it, and proceed to return instead of continuing and we lose the update to `completely-unrelated-widget`.

There are not many ways of testing this because we don't have a proper case where this happens, but the added unit test should cover it.

🌎 **Test env:** https://amp-model-update.mural.engineering/

title: Improve Knip detection in workspaces configuration

body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer As part of the work for custom theming, this change adds a new section for company colors to the color picker. This section appears above the custom colors section and follows the same styling. title: [CPT-2148] Public template path simplification
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR modifies the route when viewing a public template to skip template preview step.

For a new user, it triggers the sign-up flow, and then sends them to an automatically created template-derived mural for that template.

It does the same for an existing user, minus the sign up step.

If the user has a free account and is at their mural limit, it sends them to the template page, and tells them that they need to upgrade.

NOTE:
I was not able to open the `reached-mural-limit` modal, because I couldn't figure out a way to trigger the modal in this context. I am open to ideas about how to trigger this, if possible.

If not, this fulfills the "less than ideal" part of the third acceptance criteria in the Jira ticket.

title: [CPT-2224] Shows user an error message for 400 errors while saving a template
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

**Bugfix**
When a user copied a widget with an asset (like photoWidget) with one of the following conditions 

> encryptionData.isAleActivated ||
> sdkContext.mural.get().aleActivation?.companyId ||
> encryptionData.zone !== sdkContext.mural.get().zone

into a public template, we were not sending the public hash when creating a content session, which resulted in assets not being copied as template assets and getting validation error as a result.

This PR adds the public hash to the `createTemplateContentApi` function to fix this bug and allow the creation of new template asset URLS.


Additionally, I updated the logic in the paste handler, as a backup, to ensure parity between the photo and thumb URLs, to make this process consistent with widgets with assets with both. We saw an error in the bug in question, because it had a `thumbURL` but not a `photoURL`, but it was only checking for `photoURL` when updating the asset URL.



**Error Handling**
Also, we've added some error handling, to show users better error messages for similar issues in the future.

Prior to these changes when a user tried to save a template, is there was a 400 error during the validation process, the saving process would hang and not give the user any feedback.

Now, with these changes, if this error occurs, it pops up a modal and lets the user know there was an error saving their template, and encourages them to contact IT.

title: [CAN-7332] Reduce calls to `apply` and `commit` in `resizeWidgets`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is the final PR in a very long effort to improve the way we update the widget model when we resize widgets.

The goal for this effort is to prepare the field for moving absorption to be a system, in which case it will run automatically after every call to `sdk.widgets.changes.apply`.
Since one of the most affecting operations that could cause an absorption is the resizing of widgets, we needed to have this function call `apply` consistently (this means that it will not update the widgets model in any other way) and as few times as possible to reduce the possibility of an ambiguety when handling the absorption.

With these last changes, the method does not execute any `sdk.widgets.update` call _(when the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag is enabled!)_, and only executes a call to `sdk.widgets.changes.apply` once per dragging movement (with the exception of tables, which execute an extra `apply` call to re-shape the table) and then one more after resizing has ended, where it also executes the only call to `sdk.widgets.changes.commit` in the entire operation.

All this logic is guarded with a unit test that assures that this behavior remains when the flag is enabled, and protects also all the internal calls by calling the real implementation for each case.

No change in behavior is expected, we should check that resizing works as expected for all widgets on all cases.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7332)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://resize-widgets.mural.engineering)

title: Fix widget ids provided to systems
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This simple PR fixes how we call each system: we were always sending the initial list of widget ids to each system, but recollecting all the ids affected by each system to return them as result.

This means that each system might potentially affect ids not included in the original list.
Therefore, there's no reason to think that each system should not be considering the ids returned by the previous executed systems.

This PR addresses that situation by providing the full list of affected ids to each system and still returning the full list as output.

The returned list will now also include the initial list of ids, so the caller can now rely on this list alone and not need to concatenate the original value.

No change in behavior is expected

🌎 **Test env:** https://systems-ids.mural.engineering/

title: [CAN-7376] Refactor `resizeTable` business rule to reduce calls to `apply` and `commit`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is part of a much bigger effort to reduce the number of times that resizing a widget executes an `apply` or a `commit`.
In this PR the focus is specifically in the `resizeTable` business rule, which is a sub-api of the general resizing widget dealing specifically with the effects of resizing a table.

The goal here is to, ideally, remove all calls to `apply` and `commit` and only return a list of changes for the general function to apply.

There's one caveat here: each resizing step of a table calls `reshapeTable`, a function that deals with the re-creation of the table's layout after a change has occurred.
This function, in itself, does an `apply` and a `commit`.

The call to `commit` has been succesfully removed from here and moved onto the caller, so we can assure that `resizeTable` _does not commit changes_.
However, the function still does one call to `apply`. It's quite hard to remove that call because the function also executes some post-reshape functions that depend on the changes to be in the model.

With the goal in mind of reducing the times systems are run as much as possible, having this one single extra call to `apply` only for tables seems to be an acceptable trade-off.
In fact, when this happens, in most cases, the method `resizeWidgets` will have no changes to apply, so that call in `resizeTable` will still be the only call there.

If the need comes to remove that call altogether, we can create a new effort specifically for that.

This change affects only the resizing of a table, so a proper test should check that tables can still be resized as expected

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7376)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://resize-table.mural.engineering)

title: [CAN-7350] Refactor `applyDeltasAndResize` to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
As part of the refactor of the `resizeWidgets` business rule to reduce the number of widget model updates, this PR handles the function `applyDeltasAndResize`, which is the main entry point for each resizing step.

Since the internal functions have already been addressed, in this one we focus on making this method return a list of changes and not perform any updates itself.

The PR is split into two parts because in order to properly address this function we first needed to make sure that `resizeMultiWidgets` works over our provided copy of the `WidgetStore` and not the one that it can fetch from the `SdkApis`.

No change in logic is expected whatsoever, every resize of every widget (or widgets) should continue working as expected.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7350)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://apply-deltas-resize.mural.engineering)

title: [CAN-7349] Refactor `resizeSingleWidget` to return a set of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The method `resizeSingleWidget` is in charge of handling the case of widget resizing when only a single widget is part of the selection.

As such, it handles the caveats and side-effects of the resizing regardless of the widget type, which results in having a lot of different places where the widget model is updated to reflect both the resizing change as well as any related side-effect.

As part of the effort to create a new absorption system, we need to minimize the number of updates to the model as much as possible so the systems can run over the full set of changes only once.

In this PR the method `resizeSingleWidget` is refactored to accumulate every possible change to the widgets model and return it as an array of `WidgetChange` instead of applying them itself, leaving the updating itself to the caller.

We don't expect any change in how resizing works. However, given that we're now accumulating changes to apply them once instead of do partial updates, it is possible that some behavior broke because of this, so please make sure single widget resizing works for all types of widgets.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7349)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://resize-single-widget.mural.engineering)

title: [SCQM-642] Replace Create Workshop canned response with codeblock
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR replaces the Create Workshop canned response with the brand new `getCustomResponseMessage()` solution. To this end, that function had to have some changes applied so it could support receiving a message as well as an entry (for custom rendering) at the same time.
This meant that the way the error message called it had to change, but it shouldn't be that big of a deal.
This PR also replaces `callId` with a more explicit boolean were possible, as we are moving towards removing the `callId` logic in the future.

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-642) to understand the context of this effort.

Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes:

title: Stable-Fix: Remove locale parameter from LinkedIn URLs for scrapping compatibility
body:
### Description:
This PR updates the LinkedIn URL handling logic to remove the locale parameter (e.g., ?locale=en_US) from profile URLs. The previous implementation did not work with URLs containing query parameters, which caused issues with our scrapin tool.

### Why:
Scrapin fails when LinkedIn profile URLs contain locale information as a query parameter. To ensure compatibility, we need to process URLs to remove ?locale=... or similar parameters and keep the URL in the canonical format.

### What was changed:
Added logic to strip query parameters from LinkedIn profile URLs

### Impact:
This change ensures all LinkedIn URLs passed to the scraping tool are in the accepted format, improving reliability.

### How to test:
Try submitting URLs like https://www.linkedin.com/in/kmiloandres/?locale=en_US and verify that scrappin processes it correctly after stripping parameters
Confirm that URLs without query parameters remain unchanged and functional

title: [CAN-7370] Make `resizeMultiWidgets` return a set of changes instead of applying them.
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors `resizeMultiWidgets` to return a set of changes instead of applying them. This PR is _long_ but _repetitive_ because each widget has its own logic for resizing 😢. Also, the resizing of frameworks was split in two parts, so I had to work quite a lot to unify it in a single function. Add to that that it recursively used `resizeMultiWidgets`, so I added a temporary parameter (which I removed in a latter commit) to be able to return changes without breaking any existent behavior at that time.

First I extracted the logic for each type of widget into a function. Unified the logic for frameworks. Created a temporary parameter in `resizeMultiWidgets` so I could have a different behavior when called from a recursion than from outside so no behavior broke. Finally removed this parameter and made sure all callers are applying the changes and there's no apply in this function. Some instances of the store were needed to updated, because changes weren't being applied but we needed an intermediate store to check what its state would be.

Ideally all this functions would use the store instead of the SDK, but `computeFontSize` and `scaleStrokes` wouldn't let me do that. We need to analyze what to do with those functions in the future. The same applies to the `measureWidget` dependency that uses an engine, we need to find a way to have a helper that already has it in its scope.

**What to test?**
Resizing should work for all widgets as it does in `beta` or `app`. Please test areas, groups and if possible frameworks (which are deprecated and can't be added from the app itself, however we need support for them).

#### Reviewer Resources
- Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7370
- Env: https://can-7370.mural.engineering

title: Add `TablesStore` to the `WidgetStore`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The `TableSdkApi` provides a lot of methods to get information from a certain table based on its layout. However, to do that it relies on the `WidgetsSdkApi` to get the widget based on its id.

With the new approach of model updating where we generate a set changes to apply them all at once, having these methods query the state is not ideal because we'll be generating iterating changes that need to rely on a version of the widget that is not yet stored in the state.

This approach moves all the relevant methods to a new `TablesStore` which is accessed via an instance of the `WidgetStore`, this means that those methods will always act over the widgets stored in that particular instance of the store.

Given the store's immutability nature, if we now want to generate changes iterating over versions that are not in the state, we only need to generate a new store out of those changes and query the table there.

For compatibility, the `TableSdkApi` keeps its funcionality intact but relies on the `TableStore` obtained by `sdk.widgets.getStore()`, which is equal to getting the widget from `sdk.widgets.get`.

No change in logic is expected whatsoever.

🌎 **Test env**: https://tables-store.mural.engineering/

title: [CAN-7347] Analyze and refactor absorption systems flag usage
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
In this PR I'm doing a full analysis of our current usage of the `ENABLE_ABSORPTION_SYSTEMS` flag.
The goal of that flag is to prevent code that specifically executes absorption or expulsion from running in favor of using a new system to handle that.
While the system is not yet implemented, we wanted to have this flag in the code first so we can stop the logic from running.

However, there were some cases where the flag was also stopping unrelated code from running, so the work here intends to address these situations and have the flag only prevent absorption and expulsion, and nothing more.

Since the flag is currently disabled everywhere, there should be no productive changes in the app.
When the flag is enabled (using the flag manager) we should expect the app to function exactly the same, but there should be no absorption or expulsion happening anywhere.

#### Reviewer Resources
- This addresses the following JIRA tickets: [CAN-7347](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7347), [CAN-7345](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7345) & [CAN-7334](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7334)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://absorption-flag-usage.mural.engineering)

title: [CAN-7356] Fix arrow recalculation on uniform dragging
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes a bug reported that happens when dragging two widgets connected by an arrow. The arrow would sometimes behave in an unpredictable way, positioning in a different place.

The reason why this happened was because some instances of the dragging operation were not considered as a "uniform dragging", which was a wrong assumption.
We consider a dragging to be uniform when both connections of the arrow move the exact same amount of pixels.

If we falsy accept a dragging step as "not uniform", the connectors system would default to a route calculation operation where a new route for the arrow would be calculated.
However, the problem arised when some steps of the dragging were taken as "not uniform" and some were taken as "uniform".
The first falsy operation would generate new points and the other true operations would reposition the arrow but with a wrong set of points now, which caused the issue.

There were several things causing the operation to be considered "not uniform", this PR address the two I could find:

1. We check if the connected widgets were rotated, in which case we consider that to not be a uniform dragging. However, the method that checked if a widget has been rotated was wrongly returning `true` for a non-rotated widget. This happened mainly when the widget moved only on the `y` axis.
The first commit fixes the logic from `isTranslationOf` from the `Matrix` package, while the second commit addresses how we use that to check if there was a rotation.

2. We check if the connected widgets were moved. If they were, we can have a uniform dragging. However, there were cases where the movement was so insignificant that we were thinking it to have moved when, at a pixel level, it did not. This is typical of the beginning of a dragging operation.

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

We currently have a confusing mix of notification systems for saving changes in the company dashboard. This changeset reduces it to one consistent experience. Unexpected errors in saving were not being signaled at all in the UI 😢, but now the user will at least see a notification banner indicating that their attempted update failed for some reason (likely a transitory error) and they should try again.

Implementation details:

title: [CAN-7353] Fix linear resizing of connected widgets
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes the following situation:

When creating two widgets connected by an arrow, selecting all of them (including the arrow), then proceeding to resize the selection, the arrow would get wrongly positioned relative to the connected widgets.

The expectation for this is that the arrow scales accordingly to the resize.

_This PR:_
![May-13-2025 15-58-06](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23b7a449-6c22-4bc8-af7d-14dfd4913c86)

_App:_
![May-13-2025 15-58-15](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4f067c7-7cbc-4658-8edb-2504183259f7)

The reason this happened was that we were wrongly using the `nextArrowObb` for calculating the translation.

The `nextArrowObb` represents the global position of the arrow after the resizing. We were comparing that to the calculated scaled global position of the arrow's original position. Of course this gives us that there are no translations because they match. 
We need to use the original position and compare that to the scaled version in order to get a real translation value.

This is the change we implement in this PR.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7353)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://resize-arrows.mural.engineering)

For testing this you need to have an arrow connected to two widgets. It doesn't matter which widgets.
Then you need to resize either one widget, both widgets, or the two widgets plus the arrow. When the resize is linear (i.e. the resize follows the same scale on the `x` or the `y` axis), this system kicks in and you should see the arrow follow the resize accordingly.

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR addresses a race condition triggered by the way tags creation worked.
Before these changes, creating a new tag would trigger 2 api calls; 1 to `/labels` to create the tag definition in the mural and 1 to `/widgets` to add it to all widgets involved.

title: [CAN-7340] Refactor `fitTableCellToContents` to return a `WidgetChange` set
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is part of the effort described in [CAN-7332](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7332) but it was isolated enough to be its own PR, which will make reviewing way easier.

The method `fitTableCellToContent` is used to re-accomodate a table after something inside of it has changed, so cells can always contain widgets without overlapping their borders.

This function is self-contained in the sense that it generates a list of changes, applies them and commit them all within this function.

In order to reduce the number of calls to `apply` and `commit` (which is the target of the mentioned card), we need to have this function simply return the list of changes and defer the updating to whoever corresponds.

However, for this to work as expected, we also need to modify a lot of functions that were using the `WidgetsSdkApi` to fetch some widgets needed to do calculations.
Given that in this new logic we calculate things first and apply changes later, we can't rely on those functions using the state to get the needed widgets, we need to provide them ourselves to assure we're using valid values.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7340)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://fit-table-cell.mural.engineering)

While there are implementation differences here, the expectation is that behavior does not change at all, so make sure to test resizing an entire table, a particular row, column, adding content to a table, creating and deleting rows and columns, etc.

title: [SCQM-953] Continued Mermaid-to-widget improvements: connectors
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, connectors took the "shortest path" to other widgets, sometimes resulting in connectors cutting across other connectors or widgets.

Now, with these changes, any connector that traverses more than one "hop" is analyzed by a path routing algorithm from longest-to-shortest order to try and route them around any other widget or connector. It falls back to our standard routing algorithm.

title: [EN-3277] feat: add the number of unlinked workspaces
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When loading the page, as a global admin (with permission to view unlinked workspaces), fetch the first page of results for unlinked workspaces to get the total value.

Thanks to React Query, navigating to the "Unlinked workspaces" tab does not fetch the first page again because it's cached. And we do not worry about updating the total, because linking a workspace does not remove the workspace from the list, thus the total is unchanged (because the data is refreshed every 24 hours).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The current [MrlTabLink](https://tactivos.github.io/ui-toolkit/main/?path=/docs/components-tabs-mrltablink--docs) component [only accepts](https://github.com/tactivos/ui-toolkit/blob/948ed93d3cf9462ad257277d0ab017f6a0f0c576/packages/ui-toolkit/src/components/tabs/MrlTabLink/MrlTabLink.tsx#L20) a `text: string` property, [instead of](https://github.com/tactivos/ui-toolkit/blob/6b16ea335b5d71bc58e3511a068cfb7368bfd40b/packages/ui-toolkit/src/components/navigation-sidebar/MrlSidebarNavItem/MrlSidebarNavItem.tsx#L26) a `text?: React.ReactNode` value. Hence, the [proposed design](https://www.figma.com/design/bZWdTnzbmuVHCd6NIz2z1s/Workspace-consolidation-M1.0-and-M1.1?node-id=1096-33017&p=f&t=DdiYWrrHxrVVR7wA-0) will be implemented at a later stage once I update UI toolkit with that change. The only difference is that the text will be **red** `¯\_(ツ)_/¯`

#### Reviewer resources

- 🏷️ [**EN-3277**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/EN-3277)
- 🧪 [**en-3277-unlinked-count.mural.engineering**](https://en-3277-unlinked-count.mural.engineering/)

When loading the page as a **global admin**, the tab component fetches the data from `GET unlinked workspaces` endpoint with the default state from the unlinked workspaces table. This way, the data is reused by the page if the user switches to the unlinked workspaces tab. It's also **non-blocking** when the `GET unlinked workspaces` is resolving.

This is part of the effort described in [CAN-7332](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7332) but it was isolated enough to be its own PR, which will make reviewing way easier.

The method `reshapeTable` is called whenever we resize a table widget or a table's row or column, and is in charge of recalculating the new sizes for each row and column of the affected table, as well as accomodate the cells to fit the content and handle the side effects of that size changing.

This function is self-contained in the sense that it generates a list of changes, applies them and commit them all within this function.

In order to reduce the number of calls to `apply` and `commit` that the entire resizing operation does we need to refactor this function to do the absolute minimum possible.

In this case, this means calling only one `apply` and one `commit`. We'll refactor this even further later, but should be enough for now for this PR.

By the way, I suggest you turn on `Hide whitespace` for the review, specially when reaching [this commit](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43955/commits/4d701928f9739587dd90193f89517391f710e48f).

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7338)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://reshape-table.mural.engineering)

While there are implementation differences here, the expectation is that behavior does not change at all, so make sure to test resizing an entire table, a particular row, column, adding content to a table, creating and deleting rows and columns, etc.

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This pull request introduces a new feature for replacing HTML text using Lexical, along with supporting changes to integrate this functionality into the existing find-and-replace workflow. It includes updates to the `FinderSpec` interface, the addition of the `replaceHtmlTextUsingLexical` function, and modifications to the API to support conditional usage of this new method. Test cases have also been added to ensure the correctness of the implementation.

### New Feature: HTML Text Replacement with Lexical
* Added a `replaceHtmlTextUsingLexical` function to replace occurrences of a term in HTML text using Lexical. This function supports options like case sensitivity, whole-word matching, and replacing specific occurrences. title: [CAN-7235] Replace removeHtmlFromText in find-filter with lexical
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and updates to the text filtering and formatting functionalities, along with some refactoring and cleanup in the codebase. Key changes include adding a new format handler for converting rich text to plain text, integrating a lexical-based text filter, and improving the modularity of the `textFilter` implementation.

### Enhancements to text formatting and filtering:
* Added a new format handler, `lexicalPlainTextFromRichTextFormatHandler`, for converting rich text to plain text in the `widget-editor/headless` module. This handler is registered in the `widgetEditors` function. (`src/mural/addons/core/editors/index.tsx`, `src/mural/addons/core/editors/lexical/widget-editor/headless/index.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a4cde9dedb3e92ab83737efc9210ae83633b6746a0ee064028b4db6363875f48R43-R46) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4cde9dedb3e92ab83737efc9210ae83633b6746a0ee064028b4db6363875f48R298-R301) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3bf6c6835c057d6817ee62c371a0ce62e9e84db7aeab05f0c3146a52d5ac9ef9R183-R196)
* Introduced a lexical-based text filter (`textFilter`) implementation, exported from `find-filter/text/index.tsx`. This filter integrates with the SDK context and supports feature-based conditional logic for text processing. (`src/mural/addons/core/find-filter/index.tsx`, `src/mural/addons/core/find-filter/text/index.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-940e1c653302f8bc2801d2d17bf50872d36ce5990662a851a6c33e67c1a8a56aL23-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4dff8b6e050ed7008edb57ea0e34901d0ca5d3668f2edbf2101fc797001a4d26R24) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4dff8b6e050ed7008edb57ea0e34901d0ca5d3668f2edbf2101fc797001a4d26L74-R75)

### Code modularity and refactoring:
* Refactored the `textFilter` to be exported as a named export instead of a default export, improving code clarity and alignment with other modules. (`src/mural/addons/core/find-filter/text/index.tsx`)
* Enhanced readability and maintainability by breaking long lines of code and improving indentation

title: [CAN-7325] Don't run uniform dragging logic when area is dragged
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes a scenario in the connector systems where uniform dragging was being wrongly considered as happening. Uniform dragging is the scenario where two widgets are connected by an arrow, and they are dragged the same distance in any direction, so when we dragged an area and the Obbs of the references of an arrow were checked, they indeed had moved the same distance thus recalculating the arrow position. Now that arrows share the parent with their references, if both of them are in the same area, uniform dragging is not really happening, because the models remained the same but their global space did change but, given that everything with a parentId is relative to the origin of that parent, we don't consider this an uniform dragging.

title: [CAN-7336] Refactor `computeGridLayout` to return a `WidgetChange` set
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is part of the effort described in [CAN-7332](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7332) but it was isolated enough to be its own PR, which will make reviewing way easier.

The function `computeGridLayout` is being used to re-generate the layout of a grid area after something has interacted with it.

In order to reduce the number of calls to `apply` and `commit` (which is the target of the mentioned card), we need to have this function simply return the list of changes and defer the updating to whoever corresponds.

In this PR we do precisely that, and add a set of guarding unit tests to prevent this intention to change in the future.

This should ideally not change any expected behavior. However, there's an implementation change here: the original code was doing `sdk.widgets.update`. And when `withSystems` was not provided explicitly, this was not running the systems.

However, with this change we're now running the systems everytime we call this, so we need to make sure that this didn't break.

The way to test this is by interacting with a grid area as much as possible: adding items, removing, changing places, etc.

**Note**: I don't want to cause a controversy here, but when testing this, please compare it to `master`, because grid areas already work quite bad so my hopes with this PR is only to not make it worst.

title: [PLAY-309] Fix: When I add a page or activity on prod, I sometimes get the"uh oh" page
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer Sometimes when I add content like a page or activity on prod I get an unexpected / unhandled error. My suspicion is that this is occurring due to a race condition: After creating content we POST the new data, fetch the updated playbook, and then redirect the user to that new content view or show the new content in the UI. It appears that we are redirecting the user before that new data has been retrieved or attempting to render that new activity before we have the data. To fix: 1. add handler for sidepanel that's causing the error to trickle up, it's getting an unexpected case (no activity), but adding extra handlers for more security 2. Add a tracker in local state for the content id being added, if it doesn't match anything in local state, wait to load the page view until it enters state. example of bug in beta: https://www.loom.com/share/ae857ba4d7aa4251a3c9df72367eb395 example of bug locally: #### Reviewer Resources - Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/PLAY-309) to understand the context of this effort. test env: https://add-content-race-condition.mural.engineering/ demo: you can see a brief flash in the 1 instance this occurs the 1st time adding content https://www.loom.com/share/d02d18a17b96448ca4769b4cd0b90239?sid=b28789ca-feed-4a1c-813f-9f94e219ff03

title: [SCQM-853] Ensure CE data is updated when copy/pasting a planner
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes copying a board would result in planner columns that did not contain widgets in `widgetOrderByWidgetId`
Now, with these changes, the appropriate widgets are mapped each columns property `widgetOrderByWidgetId` as an additional side effect after pasting.

It seems this bug was introduced [here](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/commit/77112fd681458701002085156ce062a7e17d994e#diff-3e9a36d00ff0ba0d521ccc25c3c7eb3c4175c95018e1089c84dab1f2bb40b28eL45). Removing `?? widgetId` allows duplication of boards without widgets, but it breaks copying. It would be nice to have an extra arg in this hook that allows something like: `const newWidgetId = boardOnly ?  widgetReferences[widgetId] : widgetReferences[widgetId] ?? widgetId`
but I was hesitant to make changes to the hooks themselves. Happy to dive deeper if the reviewer feels my proposed solution is not ideal.

title: [CWI-1788] Update realm call to not use authenticated call
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Recently some change were made in the sign-in routes. When using `signin-clean`, it's not waiting anymore for the session to be cleared before rendering the component. The side effect of this is that the `realm` call is called fast enough to use the session before it's cleared. (When using the `auto` parameter) When the session is expired and need to be refreshed, this is making fail the `realm` call.

This PR make sure the realm call is never using the current session to make the call. This endpoint is public and no session is required to use it.

title: Replace/clone element w dashboard props
body:
# Get rid of react.cloneElement() in DashboardView
The main change in this PR is to create a DashboardPropsContext that contains all the of high level DashboardView fields and functions that used to be prop-drilled in to each route component.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22ab1c8b-697c-45c4-a940-a102dc89b49e)


### Additional changes
Many of the props were either 1️⃣ already in another store or 2️⃣ not used at all. The props were completely removed _or_ updated to now be retrieved via their stores.

### test-env
https://clone-element-w-dashboard-props.mural.engineering/t/kevinwork5924/recents

### Notes
There were a few props that were typed differently in the component than they were defined in DashboardView. There were some small changes to account for this.
Example: `openModal` was defined as being optional, but always defined when passed in. So there's code that removes if() checks

title: [CAN-7329] Add `repositionChildren` absorption-related system
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR refactors the existing `repositionChildren` system that currently applies only to `ALL_OR_NOTHING` widgets so they apply globally to all widgets regardless of their absorption strategy.

You'll see [a commit](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43892/commits/a386020b1bb9479306cca42dbfd21c913491aa67) there doing something quite bold: making the system run unflagged.
It's a big move to do that from the beginning, but I'm willing to take the risk here: I'm making this system be completely unflagged and removing the original code that handled repositioning of children.
This means that we're going full speed on this.

I believe it's wrong to flag this under the `absorption system` flag, because repositioning children after a cluster has been resized is not really about absorption, but about keeping consistency on existing children.
I can very easily remove that commit and keep things flagged if you think we should do so, but we've learned from the connectors system experience that flagged code can extend so much that it complicates reading and bug debugging a lot.

I believe this change is making things continue working as expected, but even if it doesn't, I prefer to fix a bug on refactored and cleaner code rather than continue flagging for fear of introducing new bugs.

Let me know your thoughts on this.

The commits that you'll see after that one are fixing a specific situation that arised from doing this change directly: when you select an area and any of its children together, and resize the selection, we _don't_ want a reposition of the children because they should scale together.
However, in order to have the system avoid that situation, we first need to modify the code so the system is aware that both widgets were affected together.

title: [PLAY-300] Activity text displays default copy upon first exit of editor
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This bug was occurring due to React! because we are tracking the block description with a useState, there were some instances where the component was switching from showing editing state to view state before the new text could propagate down. 


To fix this I separated the view from the edit. This turned the view portion into a data read only component that will always rerender when a change occurs. An alternative fix would be to keep 1 component, but add 2 useEffects to track updates to the text and description.

title: [CAN-7264] Fix remote editing stickies and shapes perma lock
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer There was a bug causing the auto save feature to permanently lock stickies and shapes in "remote editing" mode even after widgets were unselected. This was caused by the existence of an editing messages queue on our Remote SDK AND the auto-save feature firing a "UPDATE_WIDGET_SELF" message. The previous implementation would enqueue editing messages, and only send them either on "UPDATE_WIDGET_SELF" or if the changes were discarded. Since auto-save would trigger an "UPDATE_WIDGET_SELF" without the widget being unselected, by the time the user unselected the widget the editing message had been enqueued, but there was no event left to actually flush the enqueued editing messages 💀 . A first attempt to fix this was to immediately send the messages when needed, however this would result in the "WIDGET_EDITING" message being received before the "UPDATE_WIDGET" one, thus showing for a brief moment the old content until the "UPDATE_WIDGET" arrived and updated the content. This bug had been fixed in https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/33095 (which introduced the concept of a editing messages queue). To fix this, we decided to move the enqueueing and subsequent flushing of the messages to the message processor. Now we only enqueue messages if a "WIDGET_EDITING" message is received and the messages informed us that the content is different from the currently saved one. In that case we let the "UPDATE_WIDGET" message process and clear the editing message queue, else we simply process the message since there are no unsaved changes. This ensures the "remote editing" feedback is cleared after the new content has been saved, and reduces the complexity of having to enqueue the message and then knowing when to flush the queue. Here is a simplified diagram of the old flow, why the auto-save bug happened and the new flow.

title: [CAN-7251] Fix mindmap remote dragging
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes a bug that occurs when dragging mindmap nodes on a remote session.
On some cases the remote instance would see the arrows connecting nodes move in a weird way, such as the image shown here:
![010b7b02-4f56-4c78-9fbc-7b981d7fcd07](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39af2e4b-3677-43ef-b9cf-c18378d6ce79)

The root cause for this comes from the fact that we use the same code for local and remote dragging. However, the issue arises when we do `sdk.widgets.changes.apply` in the remote view.
Given that this is remote code, we don't need to apply changes because it creates a stage that we'll never commit. This is exactly what was causing the issue. Different dragging instances would accumulate not-commited changes on a stage that still bases the difference on an initial stage.
If we use `remote.updateWithSystems` instead of `apply` in that case, we'll still execute all the systems (which we want so the arrows are properly updated) but we don't create any stage that would cause this issue.

The solution, while simple, required a bit of refactoring, because the code that executed the `apply` had no context on whether it was being called by a remote code or a local code.


#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7251)

title: Refactor `registerSystems` to facilitate reading the catalog
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a simple PR to refactor how we register new systems.

The current implementation of the systems catalog defines each entry as an object with an `applies` function and a `systemFn` property that's the system or systems functions.
When `applies` returns `true`, we register the system into the catalog.

This is made this way so we can flag systems easily, and that's absolutely perfect, but as we move forward with this new approach, we'll have more and more systems, and the vast majority will eventually be flagless, so to have a lot of `applies: () => true` can complicate the reading.

This PR does not remove that possibility but basically redefines the definition to allow an entry to either be the mentioned object, or simply the system itself (or systems).

This way, any system that's registered by a reference to its implemention directly will get registered without any checking, and the catalog becomes a much easier to read list.

No change in logic is expected whatsoever.
