title: [ENGAGE-854] Scaffold createContextSafe() and use in packages/route-signin
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR introduces a new state management pattern that for now will only be piloted in code owned by Engagement Team.

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
- Create `createContextSafe()` wrapper
- Write unit tests
- Update `CODEOWNERS`
- Use `createContextSafe()` pattern within `@packages/route-signin`
- Smoke test available at https://engage-854.mural.engineering/

___

## TL;DR What is `createContextSafe()`?
- It's a very shallow wrapper around `React.createContext()`
- It provides an object with `{ useContext, Provider, Consumer }`, with all three having extra protections against accessing an empty state

<details>

## Why does `createContextSafe()` look similar to the existing `createStore()`?

### Because it **_is_** similar! They both:
- return a `Context`-like object with `Consumer`, `Provider`, and a hook to access state
- have additional protections against accessing an empty state
- allow for the instantiation of a `Context` (internally) without providing an initial/default value

### So why re-invent the wheel?
Because as someone who's been using React since 2016, and both Hooks and Context since 2018, the `createStore()` pattern feels **_all wrong_**.
- It uses the word `Store` without any involvement of a `reducer`, a `dispatcher`, or `actions`
- It takes a hook as an argument despite not being a component
- In most cases these hooks are **_never_** used within a component or referenced anywhere else in code
- If your hook needs inputs, you instead pass those into the `Provider` as a `params` prop
- The `Provider`'s `params` prop **_is not_** a `value` prop, making it confusingly different from a traditional `Context.Provider`
- If you want to use `createStore()` to just pass prop values around the React tree, you have to write a hook that takes all the values you want to pass as inputs, then pass all those values into the `Provider`'s `params` prop

#### In summary, the existing `createStor

title: [CAN-7303] Remove `trackWidgets`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The function `trackWidgets` is used to apply some transformation side-effects when an action is executed indirectly over a widget, such as what happens to an arrow when a sticky is dragged.

What this function does, technically, is receive a callback function, create an instance of the widget transformation module and defer the calls to it while executing the callback in between.

However, with the changes from https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43824 where we removed the widget transformations code entirely, this function became a noop that merely executes the provided callback and does nothing more.

That's why this PR is removing `trackWidgets` altogether and modifies the callers to execute their provided callbacks directly.

No change in logic is expected whatsoever.

title: [CAN-7302] Remove widget transformations
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The `ENABLE_CONNECTORS_SYSTEM` flag controls how we apply a set of transformation to arrows that have indirectly changed due to an user action (i.e. when dragging a sticky with an arrow attached).
When the flag is off we use the `widget transformations` to execute these side effects, and when it's on we run a set of systems after each change.

The `widget transformations` module receives a boolean whose value relies on this flag. And when it's on, the module itself becomes a complete `noop`, a function that does absolutely nothing. It does not execute any logic nor changes any state.

For a couple of weeks now we have had the flag enabled for all users on all environments, thus proving that the new code is stable enough to start removing the legacy one.

So, as part of this massive removal effort, this PR deletes the `widget transformations` entirely.

Almost all calls to the module was setting the boolean flag in `true`, with two exceptions (the drag plugin of the Enhanced Kanban Board and the undoRedo api) which I believe were merely omissions rather than an explicit intention of not running the systems.
I did test fully those two behaviors with the systems approach instead, and they seem to be working as expected.

So the changes here are pretty straight forward, it's all about removing the calls to the widget transformations.

The one thing that became a problem with this change were the test suites in Cucumber (both rig v1 and rig v2).
Because they run the code with all the flags off by default, and given that the systems itself are still flagged, this change would not run the widget transformations (because they were removed) nor the systems (because they are flagged), so many tests started to fail.

In the vast majority of cases the fix consisted in enabling the flag for that particular test (or set of tests), but there are some minor cases where a particular decision had to be made. I'm

title: [CAN-7249] Prevent mindmaps from being expelled from areas when resized
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR fixes the resizing of mindmap nodes inside areas. Our code would expel widgets when resize started and reabsorb them when resize ends. Mindmap absorption ios handled by systems when the connector systems flag is enabled so this behavior is now wrong. To properly reflect what we needed for mindmaps in this PR I add a `filterFn` parameter to `detachWidgetsFromCluster` because I _only_ want to avoid expulsion in this scenario and only for mindmaps (when we implement absorption as systems this _**must**_ be removed) and add the condition to `resizeWidget` where a widget with a parentId was considered to _always_ be resized with its parent, now for mindmaps this is not true anymore. #### Reviewer Resources - Ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7249 - Env: https://can-7249.mural.engineering PR: ![pr](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a11e3a9e-6eba-44da-99cd-0a182a235aef) Master:

title: [CAN-7214] Fix repositioning of mindmap nodes when resizing an area
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes how absorption works for `ALL_OR_NOTHING` widgets (i.e. mindmaps) when the `ENABLE_CONNECTORS_SYSTEM` flag is enabled.

![Apr-22-2025 17-24-27](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d446201-b6d4-4e71-815c-9635b1470bd5)

The issue was merely in the order in which we were running the systems (absorbing/expelling first, positioning the children second), which was causing this behavior:
![Apr-22-2025 17-26-02](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe2282ba-2d78-42dd-9142-768864f523dd)

But, of course, being me, I couldn't just revert the order and that's it.
In this PR I'm organizing the code so the issue became way more easy to find, while at the same time helps us clearly see how the systems are running.
And I'm also adding some integration tests in Jest, where we're running all the systems and comparing the resulted widget store with our expectation when we resize an area from any border and on any direction.

title: [CAN-7041] Use `Matrix` to represent transformations in `Obb`
body:
**[CAN-7041 Use matrices in Obb instead of sin/cos, shift, and parent reference](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7041)**

This PR introduces `Matrix` class and use it in `Obb`.

The environmenmt: https://can-7041.mural.engineering/

## Why Matrix?

Matrices is an efficient way to apply coordinates transformatios.

It can combine multile operations into single matrix:
```typescript
const rotateAroundCenter: Matrix = Matrix.translation({ x: -cx, y: -cy })
  .rotate(alpha)
  .translate({ x: cx, y: cy });
```
Matrices can be combiled:
```typescript
const widgetToCanvas: Matrix = ...;
const canvasToScreen: Matrix = ...;

const widgetToScreen: Matrix = widgetToCanvas.then(canvasToScreen);
```

It's easy to reverse a transformation:
```typescript
const canvasToWidget: Matrix = widgetToCanvas.inverse();
```

There is a nice articles series about matrix transformations: https://graphicmaths.com/pure/matrices/matrix-2d-transformations/.

title: PLAY-284: Stakeholder Mapping LinkedIn Card
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This pull request introduces a new feature, `STAKEHOLDER_MAPPING_V1`, and integrates it with the existing LinkedIn internal integration. The changes include adding the new feature to the constants, updating feature flags, and implementing the logic for handling LinkedIn data with the mock data from Scrapin.

### Jira
https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/PLAY-284

### Demo
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58afee59-2b7c-48b9-9a59-9b93aff55cc4

Key changes:

### Feature Addition:
* Added `STAKEHOLDER_MAPPING_V1` to `FEATURES` in `optimizely-constants.ts` to track the new stakeholder mapping feature.
* Updated `muralFeatureFlags` in `flags-manager/types.ts` to include the new feature flag for enabling stakeholder mapping.

### LinkedIn Integration:
* Modified `linkedin/index.ts` to conditionally register the new `registerSmartPostPhotoWidgetCreationHandler` based on the `STAKEHOLDER_MAPPING_V1` feature flag.
* Added mock LinkedIn data in `scrapin-mock-data.json` to support the new feature.
* Implemented `registerSmartPostPhotoWidgetCreationHandler` in `register-smart-post-photo-widget-creation-handler.ts` to handle LinkedIn post photo widget creation using the mock data.

title: [CAN-7247] Fix connect menu creation in tables
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a 2 for 1 combo, you should appreciate this great opportunity! You'll be reviewing and (hopefully) approving two fixes for the price of one!

In this PR we're fixing how creation through the connect menu worked when doing it inside a table cell.

**_Look at how it works now!_**
![Apr-15-2025 17-03-43](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4475ca7c-eb5e-415a-8a5d-98168e4fcf9c)

**_And now look at how it used to work:_**
![Apr-15-2025 17-06-03](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da0f42b8-9b00-4bf8-b5ef-4e8489562621)

### So what are the two bugs?
Good question! (of course, I wrote it myself)
It wasn't quite visible in the gif and it's not actually noticeable in the app because bug 1 covers bug 2, but what was happening was that:
- When creating a widget using the connect menu inside a table, the new widget would not be positioned _inside_ the cell but rather in the canvas, using the calculated relative position as absolute.
- Even when fixing that to place the widget inside the cell, the arrow would not correctly point to the widget but rather to a random spot near the center of the widget

### The fixes
The first issue was basically caused by the function `getConnectorOffset`. It sounds weird, but it's true.
This function would return the offset between the global arrow position and its local counterpart, but it had a special case that omitted table cells as possible parents of arrows.
We do allow cells to be parent of arrows, so by fixing that, we get a correct offset, which is then used to place the newly created widget in its final position.

The second issue was a bit more complicated.
After we create the new widget, we would apply the changes and, as a special case for table cells, create an action to place the widget as child of the cell.
This action would then trigger a call to our systems.
The "connector connected system", in charge of making sure that arrows k

title: [CAN-7254] Refactor `fitTableCellToContent`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This (probably unnecessary) long PR is doing a lot of stuff and yet somehow it's actually doing one thing: refactoring `fitTableCellToContent`.

So, long story short: this function is being used in many places to make sure that whenever the content of a table cell changes, we accomodate both the cell as well as the column and row it's in to fit the new content.

Now, there are two main things that can be placed in a cell that might trigger a need to fit: text or widgets.
For the case of widgets we were good and covered, but for the case of text we had absolutely no testing coverage, because we relied only on our Cucumber test rig, which would only work for text using DraftJS and we're now using Lexical.

The intention of this PR is not to fix that situation but to add a different kind of coverage, the kind we want: unit testing.

This function doesn't care at all whether we're using DraftJS, Lexical or any other solution, so why should the tests care?

But of course, in order to have proper testing, we first need to be sure about what the function does and how it behaves depending on how we call it.

So the first big portion of this PR refactors the code a bit to make it more readable and to make it simpler while retaining the full capabilities it already had. There was a lot of old outdated code that did absolutely nothing and was still there because we forgot to remove it.

The second big portion of the PR begins to modify small things to take advantage of the `changes` api and have a function that's as pure as it can be.

The third big portion, finally, adds the expected unit tests covering both this function as well as the two functions that return the minimum sizes for a cell.
Why? Because we're mocking those functions in the unit tests for `fitTableCellToContent`, so in order to have confidence in that mocking, we need to have proper testing for those functions too.

title: [SCQM-842] Refactor some AI helpers into dispatcher and sdk
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR moves a bunch of helpers into dispatcher, sdk or more globally available locations to enable code from outside of the AI addons folder to interact with them. This will enable the creation and registration of AI features from anywhere as well as set us up for the next steps in the AI refactor effort.

This has lots of import changes, so best to be followed by commit:
1. Changes the `AI_DEBUG_MODE` flag to be an sdk state boolean. This limits our capacity to remotely toggle it through Optimizely, but the chance of leaking PII was too big. We'll try to keep it as a dev-only option as much as possible for now and only accessible through the AI Chat Inspector panel.
2. Moves the AI tokens helpers to a more accessible spot and adds the `removeHTML` option to the function that didn't have it (although we tend to use the default value always).
3. Move `showAIOperationErrorNotification()` to AI dipatcher and `getAIErrorMessageByType()` to sdk, and sorthen both function names for convenience.
4. Move `aiChat` operation creation to AI dispatcher and `AIChatResponse` to the api chat types package. (this will make moving the AI chat `sendOperation` and `sendMessages` functions easier, coming soon)
5. Move `AIChatOptions` from `/chat.ts` to `/ai.ts`. The "chat" one here refers to the legacy chat. We could eventually split the "ai" one into 2 files, but not for now.

title: Improve package json validation
body:
### Summary

This pull request makes significant changes to the `.github/workflows/quality.yml` file to improve the npm linting process and ensure package-lock consistency. The most important changes include removing an existing task, adding a new npm-linter job, and implementing steps to ensure package-lock synchronization.

Changes to npm linting and package-lock consistency:

* Removed the existing task that ensured package-lock consistency.
* Added a new `npm-linter` job that runs npm linting tasks and includes steps to compute filters and ensure package-lock consistency.
* Implemented a step to check if the package-lock file is in sync with the package.json file and provide instructions if discrepancies are found.

title: [SCQM-825][SCQM-845] Kill multi cluster and result picker
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR kills multi-cluster and result picker as they are not needed anymore. And updates preview mode feedback toast notification.
It is done in 3 commits:
- The first commit updates the function calling and some other stuff to start using single-clustering always, although some parts were still a bit rough and cleaned up in the other commit.
- The second commit removes all the "resutls" and result-picker logic, does the remaining multi-clustering cleanup and removes the tests that no longer apply.
- The third commit updates the feedback toast notification to comply with https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-845 using a more generic solution that should be scalable when new features are added to preview mode.

In the end we should be left with a more streamlined clustering logic, still supporting preview mode when enabled and a simplified `previewController` since it no longer needs to handle results-picker stuff.

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [CAN-7229] Fix tables persistance when expanding a cell
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes the following bug:
When the `ENABLE_CONNECTOR_SYSTEMS` flag is on, if you typed enough text on a cell to cause the entire row to grow, the new size for the row would not be persisted.

_PR:_
![Apr-08-2025 13-59-04](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2929f39e-24d0-4a18-ae46-bd3dfbe5334c)

_Master:_
![c9c49b9c-705a-47ad-81d6-e915ac851484](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68fcb438-2c89-4f43-b9d9-829ecf67c5a9)

### Context
The issue occurred because, when the flag is enabled, we're calling `sdk.widgets.changes.updateWithSystems` instead of doing an `sdk.widgets.update` or `sdk.widgets.changes.updateWithoutSystems`.

This method would apply the provided changes to the local model and run the set of systems but, unlike `sdk.widgets.changes.apply`, it will **not** stage the changes.
So when trying to persist the edition, there would be no initial stage, so the diff between initial and current would be empty and nothing would get persisted.

The fix consists in simply using `apply` instead of `updateWithSystems`.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7229)

title: [CAN-7221] Fix remote dragging effect after dragging has finished
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is the final step in what became a much bigger effort than expected.

The main goal of this PR is to fix a bug that happened when using mindmaps with remote collaborators under the `ENABLE_CONNECTORS_SYSTEM` flag.

The problem was that when a remote dragging finished, both the remote and the local mindmaps would break because any children of the dragging node would be positioned in a wrong place.

This was due to the fact that we were calling `afterDragEnd` (our handler for finishing a local dragging) when finishing a remote dragging.
This method was calculating a final state of the widgets after the dragging and persisting those changes.
However, for the remote end we don't need to do that at all, because we'll be receiving an `UPDATE_WIDGET` event with that information.
Therefore this PR fixes the situation by removing that call.

The unit tests that the code had was wrongly asserting implementation instead of behavior, and that's why this was undetected.
A new set of tests is added to assert the expected behavior of this realtime processor.

In order to test this properly you should open two sessions on the same mural, create a mindmap with more than one level of children and then move the mindmap around, change directions, attach to other nodes, etc.
Both the remote and the local sessions should work as expected.

**Important:** there's another related bug detected here which is _not_ being fixed by this PR.
During a dragging, the remote end will show the arrows wrongly, they will assign the right start and end position but the middle points would get a wrong calculation, which can potentially affect the end result after dropping.
Given that this is mostly fixed after dropping, and that it's not related to what we're doing here, it will not be fixed in this PR.
This card is created to handle that secondary problem: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7251

title: [CPT-2231] Fix/small rows
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The previous responsive layout was adjusting the number of columns based on the container's width, maintaining a minimum column width of 150px. While this provided flexibility, it led to inconsistent column widths in different container sizes. We want to fix that. This change is comparable to the [quick sketch ](https://zingy-crisp-d0e293.netlify.app/) that Ryan Nee made, "which has responsive rows but not responsive cards."
![Screenshot 2025-04-03 at 2 17 29 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80d2d8b8-d712-4fbf-a4d1-11d6927b39df)

- For "small" `cardWidth` only, (which was defined from the backend API),  this PR modifies the grid layout configuration in our CSS from a responsive layout using auto-fill and minmax(150px, 1fr) to a fixed layout with repeat(50, 1fr).
-- By switching to a fixed configuration of 50 equal-width columns, we aim for a more uniform grid appearance across different sections and screen sizes. This change ensures each column takes up one fraction (1fr) of the available space, maintaining a consistent layout.

title: [CAN-7231] Move remote edition broadcasting to dispatcher
body:
This PR moves the remote broadcasting into the dispatcher instead of the business rules for edition.

The business rule is now dealing with setting the proper state, upon which the rest of the edition protocol will be fired (the editor mounted, the dispatcher called from UI to orchestrate the edition flow).

When the edition ends, the dispatcher will send the remote event to end the edition, and call a business rule to update the state back to a non-editing state.

JIRA: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7231

title: [CAN-7221] Refactor mindmaps dragging hooks to prevent wrong commits
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a big piece of work that started [here](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43560), continued [here](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43596) and is now here ⬇ (where is not really ending, sadly)

You can look at the previous PRs and the associated card to find out a bit more about the context for these changes, but what's important here is what _this PR_ does:
Our mindmap dragging hook handlers have the task of managing the consequences of dragging a mindmap node. That is making sure that the children follow the dragging node, that they change direction accordingly if needed and that they can get attached to other nodes when hovering them.

Our problem here is precisely with our `afterDragEnd` hook handler, which is the one that handles the end state of the operation and persisting all the changes calculated. This method is, in fact, doing that, but it's doing most of that stuff in an indirect way.
While there is a call to `commit` there as a final step, sadly it's not _the only call to `commit`_ that takes place within that operation. That's because some of the internal functions and helpers are also committing changes, which makes us lose a bit of control on when our local widget model is modified.

The aim of this PR is to address that and have a consistent, unique, and controlled place where changes are applied.

To reach that goal, we now handle the last of our functions here: `checkForNewParent`. That's the only thing within `afterDragEnd` that was also committing changes indirectly.

After this work here is done, we'll have that everything inside `afterDragEnd` can only generate a list of `WidgetChange` but is not allowed to push any of those changes, and is this `afterDragEnd` function the one responsable for doing that.

It's very important to note here that **this PR does not attempt to modify any behavior whatsoever**.
Every piece of code should behave and act exact

title: [CAN-7221] Refactor `rearrangeNodes` to return a list of changes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

**It's highly recommended to review this using the `Hide whitespace` option on**

This is part of the bigger effort that is fixing the bug reported in https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7221.

The big problem there is that our remote processor for mindmaps is using the same code as the dragging hook handler, which is a very conscious decision given that we expect both local and remote dragging to behave exactly the same.
However, the big issue here is that the code executed in `afterDragEnd` is persisting changes by doing `commit`, which is something we _don't_ want on a remote processor.

The thing is that the code in there, while it seems relatively easy to follow, has a lot of spaghetti code where inner functions are also doing `commit` everywhere.

Refactoring it all is a massive task, and so it needed to be split into smaller chunks.

This one handles the code for `rearrangeNodes`, our function to accomodate nodes after a change in layout.

This PR modifies that function (and everything inside) to only generate a list of `WidgetChange` but not apply or commit anything, a responsability that is now handled by the callers of said function.

It's very important to note here that **this PR does not attempt to modify any behavior whatsoever**.
Every piece of code should behave and act exactly the same as it did before these changes, we're just modifying where the calls are being made, but we're not modifying _how_ or _why_ they are being made.
We'll address that, if needed, on a different PR.

Given that this affects the re-arranging of nodes, you should test that moving nodes around, switching sides and attaching them to other nodes all work as expected, both when the `connnectors system` flag is on and off.

title: [SCQM-819] Frontend support for AI_GENERATE_CHANGE_SUMMARY
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This adds preliminary frontend support for the new `/ai/generate-change-summary` endpoint and `AI_CHANGE_SUMMARY_READY` real-time result in tactivos/mural-api#13409.
The infrastructure (contentApi method, realtime handling) are added and a new AIOperation has been created to request a changes summary for a group of widgets.

For the POC, a flagged pair of Explore with AI dropdown menu items have been added which will use the lastUpdate timestamp of the (first) selected widget and summarize all changes since then. There are two different options to allow testing results when ignoring the current user's own changes vs. including them. The dropdown items are just POC stand-ins for implementing this inside the AI Hub as a feature and using the timestamp of the selected widget is a stand-in for using the user's previous visit timestamp (which is not implemented yet and also this allows testing of different timestamps to see the effect on results).

To test this, the `feat-mu-enable-ai-catch-me-up` flag must be enabled in the flag manager with persistence and the mural reloaded to add the new entries to the AI dropdown menu.
![catch-me-up flags](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a0c6fa6-42c9-4feb-b639-e998321d95c7)

body:

This is a follow-up of https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43529

This PR replaces the `AIChatFeature` type with plain `string` to ensure addon extensibility, but to prevent inconsistencies it adds a `KnownAIFeatures` enum. title: [SCQM-827] Remove <15 reclustering validation
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR removes the <=15 widgets validation when deciding if the `Try with fewer/more clusters` suggestion pills will be shown since it is no longer relevant and we can properly handle cluster count in our prompt.

**NOTE**: Keep in mind that we still have other rules for showing these pills to avoid extreme cases like showing the "fewer" option when the total clusters are already too few or showing the "more" option when the widgets are already too spread (as in, having one widget per cluster doesn't make sense).
Also, depending on the content being clustered, it might not do a good job creating more or fewer clusters at some point and just return the same result, it is to be expected.

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-827) to understand the context of this effort.
- 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://scqm-827-recluster-under-15.mural.engineering) to perform a smoke test. ([all testing envs](https://testing-envs.mural.engineering))

Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes
1. Create 15 or less stickies with text and cluster them
2. See that the  `Try with fewer/more clusters` suggestion pills are visible (as long as there are not too few stickies, or too many clusters already)

title: [EN-3241] fix: show 0 as a value in duration
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

It's possible for a company to have a "0" duration value set in their guests setting duration (either forced or defaults). But since "0" is a falsey value, we are showing the default (14 days) instead, which is confusing because that's not what's stored in the database.

Furthermore, this impact the "isDirty" computation in other pages, such as the internal settings page. It was preventing the "save or discard" logic from being triggered.

title: Use `WidgetStore` whenever's possible in mindmap code
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a very straightforward PR.
The real objective of this PR is to actually prepare the field for a next set of changes, but these were isolated enough that they could very easily convey one small(-ish) PR on its own.

The goal of this PR is to use, whenever's possible, an instance of the `WidgetStore` to obtain information related to mindmaps instead of accessing the `widgets` sdk api.

Why? Well, mainly because sending the `store` instead of the api assures us that the method is not making any changes to our local widget model, given that the store in itself is immutable.
But also because it facilitates writing unit tests, because we don't need to mock the `WidgetStore`, it's an encapsulated class that can be instantiated in any Jest test the same as how we use it in the app.

So each commit in this PR does a one to one replacement on a mindmap utilitary function.

No change in logic is expected whatsoever, since every method replaced here was originally using the same store that we're now sending (via the `widgets` sdk in the _before_ version).

- 🎫 [**Jira ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7221)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://store-mindmaps.mural.engineering)

title: [SCQM-797] Migrate all AI Features to use registry system
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR moves all AI features to use the new registry-based solution. This is one of the biggest steps in the AI features refactoring effort.
This meant moving all `AIFeatureSpec` to use the new version which is registered as addon extensibility points. Besides the flexibility it provides, it makes it easier to unify all feature-specific definitions in a single point and reduces clutter.
This PR can be followed by commit:
- [50a1412](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43529/commits/50a1412dabdb05362f85bd00fa82225973762202): Rename the old `AIFeatureSpec` prop `name` to `title` to avoid collision with Extension's `name` prop.
- [4b86f30](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43529/commits/4b86f30e39c6de8bca1bef88237e661b1aaa328e): Register all AI features in the new system, while retaining the old one.
- [ade17cd](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43529/commits/ade17cd19e071b610c9b640438259732a7246ec6): (This is the biggest one of all commits, I wanted to split it but it was to entangled, sorry) Migrate all AI Features to use registry. For this we:
  - Replace all `launchFunction()` calls for `dispatcher.ai.chat.startChat()`.
  - Replace fetching features from `ALL_FEATURES` in favor of searching in the registry. This means we need to support possible `undefined` features in some places we didn't before, but nothing that breaking, mostly small validations in UI components.
- [ea0a93c](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43529/commits/ea0a93cd85eb756a547083db9dba2c530a7ea3fc): Moved AI features' `trackingId` to each feature registration to showcase the unifying benefits of this new approach.

title: Fix/playbook UI bugs
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Issues this PR fixes: 
1. we have inconsistent styling across pages with similar ui 
2. the topbar was causing the page's horizontal scroll to trigger because of the competing padding and margins

What I did. 

The page component has built in padding that made styling our topbar really difficult. To fix this I removed the padding and created shared classnames to add the padding back in only where we want it. To the left of the side panel and to the right of the mrl main. I did this to avoid wrapping these components in a shared parent that could make styling harder. 

In doing this I was able to remove a ton of styling to the topbar, and instead use it's default height, and add a secondary small height for our UI. 

In creating these shared classnames, I was able to make the styling for the sidebars the same across all page.

title: [CAN-7186] Refactor widget absorption for ALL_OR_NOTHING strategy
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

First of all, I want to apologize for what you're about to read.  

I went over this a thousand times, and in the end, I had no choice but to start everything from scratch. So this PR might be a bit hard to follow, but I think we’ll get through it together.  

Let me start by giving you some context.  

### How Systems Work  
This might be redundant information at this point, but for the sake of understanding the change, it’s important to be clear on what a system operates on.  

A system is always executed after an operation. It doesn’t know what operation was executed—the only context it has is the widget store before the change, the widget store after the change, and the list of widget ids involved (plus the rebder engine, but that’s not relevant here).  
Based on this, the system determines what changes it wants to apply and returns them.  

### How the Current Absorption System Works  
The system we currently have for handling the absorption of widgets that follow the `ALL_OR_NOTHING` strategy is not exactly wrong, but it's not entirely comprehensive either.  

What do I mean by that? Well, here’s a quick rundown of how it currently works:  
- First, we check if the operation that was executed is relevant to our goal (resized areas or dragged `ALL_OR_NOTHING` widgets).  
- Then, we scan the list of widget ids and extract three groups:  
  1. Areas that contain `ALL_OR_NOTHING` widgets.  
  2. Areas that are candidates to absorb `ALL_OR_NOTHING` widgets.  
  3. Areas that were simply included in the list of ids.  

Once we have that information, we iterate over the areas one by one, and for each area:  
- We scan for widgets that are no longer overlapping and remove them.  
- We scan for widgets that are now overlapping and absorb them.

title: [EN-3218] fix: always show all ticks in the X-Axis
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

We are passing a value of `YYYYMMM` which is used by `<Recharts />` to compute the space taken by the label, but we are in fact transforming its value to only show the 3-letters month (Jan, Feb, etc.) on the X-Axis as `MMM`.

This forces Recharts to always show all ticks in the X-Axis as labels by setting the [interval](https://recharts.org/en-US/api/XAxis#interval) option to `0`.

Also see https://github.com/recharts/recharts/issues/397 for the initial hint to use that option.

**Before**

![Screenshot 2025-03-28 at 17 32 33](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/490d7820-c423-4dc6-aebd-83b5554d4dbe)

**After**

title: [SCQM-702] Fix voting results scrolling
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, once the width of all the voting session names extended beyond the current browser window size, the user could no longer select or view those subsequent sessions.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1145821e-5588-4146-b17e-9fee7a9cd2bb)

Now, with these changes, the scroll arrows work as expected.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58018166-95a5-4459-96f3-9d509d259fcc)


#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-702) to understand the context of this effort.
- Please see this  🎬 [**demo**](https://www.loom.com/share/6dd47a4cd54148778d69b1f12c42462e) of the acceptance criteria for the above ticket
- 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://voting-results-scrolling.mural.engineering) to perform a smoke test.

- Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes
1. Create a voting session (give it a longer title if you want to create fewer sessions)
2. Cast your vote
3. End the session
4. Repeat (1, 2, 3) at least 5 times; enough so a thinner window results in overflow
5. Shrink the width of your tab/window so that you cannot see all the session titles
6. Play around with the left / right arrows and resizing the width of your window at different item stops
7. Everything should behave nicely

Of particular note:
A) give the "last session" a "really long name" and play around trying to see the right-most part at various widths
B) add another session with a short name after that to see how it behaves then

- [x] No new cucumber tests were added 
- [ ] Exception: no unit tests were added or updated for this change

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

title: [CAN-7116] Fix toolbar menu broken selected state
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer There was a desync between a tool's selected state, and the menu being opened. This happened because we were never setting the 'isSelected' state property to the toolbar button if we had childTools. The menu was using it as a triggerRef, so it would still render the child tools menu even if the selected state was false. To fix this I removed the conditional check so the button's state works as the rest of the toolbar buttons, and added the actionState to the `ToolbarMenuAdapter`, this way both it's opened and the button's isSelected state acts as the single source of truth. By doing this, the issue appeared fixed but we were actually rendering two menus, so I removed the extra renderMenu call we were passing to `ToolbarButtonAdapter`. Finally, after fixing this. The mobile xs comments addon was not working as expected. This was due to it's selected state being set on tool creation through a tool factory. I removed the factory since it was getting to complicated to make it compatible with both use cases. (Desktop browser vs mobile browser) #### Reviewer Resources - Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7116) to understand the context of this effort. - 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://toolbarmenu-selected-state.mural.engineering) to perform a smoke test. ([all testing envs](https://testing-envs.mural.engineering)) - Steps to reproduce: 1. Click the 'Facilitation' tools in the topbar or the downwards chevron next by the mural's title 2. Click outside of the menu 3. Repeat step 1. 4. Focus on the button's selected state

title: [CAN-7169] Fix requestAnimationFrame overwrite bug
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

So, this is a funny story.

We have detected a weird behavior in some parts of our canvas integrity that were really hard to spot, find or debug.

The visual indication is visible in the following two gifs:
![Mar-25-2025 14-35-31](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9b45e33-6139-489d-81f4-f90e51bc0401)

![Mar-25-2025 14-35-37](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ef8cbe0-2df6-4ace-a895-af3cab6f9241)


We were able to identify the problem: the new `identity-and-access-management` package was exporting a test utilitary file that, on its first line, was overwriting `window.requestAnimationFrame` with a custom implementation that would cause desynchronization among our entire app.

This is a file that provides utils for some testing scenarios. However, by moving it into a package and exporting it, we were causing the code inside to get executed as soon as anyone imported that package for any reason.

The fix in this PR consists in moving those overwrites inside the exported function, so the tests using it would still function but the code will only get executed when someone explicitly calls `mockLocation`, not upon importing the package itself.

### How to test
We have, so far, identified two visible situations where this was affecting our code: when dragging a mindmap node and when resizing the canvas window. There might be more, but we can confidently pinpoint them to this particular bug, so a good test would be checking that those two situation are no longer reproducible.
Also, the unit test that was using this code should still be functioning, but you can assert that by checking that the build finishes successfully.

**Test enviroment:** https://iam-raf-bug.mural.engineering/
_(still building)_

title: [SCQM-232] Require AI to ask before running deleteElements
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Card: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-232
Env: https://scqm-232-ask-before-delete.mural.engineering/
mural-api PR: tactivos/mural-api#13304

This adds a `confirmed: true` required argument to the `deleteElements` function and returns an error if the argument is not sent. Combined with the description of the argument in its definition (tactivos/mural-api#13304) this pushes the AI to always ask the user before calling `deleteElements` to confirm that they want to delete the elements.

The `deleteElements` function was also moved out of the old `widgets.ts` file into its own `delete-elements.ts` file and tests were added.

To test, especially try situations where it might chain the function. E.g. "Generate 3 ideas about penguins and then delete any that don't mention fish" (`generateIdeas` and then `deleteElements`) or "Delete the red sticky notes in my selection" (`getSelectedElements` and then `deleteElements`).

Known issue: Triggering when a parallel function call includes deleting is hit-or-miss. At the moment, parallel functions are broken in prod and beta so this isn't a pressing concern but following up on this if it is shown to be a problem once available in production might require moving to a system where the deleteElements function itself implements a confirmation UI or making use of the preview mode.

title: [EN-3173] Invalidate search queries after succesful mutations
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors and updates the mutation hooks used to make changes to company workspaces via the new Company Workspaces view. Main goals:
- Add fuzzy query invalidation logic to post-mutation handlers. This is important to avoid the scenario described in the ticket where a user will see accurate data after a mutation due to the optimistic update but might then see stale/cached data if they change to a search that contains the mutated data
- Updates the keys for the `search*` hooks to use separate indices for the `companyId` and additional search options. This allows for invalidating _any/all_ cached data for a company via the fuzzy query matching behavior noted above.
- Adds some generic typing to improve the flexibility of shared functions for optimistic updates

title: [CAN-7048] [CAN-7145] Make type of `WidgetChange` explicit
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR addresses some simple type-guard modifications.
First of all, an utilitary function `toWidgetChanges` is created to easily convert several input types to `WidgetChange[]`, which is what our `processChanges` function needs.

Next, a new method `apply` has been added to the `WidgetStore` so it can, within itself, process all types of `WidgetChange` regardless of whether they are creational, removal or update.

Then, with that change in place, the `WidgetStore.update` method has been refactored to process exclusively `WidgetUpdateChange` changes, instead of the more generic `WidgetChange`.

Finally, the `calculateDerivatives` method is now refactored to take advantage of this `apply` method and keep its internal copy of the store up-to-date on each iteration.

These are mostly changes in interface, so no functional change is expected.

title: [CAN-7133] [CAN-7128] Refactor `ALL_OR_NOTHING` absorption systems
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is only the first part, so you go imagine how the rest is gonna be.

Even though this is linked to a card about implementing absorption as a system, this is actually a pre-work to that.

We currently have four systems handling absorption and expulsion of widgets that work under the `ALL_OR_NOTHING` strategy (i.e. mindmaps).
Two handle dragging mindmaps over areas, and two handle resizing an area over mindmaps.

This PR unifies everything so they all share the same behavior, bringing consistency to the code.

Regardless of whether we were dragging or resizing, what we want here is to check if an area had a mindmap and is not overlapping it anymore (in which case it should expel it) of if it didn't have a mindmap but is now overlapping (in which case it should absorb it).
That is true regardless of whether we were dragging or resizing.

You should not expect any change in behavior here, except the fixes from [CAN-7128](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7128), which are applied in the first commits.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ **JIRA tickets**: [CAN-7133](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7133) & [CAN-7128](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7128) to understand the context of this effort.
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://all-or-nothing-systems.mural.engineering)

#### What you should check for
We're targetting two specific behaviors here: resizing an area over and out of a mindmap, and dragging a mindmap over and out an area.
Make sure that all those cases continue working as expected. That is, mindmaps are only absorbed into the area if they're fully inside it. If any part of the mindmap is not overlapping an area, then none of it is absorbed.

title: [PLAY-142] When I add content to an Activity Card, the border goes from dotted to solid
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

We made an update to refetches to only refetch the playbook if the updated content was seen in multiple locations. This inadvertently broke the outlines, because when a user updated just a content block, we never refetched, so we never knew that the content block was dirty until the user refreshed the page. The fix was simply to refetch after every update, because every card needs to know if a content child has had text added, so we can properly determine the card state. 


reasons to remove `shouldUpdate` check
- as described we can't tell how to render the activity card
- When a user adds a content to text, url, or activity or updates the page description we won't render those updates in the overview until they refetch

title: [SCQM-391] Make AI functions work on widgets within table cells
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Updates a few checks to make sure that AI functions work with table text as well as text widgets within tables. I also went ahead and made it work for areas and groups too because I noticed that was not working / it was easy enough to add an extra check. 

So in summation, `Translate` / `Rewrite` / `Spellcheck` / `Classify by Sentiment` / `Summarize` should now all work on:
1. table cell text
2. text widgets within table cells
3. area text (title)
4. text widgets within areas
5. text widgets within groups

### Testing
To test table:
1. Create a table, add text to a cell
2. In another cell add a sticky with text (bonus points: add other widgets with text like a shape / heading / paragraph) 
3. Verify refine functions work when you select the whole table
4. Verify refine functions work when you select a single table cell
5. Verify the classify by sentiment function works on the sticky with text 

To test group:
1. Create a group of stickies with text
2. Verify refine functions work on the group 

To test area:
1. Create an area, add a title
2. Add a sticky with text (bonus points: add other widgets with text like a shape / heading / paragraph) 
3. Verify refine functions work on both title and widgets inside the area

title: [CAN-7142] Refactor derivatives to use store comparison
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes a bug reported when attempting to create a template containing a table.

The issue was that the generated table would look messy because it didn't run the layout computation.
This was due to the fact that the method checking the need for computation was not considering creational changes.

This PR addresses the situation by changing the way derivatives in general calculate changes: instead of using the generated changes from the apply call, it uses the same approach as the other methods use: it checks the difference between the initial store and the current store, and calculates based on _those_ changes.

title: [SCQM-709] Show error toast for custom error `widget-update-while-voting-error`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Not sure how the user got into a state where they were able to make a widget update call while a voting session was active, but this change should prevent it in the future. 

In the api, throw a 400 with a custom error message to circumvent front end retry logic.
In the front end, show a disappearing toast when that 400 is received instead of [retry logic.](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/master/src/amp/apply-changes-to-mural.ts#L140)

### Relevant Links 🔗
- [**API PR**](https://github.com/tactivos/mural-api/pull/13286)

https://www.loom.com/share/77a71c3ea7ba48b1843203f047210581?sid=292ec812-7494-47b9-b8b2-887674f74a10

### To test
1. Add a sticky, copy its ID 
2. Start a voting session
3. Via the console run `sdkContext.widgets.update(*ID*, { height: 500 })` 
4. Verify the widget update call fails with a 400
5. Verify the error toast appears
6. Verify no retries occur

title: Fix hooks non-wrapped imports
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
The Hooks SDK api uses some types that, by our linter rules, should not have access to.
However, those are special situations that do need to bypass the rules, but in order to discourage a wrong usage, some "wrapped types" were created to address the situation.

However, the types file containing those wrapped types was extended over time with more local imports which, because of how VSCode manages import sorting, got caught within these wrapped types even they're not such.

This PR simply moves those imports out of the wrapping.

title: [STT-110] Instant slide change
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes we were moving from one slide to the next with a "scroll" or "pan" animation.
Now, with these changes, we jsut update the viewport and there's no animation

Prior to these changes, with the scroll animation, moving from slide 1-2 may skip over many widgets associated with slide 3,4,5,6 etc...

The intended result is that elements on the canvas and their x/y position has no impact on the presentation experience. Now, only the outline arrangement/order is relevant.

title: [CAN-7062] Prevent `Organize into area` when partial mindmaps are selected
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR addresses a particular situation that is currently happening with mindmaps:
Given that mindmaps can only be absorbed in their entirety (either the entire mindmap is absorbed or none of its members is), when we select _some_ nodes, we would ideally **not** want the context menu option `Organize into area` to show up, so we can prevent the unwanted situation of a user organizing a partial mindmap only to find that it wasn't absorbed at all.

In this PR we remove the option from the context menu whenever a partial mindmap is selected, and only show it if the entire set of nodes from the mindmap is selected.
Connectors don't need to be part of the selection because they will always be absorbed anyway when doing the organizing.

![Mar-17-2025 16-49-53](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1defb5e-ec7c-41e9-a646-d9689bc6a1ea)

title: Trigger build for branches pushed without a PR
body:
When a PR is created this workflow has already ran
for the HEAD commit of the branch because it's push-triggered (see #43279)

Having a restriction about only building for branches with a PR means
the workflow appears failed until a commit is pushed after the PR is created
which is wrong.

The downside is that we will do builds for branches without PRs but I expect
those are very few.

title: Toolbar IA Clean up
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, we had the styles defined in the `layout` style
sheet. The core team is releasing an Information Architecture (IA)
update which complicates our change.

Specifically, it complicates our concern because they are dynamically
choosing between one of two style sheets. One assuming the new IA, the
other assuming the old IA.

Since we are using CSS modules, in our markup we import the new style-
sheet and associate it's class name -- which has a dynamically appended
suffix at build time. We have the exact same class name and rules in
the old style sheet, but it has a different suffix which we do not
associate with the markup.

The net result of all this is that when the new IA is in place, our
styles are applied because we (a) load the new style sheet and (b) have
a class name from that style sheet applied to our markup. However,
if we are using the old IA (which we are doing in production), we have
only the new-IA's class name defined in our markup, but that style sheet
is not used.

title: [CAN-7129] Prevent snapping suggestions on mindmap nodes
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
With the new connnectors system flag enabled, when we drag a mindmap node we get an annoying list of suggestions for snapping lines to align our dragging node to other widgets.

This is probably due to the fact that the way the dragging of nodes work with the flag on is that we only have the dragging node selected and all the other nodes move along with it.

This is causing the snapping api to suggest all those other nodes as “potential widgets to snap to”, which is something that didn’t happen before because dragging with the flag off would select all the nodes that come along, and the snapping api ignores selected widgets as potential suggestions.

This PR fixes that situation by implementing a new hook handler for the snapping operation to modify the list of potential widgets and exclude those that belong to the same mindmap that we're dragging.

title: [SCQM-662] Remove empty comment restriction upon persisting changes.
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

**This is a workaround to fix a very specific bug, and not a proper solution**

Due to the recent modifications on how we implement changes on the widgets the following issue has arised:

1. Create a comment widget
2. Drag it around
3. Add some text to it in the right bar panel and save it
4. Refresh the page

The expected result would be to have the comment as we created it, but the actual result is that the comment is not present, nor is it recoverable.

The reason for this is related to how the updating of widgets happen with the recent changes.

Before these changes, when we created a comment, we would call `sdk.widgets.add(commentId)` and specify `avoidPersistance` in `true` to prevent the widget to be persisted until we were ready for it.
Once the widget was ready, we called `sdk.widgets.update(commentId)` but this time sending `avoidPersistance` in`false`.

The new approach handles stuff differently: you first apply all the changes you need locally (this includes creation, updating, etc) and once you're ready you commit everything to the backend.
The main difference here is that `commit()` is an atomic operation that expects no arguments. You don't choose _what to commit_, you commit everything that has changed.

When we create a comment, we apply the creational change but don't commit it, and when we type some text and press `Save`, that's when we commit.

However, if we create a comment, _but before adding text to it we drag it around_, **we are committing an operation** (the movement of the widget), and since committing sends everything that has changed, this also includes the creation of the comment.

**But...** (and a very important "But"), here's the thing: we have a restriction that says that comments that have no text content cannot be persisted.
And this is where the bug arises.

This workaround removes that restriction so the comment always exist and we don't risk los

title: [CAN-7127] Fix bug when trying to suspend snapping
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This is a simple fix for a bug that would cause the snapping suspension to not work at all.

When you drag a widget you get a suggestion of snapping lines that would allow you align your widget with others, but if you don't want those suggestions, you can press down on `Ctrl` or `Cmd` to disable them temporarily.

This was not working at the moment.

The problem was that the widget composition code had a logic where if a widget was overlapping a composition, snapping would get suspended, but upon exiting it, it would resume it.
However, the code was lacking the context of "this was inside a composition before", so on every drag movement, if the widget was not overlapping a composition, the snapping would be resumed.
So if you were pressing down the modifier key to suspend it, this code would resume it back for you.

title: [CAN-7060] Rewrite mindmap `setOrientation` when systems are enabled to use a local copy of the store and have up to date models
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR refactors how `setOrientation` works when the connector system flag is enabled. The main reason for the original bug was that when doing the `setOrientation` feature, the nodes were still absorbed even though their bounds would not overlap with the parent anymore. This caused that when expelling the mindmap, the nodes position was completely lost.

The new implementation, although it repeats some code (the original code will be deleted soon when we remove the flag from the code), is more explicit on the intention of each of the moving parts by splitting these into functions with a proper name. It uses the model coordinates as the source of truth.

It also reorders how the absorption systems are organized in the file system and, finally fixes a bug in the `allOrNothingExpulsionSystem` where the store being used for each change being processed needs to be up to date, so we use a local copy of the store in the system and update it with the expulsion changes.

It also refactors some helpers to use the store instead of the sdk, this allows us to update the store while some feature is being processed and always have up to date models.

title: [CAN-7118] Bring back the dispatcher type guard
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Our `dispatcher` api is, as the name itself implies, our entry point for dispatching commands.

In an ideal (and our initially conceived) architecture, it's our way for React views to execute actions that would modify the state, to which the same views would then connect to in order to reflect those changes visually.
As such, the `dispatcher` is a place where we **execute actions**, but not a place where we **query results**.

Because of this, we want to make sure that every method in the dispatcher api focuses only in the execution, and a good way of doing this is by enforcing it to _never return a result_.

We used to have a very clever type guard that enforced that, but [we lost it along the way](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/41099) when doing a clean-a-thon.
The reason that happened was because our type guard would prevent TS compilation, but was not _used_ in the code, and therefore our `knip` tool took it away.

This PR brings it back and in a more TS friendly way, so it shouldn't get removed again (hopefully :crossed_fingers: )

Now, during these dark times, where the `dispatcher` was hopelessly unguarded, two mischievous functions got exposed with an implementation that returned a result, defying the very heart and soul of this api.

Those functions are being addressed here to restore the faith in humanity.

#### Reviewer Resources

title: [CAN-7111] Fix bug when switching direction
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes a really specific bug with mindmaps when appending a node to another mindmap.

The fix:
![Mar-13-2025 16-54-58](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/020ebd7f-2464-44fd-b2a0-53fbeb9da338)

The bug:
![Mar-13-2025 16-54-19](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb279e29-69ef-4a26-831f-a36090649da3)

The problem was using a wrong value in the calculation that checks if the `y` value should be flipped.
Because of the specificity of where the value was used, this only affected the case where we would try to follow a node that originally had a horizontal orientation but now changed to a vertical orientation, and whose horizontal direction is not orthogonal to the new vertical direction (so a 'left' node going to a 'bottom' node, and similar).

The fix consists in using the right value, same that we were using for the `x` axis, simple as that.

title: [EN-3121] use optimistic update pattern for actions
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR updates the five existing data mutations (suspend, restore, change end date, upgrade and delete) to optimistically update the table data when a mutation is triggered, only rolling it back if an error is encountered. This is necessary as the update company workspaces endpoint is asynchronous / updated data will generally not be immediately available for reading when the response comes back from a successful update.  There is a caveat noted that because of this async behavior, it is possible that a user will change their search query quickly enough after a mutation that the updated workspace(s) will appear with their old/stale state. This will be addressed by https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/EN-3168

title: [STT-84] Keyboard Shortcuts for Active Presentation laser esc
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Prior to these changes when a user started using the laser during a presentation, they would get a notification for them to use the `ESC` key to stop the laser.

This was inaccurate -- we send the user into the browser-engaged `fullscreen` mode. Pressing ESC is not overridable -- as a security feature of this api, pressing ESC must result in the end of this fullscreen mode.

On pressing `ESC`, the user's presentation would unexpectedly end and the laser would still be active.

Now, with these changes, we change this notification to suggest the user use the `L` key during an active presentation. We then support this shortcut, along with two others for convenience (`p` and `shift + p` to start a presentation) which will only be available if the flag is present.

title: Refactor `followNode` to not apply changes directly
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR works both as a POC and a functional change.

The function `followNode` from mindmaps is our way to provide the functionality of gathering all the descendants of a node and making sure they are following it on its new position based on a provided layout that specifies how the branch is layed out.

This function uses our `changes` api to perform the needed updating.
The way it used to work prior to this PR was that we would get a list of all the widget changes we needed to properly place the children of the node, then apply those changes to have our local model updated, and then reposition the arrows connecting those nodes, based on this updated model. Finally, we would apply this last set of changes to have the entire functionality in the model.

In this PR we refactor that. We no longer apply any change in this function. Instead, we use an initial store, generate all the changes by working internally with an internal store that we maintain updated after each set of changes, and finally return everything that we generated for someone else to apply it to the local model.

The end result is exactly the same, functionality-wise, but this method is now completely free of the `WidgetsSdkApi` and is non-disruptive as it doesn't change the local model in any way. 

You should not expect any change in behavior here.

And as mentioned in the first line, this is a sort of POC, so it only applies to `followNode` as a proof of concept, to see if we can safely extend this logic to other methods.
If so, we'll create PR for those changes too.

**Test env:** https://follow-node-with-store.mural.engineering/

So this is a nice turn of events, as you'll see soon.

If you take a look at the associated cards, the report was that there were problems when pasting copied mindmap nodes onto another mindmap.

But that was just the tip of the iceberg.

What this PR handles is fixing several issues that came as consequence of appending a mindmap node onto another mindmap node.

The most noticeable case of this is when we paste, but this could also happen when trying to attach a node from one mindmap onto another one, or when trying to attach a left-sided node onto a right-sided one, etc.

title: [SCQM-432] `<ParticipantAvatar />` - if avatar link broken call `getAvatar`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
We've gotten a user report that though their uploaded **custom avatar** (not reliant upon a SSO like google) works in the top bar and in the bottom bar when they're *not* a visitor, their avatar shows as broken when they *are* a visitor (a 403 - no permission). There have also been other reports of broken avatars across other parts of the app that I think are related to this. 

When the mural is loaded, the avatar url for participants is pulled directly from the database and added to the participant state. This url, with an expired SAS token, is loaded directly as the avatar in the `ParticipantAvatar` component causing the 403. In cases where the avatar is not broken, it's making a request to the user api (`getAvatar`) which returns a url with an updated SAS token. This fix checks if the avatar is accessible and, if not, makes a request to `getAvatar` to get a working url. 

For testing:
- Log into the test environment as your work user
- In a separate browser, log into the test environment as an external user (i use my personal mural account for this and this step is important because this code is specifically for authenticated visitors) 
- Open a mural as your work user, copy the link, paste browser where you're logged in as an external user
- Verify you get the "You're a visitor" notification at the bottom when you do 

You'll probably get the initials avatar for these accounts, I haven't figured out a good way to manually create the error in order to test the fix, but for now just verify everything is still working. 

Regression test all the places the `ParticipantAvatar` component is used to make sure the avatars are showing up:

1. Edit as widget as the visiting user, open `Show info` at the top of the widget's context menu 
3. Create a voting session as the facilitator, vote as the visiting user. With the voting session active, open the `Still voting` dropdown as the facilitator

title: [SCQM-556]: Fix - Check if `chatId` changed before replying to chat-gpt
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

When I first started implementing the fix I was able to replicate the error through the following:
1. Explore with AI -> Click an AI prompt -> Trigger error (check Loom)
2. Summerize button (**Explore with AI** or **Landing Page prompts**)-> Wait for prompt to process -> Click on one of the pills
3. AI-Chat custom prompt -> In the selection, change yellow stickies to green then duplicate all pink stickies -> Trigger error (check Loom)

However at some point yesterday I rabased the code and I couldn't replicate error No.3 anymore. I left the code in that fixes the original error No.3  because it does fix error No.2.


Legend:
`tools_call` refers to AI asking the frontend to execute a function and expecting a response in the form of a `tool_result`
`tool_result` refers to the results of a frontend function that is meant to come after a `tools_call` from AI
`chat id` = session id = chat session id

What's being fixed?
Scenario:
1. User sends a chat that requires AI to make a `tools_call` and the frontend is in the process of executing the function and has not finished (aka has not provided a `tool_result`) to AI
5. User clear chat and a new chat id is created
6. Function finishes executing and `tool_result` is sent to AI.

Error occurs because AI is not expecting `tool_result`  since it had not made a `tools_call` in the new chat!

> [!CAUTION]
> Error: `AI request failed. OpenAI's GPT gpt4o error: 400 Invalid parameter: messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceeding message with 'tool_calls'.`

title: [Play-213] Adding Page and Adding Activities not updating UI.
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This bug addresses 2 issues : 
1. When we updated `status` to `isPublished` in #43071, we accidentally left `{isPublished: false}` [here](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/43071/files#diff-943dbb306578ab4cd42b9407eeb613a4365b1ec5d4b0f792db521a2b83876e14R14), which meant that after creating a page, we were generating the wrong route, causing the user to see a blank page. It should default to `undefined`
2. We forgot to add a refetch when creating an activity with children content, leading to an issue where content wasn't showing in the UI
3. When adding a page, the user sees a blank page. This was partially caused by 1, but also there is an issue where - during refetch after creating a page, there is a temporary state where the mutation has completed. But we are still refetching the new playbookcontent. Leading to a temporary state where we are fetching new content, but trying to redirect to the page that doesn't exist yet. To fix this, I added a line checking if we were triggering a refetch before attempting to redirect the user. 

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/PLAY-213) to understand the context of this effort.

This PR adds a new feature flag to toggle AI Preview Mode's overlay layout sorting. If the flag is ON, it will enable the "draw on top" sorting logic and include a translucent background.

This is part of an effort to ensure performance is not negatively impacted when this new overlay is rendering (see the [Jira ticket](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-714) for more details). 1. In a mural, add some stickies with different text and use AI's Cluster by Topic to enter Preview Mode with the overlay.

title: Fix logic for copying mindmaps
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes some bugs when copying mindmaps that were found when trying to address an unrelated card about pasting mindmap items when using systems.

However, since this is not really related to pasting but rather to copying, and has nothing to do with systems, I thought I would split this here.

This fixes the following bug:
When copying two siblings from the same mindmap and pasting them in the canvas, they would show up as two different mindmaps but would share the same mindmap id, therefore we would have stuff like **this**:
![Mar-06-2025 17-16-16](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be8db365-cbc3-4f0c-b5f9-8f5369ff5a45)

The PR fixes that by assigning a new mindmap id to each top node and its descendants before copying them into the clipboard.

But it also does a little code organizing because we were doing unneeded stuff and we were creating duplicated items.


**Test env:** https//copy-mindmaps.mural.engineering/

title: Modularize and package `LocationSelector` code
body:
## Ticket 🎫 

- This is perquisite work in order to fulfill the following ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CWI-1607

⚠️ **Please review commit-by-commit - there are 160+ changes to review and I split the commits in a way to make it easier to review** ⚠️ 

## What was changed and why? 🤔 

We want to package and modularlize the `LocationSelector`, so that it's available across murally and other packages.

The following was done in order to achieve this, we

- Moved and adjusted the `LocationSelector` code into `@muralco/dashboard-content-hierarchy`
- Moved and adjusted code related to `LocationSelector` into the appropriate packages as well.
- Update imports, as necessary
- Moved related test mocks into the `@muralco/test-mocks` package
- Updated imports for test code

## Important notes:

I decided to DI the toast function instead of trying to refactor and use `MrlToast`. The scope of this change would be too large for me and I would leave it up to the dashboard team to write and impl a toast provider to meet dashboard's specific needs (maybe something akin to how enterprise is doing it?: https://github.com/tactivos/murally/blob/master/packages/enterprise-security/src/ediscovery/common/toast.tsx).

body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes zoom shortcuts and zoom-marquee for Preview Mode.
To make zoom-marquee work properly, I had to refactor it out of the `ProperMuralMode` system, so it's now just a regular state prop that can live side-by-side with whatever the current mural mode is.

This PR can be followed commit by commit:
- Fix zoom shortcuts for Preview Mode.
- Fix zoom-marquee for Preview Mode.
- Refactor zoom-marquee to no longer be a `ProperMuralMode`.
- Add `isMarqueeZooming()` to simplify all those scenarios that don't care if it's zooming in or out.
- Update tests.

title: [SCQM-727] Fix snippets creation on widgets with crossed references
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This stable fix addresses a reported bug where users creating a snippet (i.e. a content library item) would get instead a zoom to the original set of widgets instead of creating new ones.

The real issue was actually in the code that creates widgets from the sidebar, so it would technically affect all related use cases.
However, since the content library is the only case of a sidebar creation that is composed of several widgets (templates and smart frameworks also do that, but they go through a different route, that's why this didn't affect them), it's only noticeable when using this feature.

The problem was that the creation was taking the protos for the creation "as is" and adding widgets out of them.
However, since the latest changes in the way we create widgets, we now rely on the creating code to properly assign ids and references to the widgets they're creating, and this code was not adapted to work under that new criteria, so it was using the same ids for every new snippet, thus allowing just one creation and then zooming to that one on each new one.

This PR fixes that by making sure that the creating widgets go through `cloneWidgets` which generates a new id and assigns any cross-reference needed automatically.


#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-727)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://snippets-creation.mural.engineering)

#### What to test for
Create a new entry on the content library and then add a number of instances of it onto the canvas. It should work as expected.

Try creating entries that have cross references (widgets inside clusters, widgets with arrows, etc)

title: [CAN-7020] Add `QuadMap` to `WidgetStore` for spatial queries
body: **[CAN-7020 QuadTree or other performant way to get widgets in an area from WidgetStore](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7020)** The quad map splits the canvas by 512x512 squares (size can be configured later). Each quad has it's own integer `key`. The widgets ids are stored in `Immutable.Map>` and are updated on WidgetStore changes. Quad map takes visual bound which for some widgets (arrow, shape, text) can be a bit bigger, depending on border width and arrow tips. It's very close to widget bounds from the engine. No changes in behaviour or performance expected. Dragging 800 stickies, updating ampersand and the engine takes much more time than updating WidgetStore. The environment: https://quad-map.mural.engineering/

title: [SCQM-205] - Fix 'board only' smart board duplicate card issues
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes an issue with duplicating a smart board containing stickies and selecting 'board only' from the duplicate modal - the duplication in the canvas happens correctly, but there is an issue with the context extension data being duplicated between columns in the boards that leaves a reference in `widgetOrderByWidgetId` to the cards in the old columns, which breaks both boards once any stickies are added/moved.

The fix updates the ekb JPM hook to return an empty object if `widgetId` is undefined while building the new ref to `widgetOrderByWidgetId`.

#### Reviewer Resources
JIRA ticket: https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-205
Testing environment: https://scqm-281-planer-selection-resize.mural.engineering/
mural-api PR: https://github.com/tactivos/mural-api/pull/13142

Demo:
Bug:
![duplicate-broken](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08f06888-e3b7-4517-83d7-da4d66fd319d)
Fixed:
![duplicate-fixed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d34607d5-2b05-42d1-bd08-be3d2f8283b0)

Testing:
1. Create a new smart planner and add a few stickies to it, in any columns.
2. Duplicate the board, and select 'board only' from the duplicate modal.
