title: [SCQM-213] Disconnected planner - only update the column, not status, when moving via info panel
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
When moving a card via the planner column dropdown in the info panel,  `moveBetweenColumns` is called by `onTicketStatusChange` and then there is conditional logic that determines **whether the status should also be updated 
which it SHOULD NOT be if the board is disconnected**. 

However, `moveBetweenColumns` ALSO makes its own call to update the widget status every time a card is moved. ===> Using the info panel to move a JIRA sticky around a *DISCONNECTED* board was updating both the planner column and the status (changing one dropdown changed them both). 

With these changes, when moving a card via the info panel, we should skip the call to update the status and let the `onTicketStatusChange` logic handle updating the label.

title: [CWI-1655] Add Ticket Models Service only source handlers
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This a second round to solve evaluating one problem: identify what's the origin or source of a ticket. Why? Because:
* Visual representation of a ticket is entitled to the source: Jira ticket doesn't look the same as ADO one, and the mural task ticket is different too.
* There are parts in the logic that demand to know when a ticket is internal from external.

So this logic is a new approach to get this working. By:

* Implemented the concept of source with a known list of external source and one unique default internal one (`mural-task`)
* Implemented some external source handlers plus a manager that would help us to detect when a ticket is internal or external.
* Then, refactored the way the _visual representation_ (aka Labels) is computed only to push it when is a mural-task ticket. Meaning if a ticket is _exported_ to Jira or ADO, those label if existent are removed.

title: [SCQM-80] Smart Planner does not work as a template after first edit
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, editing a template resulted in no content-extension related data being saved. You could correctly appear to interact with an existing smart planner and add or move tickets, or add a new planner - but while everything appears to work while editing, upon clicking `Save` you would find that your changes were not persisted. The widget changes themselves were persisted -- just no content extension data.

Now, with these changes, the template save procedure looks at content extension data as well and saves that entire set of data to the API. Changes will now all persist and work fine in future template edits and in murals created from the template.

Here's a guide to what is inside:

1. Extract `AbsorptionManagerContext` type - preface: I have to admit that when I wrote this `AbsorptionManager` I made a mistake: by not **ever** resetting the ctx, kms, tms, and api; during this ticket I discovered bugs exist with absorption when you navigate away from a mural or template and into another via the dashboard. Since the only reason for the singleton pattern was to ensure there was one constant copy of the private data inside `widgetIdsToAbsorbByBoard`, the rest can certainly be reset each time. As part of that, the function `getKanbanBoardApi` will be moved further inside the abstraction in a future commit, and so the composite type should apply everywhere instead of just in the main `absorbWidgets` function args. A long explanation for a small change, sorry.

2. Extract `DEFAULT_SYNC_METHOD` - a change unrelated to this PR, but seemed to make sense for a hard-coded string constant that should always be the same in two places, but could diverge. These aren't the commits you're looking for.

title: [CAN-7039] Fix attachment on absorbed mindmaps
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR fixes how attachment works when a mindmap is inside an area (when the connector system flag is enabled).

Master:
![Feb-28-2025 16-04-23](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb6ccb9b-a63e-4082-9121-ab20606bec9c)

PR:
![Feb-28-2025 16-03-35](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f5328c7-184a-473c-842a-fa457eb08225)

The fix consists in nulling the parent of the dragging node when doing the attachment.
Because the method that we use to get the next available position for a soon-to-be-attached node uses absolute positioning (`getMindmapNextChildPosition`), we need to make sure that the node correctly assigns this position as we expect it. So we remove its parent to make sure that the position is considered absolute.

The absorption systems that run afterwards will then proceed to check if this new position of the node makes it still be within the area boundaries, and will re-assign the parent in that case and compensate the position. 
And, if not, will expel the entire mindmap.

#### Reviewer Resources

Prior to these changes, we would handle OUTLINE messages broadcasted by other viewers. This would result in a bug where a viewer joins a presentation (for some dumb reason) sends a message to everyone to go to index -1 and everyone actually goes to index -1.

Why do people send this message in the first place? I'm not asking that question right now because it's before my time. We'll fix it later.

Now, we make sure these messages are ignored; principially for two reasons:

1. If the recipient is the presenter, we ignore all such messages. If I am the presenter, I determine what slide we're on, I can safely ignore realtime messages related to this subject.
2. If the sender of the message is not the presenter. If some random participant tries to tell me to go to slide 1, I don't care. I only listen to the messages from the presenter.

All that to say, yes, we should probably not be sending these messages in the first place. For now, we just make sure to ignore them.

title: [STT-17] Ensure widget visibility for audience using the "EngineBridge" instead of Realtime Processors
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
Prior to these changes we relied on two realtime processors to show and hide widgets for the audience based on their coordinate position on the canvas (and whether the feature was active with a live presentation).

Now, with these changes, we move this logic to the engine bridge. There are at least two reasons why this is a better approach:

1.  the engine bridge is intended to isolate the call sites to `sdk.engine`. Putting this code here -- rather than within an add-on -- facilitates visibility and an idiomatic implementation.
2. On the previous approach, we were calculating the coordinate position of widgets on the reception of a realtime message. This resulted in many race-conditions. Now, on this approach, we avoid such race conditions as the engine-bridge computes the state of the engine based on the state of the widgetStore after such processes are at a stable point.

title: [CAN-6848] Refactor `recoverWidgets` to use the `changes` api
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Let me tell you, my friend, this PR's title does not do justice to the number of things that change here.

This is probably the most annoying code review you're gonna do this year, and I'm truly sorry for that, but trust me that I've tried to make this as readable as possible.

So, first things first, **what's the goal here?**

### Refactor `recoverWidgets` to use the `changes` api
Yes, that's the title of the PR, and that's our ultimate goal.
We want to use the `changes` api to handle the changes that come from recovering deleted widgets. But in order to do that, we need to go back a bit and get things ready for it.

Before we dig into the how, one thing that is important to keep in mind at all times: **we are not changing funcionality nor introducing new behaviors here. The end result should be exactly equal as it was without these changes.**
We expect the recovery of widgets to function exactly the same as it has been.

### Split the call to `addWidgetsToMural` in `recoverWidgets`
After all the refactors we did to handle widget creation using the `changes` api, we were left with one more use case where widgets are being created but they didn't do it using the `changes` api: when we recover widgets.
What we do in that case is call `addWidgetsToMural` directly specifying that we're doing a `recover` operation and sending the `activityIds` to restore.

**At this point, it's important to notice that:** if you didn't work on recovering recently, you probably don't know that the way recovering works now is that we re-create the widgets locally and send the id of the associated activities to a `recover` endpoint that handles the re-creation in the backend. It didn't use to be like that not long ago (I just learned this now with this PR)

The first thing we'll do here is split this: we firstly operate at a local level and then do the necessary persistence.

### Split the persistence operations

title: [EN-2998] add initial inline action to new company workspaces view, take 2
body:
Exact same PR as #42927, which looks like it got stuck for some reason.

### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR implements the right side sticky "Actions" column so users can perform an available action on a single item in the table. Due to the overlap/code reuse between the bulk action flow and the inline flow, it made sense to implement the Suspend action as well as the Change end date action.

Git did a pretty good job of highlighting it, but I did some significant moving of files around/renaming of variables for consistency, to better support future work and better signal the purpose of various components and functions (e.g. the `BulkActionBar` was originally in a subfolder of the top level `src/views/components` folder for possible reuse, but it's implementation is pretty tightly tied to the Company Workspaces view, so I moved it to a subfolder of `src/views/company-workspaces/components`. Feedback/suggestions on that refactoring welcome.

title: [CAN-6848] Remove property `isWidgetFromTemplate` from `AddOptions`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR has two purposes: 
1. Fix an existing bug that was introduced in [this PR](https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/42802)
2. Remove the property `isWidgetFromTemplate` from the `AddOptions` interface

But, of course, you're probably wondering _why_, right? Why do we want to remove that property, how that bug was introduced and why are those related? Let me explain a bit.

We're in the middle of an architectural refactor on the code, where we want to change our current approach on how we deal with widgets updates to a model where we accumulate changes (using `sdk.widgets.changes.apply`) and push them all at once (using `sdk.widgets.changes.commit`).
There are more caveats to this, but that's basically the TL; DR version. Every change we accumulate is stored in the local model, and when we're ready to push the changes we gather everything that has changed since the first call to `apply`, and persist it all at once.
This includes every update to the widgets as well as creating and deleting.

**So what do templates have to do with this?**

When we create a template in the canvas, we gather the list of widgets and add them all together. When we do this, we pass along a property `isWidgetFromTemplate` in `true` to specify the difference between these widgets and any other created in a different way.

Now, here comes the problem: unlike any other property in the `AddOptions` interface, the property `isWidgetFromTemplate` only matters when we persist the widget, not when we create it locally.

In our previous form we would both create the widget locally and remotely in the same operation, so passing along this property worked. We would first create the widget locally, and the upload it by sending along `isWidgetFromTemplate`.

But now those are two different operations. We first create the widget locally and once we're ready, we commit the changes.

title: [SCQM-127] Smart Planner Freeform Layout: keyboard duplication of cards results in distant x, y positioning
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes you could duplicate a card via command + d (or also by editing, and pressing tab), and the card would be duplicated but end up somewhere very far away from the planner. Also, the column would be enlarged even without the card being properly added.

Now, with these changes, duplicated widgets behave just as in the canvas and appear to the right of the source widget. If this location would be outside the parent column bounds, it's moved to the far-left of that column and below the height of the source widget (ie, the next "row" below it) - which might not be as neat and precise as in grid mode, but is better than modifying the column size.

title: Refactor ActionBuilder to make it more powerful
body: ### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer This PR has some typescript porn, beware. The idea behind this is to make our `ActionBuilder` be more intuitive and smart about its usage. So, these are the things that we can do now with these changes: ### Force to set an initial widget to operate on - Before this PR you could do something like this: ```ts new ActionBuilder(store).moveTo(10, 10); ``` which makes no sense, because you're saying `moveTo` but not telling who. - **But now** ✨ when you do `new ActionBuilder(store)`, you first need to go through the class methods (`for`, `finish`, `getChanges` or `getMerged`). This means that you will need to establish your widget first before you can stack some actions: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5047176-7c7f-4cd9-9f1d-337d03dad565) ### Widget-specific methods - Before this PR you could do something like this: ```ts const myTitle: TitleWidget; new ActionBuilder(store) .for(myTitle) .setArrowDirection('left'); ``` which makes no sense, because you're setting an arrow property onto a title widget. - **But now** ✨ when you do `for(widget)` on a type-guarded widget, you will only get actions that can apply to that type of widget. This means both general purpose actions that apply to any widget (`setStackingOrder`, `setParent`, etc) as well as specific actions applying only to the specified widget. ### Restrictive access when working with id - Before this PR you could do something like this: ```ts new ActionBuilder(store) .for(widgetId) .setArrowDirection('left'); ``` which was far too permissive, because it would potentially allow to set an arrow-specific property i

title: [SCQM-142] Fix smart planner shift+resize behavior
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

**Prior to these changes** you would see incorrect feedback **during your resize** if you held `shift` down. The resize results when you released the mouse were still correct, this is just a temporal visual feedback issue.

**Now, with these changes**, the feedback behaves as if `shift` is **not** being pressed at all.

The plugin already had the function `isUniformResize`, but there were actually two problems with it:
A) the function was not typed as part of a handler, and thus wasn't being included when the plugin was registered, and never ran as a handler
B) the function was incorrectly **always** returning `false`, when it should have checked `applies` first and returned `null` for no action instead of always disabling uniform resize for all widgets
Luckily because of A existing, users were never exposed to B; when I fixed A, I encountered B..

#### Reviewer Resources
- Please review the 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/SCQM-142) to understand the context of this effort.

- 🧪 Please use this [**testing environment**](https://scqm-142-planner-shift-resize.mural.engineering) to perform a smoke test.
- Please follow these steps to perform a sufficient smoke test of these changes

2. Hold shift while resizing the planner
3. The feedback should be correct while using the resize

title: [presentation-mode] Set Audience View Without Reload
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, when some other user started a presentation, a participant would have to reload the page to see the stage etc... This is because we had some very defensive code in place that only applied the stage view and so on if the selector `isViewer` returned true.

This selector was returning `false` because we need to set the viewer mode concurrently with actually setting the application state to an active presentation.

Now, with these changes, we introduce a new selector `selectShouldSetViewerMode` which considers both application state and the realtime message to determine if we should set viewer mode to true.

title: [CAN-6373] Widget edition protocol tests for title and mindmaps
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR adds the widget edition protocol for all title widgets and its derivatives (paragraph, mindmaps)

There is quite a bit of clean-up in the test scenarios as we used the title widget as the basis to test for things like "list item being created" and "applying format to selection".

As we migrated to lexical, all the features that are related to RenderHTML mutation and generation should be dealt with in the Lexical serialization module, and the formatting logic is already tested by Lexical.

I've kept all the scenarios that deal with out-of-content formatting (text-align, vertical-align, font-family) as these are still part the widget properties.

The blast radius of this PR might seem high, but there is an important distinction here: we duplicated sections of the integration tests to test the connector system, which introduced quite a bit of duplicate scenarios, some of which have been updated, some removed.

title: [SCQM-136] Fix planner comment support
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

Prior to these changes, adding a comment into a planner would result in the column becoming drastically larger. We even tested it as a team as recently as Feb 10th. But, when I went to fix the bug this week it was not present, and a new bug was there - you appeared to be able to created comments as expected, and everything looked normal and worked fine - until you refreshed, and learned that your comment changes were not persisted to the API at all. So much worse than just being in the incorrect location, this bug has escalated.

Now, with these changes, comments can be added to stickies inside of planners or to planners themselves and there is no problem with their persistence in the mural after a refresh.

The main problem was that during creation of all new widgets we had an `afterCreationStarted` plugin that checked only if the widget was added via the context menu, but not what type it was. During drag and drop we explicitly verify the type of widget before accepting them into the board, so that identical verification was added to the `afterCreation` plugin.

title: [CAN-6969] Fix drag'n attach for mindmaps when using systems flag
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer
This PR fixes the behavior of the drag and attach feature for mindmaps when using the connectors system flag.

This not only addresses a lack of implementation, but it also fixes situations that were failing on the regular code: for instance when attaching a node to a new parent that was in a different direction or a different mindmap.

The way the PR implements this is by doing three main steps:

1. Everything related to showing or hiding feedback through the engine has been moved to a separate module
2. The logic behind when to show the feedback and on which nodes during a drag, since that does not change at all, has also been moved to a separate module
3. After this, the only remaining code in the original hook operates after the dragging has finished and handles attaching the nodes to their new parent.

This last part is when the code branches. When under the flag, the code to handle this situation moves from the existing handler to the `dragWithActions` handler, that does two basic things:
1. Attaches the dragging nodes to the new parent
2. Makes all nodes descendants follow their parent exactly in the same way as they do when dragging.

This last part is what makes this solution work even better than the original, because the code to follow nodes is agnostic of past directions or layouts, it simply follows the parent based on the direction the parent is pointing to at the moment of calling it.

#### Reviewer Resources
- 🏷️ [**JIRA ticket**](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-6969)
- 🧪 [**Testing environment**](https://mindmaps-attach-actions.mural.engineering)

title: update: button reference for context menu table buttons
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

[Test env](https://context-menu-tool-missing.mural.engineering/)

[Bug](https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CAN-7004): Many buttons for tables were removed recently from the context menu.

Why: 
step 1: https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/42614 - critical bug that had duplicated buttons. The reason was because there were two tools with the same name (id). The insertCommands referenced this name and thus was duplicated. Fix for this bug was to rename the second tool so that insertCommand only referenced a single tool and not two.

step 2: https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/42891 - this work removed the second of the two tools that originally had the same name. When this happened, the insertCommands reference no longer existed. Thus creating the bug.

This bug really sheds light to issues with our context menu, that doing changes to one tool can completely screw up another unrelated tool unknowingly. Not good

title: fix nbsp issue - svg santization improvement
body:
## Ticket 🎫 

Jira ticket
https://mural.atlassian.net/browse/CWI-650

Previous old PR for ref
https://github.com/tactivos/murally/pull/36253

## What was changed and why? 🤔 

There is currently an issue where SVGs fail to upload because there are nbsp characters within the SVG itself. To solve this, we need to replace these nbsp characters with plain " " whitespace characters instead.

The changes include the following:

- created `sanitizeSvg` - an overloaded function that can accept a `File`, `Blob`, or simply a `string`. Runs a scoped instance of DOMPurify to avoid polluting the global instance (if we want to add sanitization hooks later) and removes the nbsp characters from the svg.
   - Opportunity: usage of DOMPurify is scattered around the codebase, perhaps we can consolidate usage of it into its own package and provide sanitization methods for everyone to use.
- added usage of sanitizeSvg anywhere we upload and load svgs as assets

## Testing

- added new tests
- existing tests should pass
- testing env: https://svg-sanitization-on-upload-2.mural.engineering/

You can test manually by uploading a problematic svg in app or beta to see the issue, and then upload the same problematic svg into the testing environment to see the issue resolved.

title: [CAN-6954] Fix absolute coordinates in `sanitizeWidgetsForDuplication`
body:
### Summary of Changes and Resources for the Reviewer

This PR does 2 things:
1. Renames `sanitizeWidgets` to `sanitizeWidgetsForDuplication` because it's the only place it's being used.
2. Fixes how the bounds are being calculated when a widget is being duplicated inside the parent. Originally it would get the bounds of the widget being sanitized, but this was not working because the widget hadn't been created yet. So instead of doing that, I look for the parent (if any) and adjust the position to global coordinates _only_ if the parent is not also being duplicated.
